reviews.summary: `nerva chat -z "prompt"` runs one turn non-interactively and puts only the final assistant text on stdout — whole escape sequences and C0/C1 control bytes stripped, newlines and tabs kept — with every other word on stderr. The prompt resolves the way `nerva send`'s body does (argument, else `-f PATH` where `-` is stdin, else piped stdin) and a terminal is never read, by either spelling: `-f /dev/tty` is refused rather than blocking forever. A prompt over the hub's own 4,096-character `ChatRequest` bound is a usage error before the request, not an HTTP 422 a script reads as a failed turn. The ladder is stated in `--help`: 0 answered · 1 the turn did not complete · 2 usage · 3 no hub · 4 not authorised · 130 interrupted; Ctrl-C returns 130 with one stderr line instead of an uncaught traceback that could spill a partial answer. **The governance clause is implemented against Hermes, not after it:** no flag auto-approves, a turn that queues an action stays queued, and the verb exits 1 naming the pending id to decide with `nerva approvals`; a test asserts the one-shot path issues no decision call at all. For a queued action the verdict no longer rests on the reply text. The hub reports what the turn queued: `ChatResponse.pending_approvals` on `POST /chat`, and the same list on `/chat/stream`'s end event. A per-turn collector (`agents/core/turn_approvals.py`) gathers the ids at the gated Tool-RPC enqueue, and they are still reported when the turn raised after queuing. Any reported id makes `-z` exit 1 with the id on stderr, whatever the reply says, so a model that writes a plausible answer around a queued action does not exit 0. The reply text is a second detector, for stops that queue nothing and for a hub that reports no ids. It is matched by containment over the sanitised text, so the deterministic `[athena]: …` join that the synthesis pass falls back to still matches. The table holds the approval reply, the busy/compaction/continuation refusals, the no-local-model reply, the hub's two failure replies, the five tool-loop stops and a prefix rule for the stop built with an f-string. A drift test imports the ten runtime constants and asserts each is matched both verbatim and wrapped. Sanitising happens before the verdict, so a reply of pure control bytes is an incomplete turn rather than exit 0 and a blank line. `--usage-file PATH` writes `nerva.chat.usage.v1` atomically on every path including the interrupt, cleans up its temp file when a write fails, survives a field it cannot encode (a warning, never a crash after the answer is already out), says so when given an empty path, and refuses to call a turn completed while naming an approval it left queued. A hub that reports `pending_approvals` in a shape this version cannot read is told so, rather than the string being exploded into one fabricated id per character. 51 tests in tests/test_nerva_oneshot.py; the hub-side report is pinned by tests/test_turn_pending_approvals.py.
reviews.remaining: Two parts of the row are open. (1) THE SPEND HALF IS A SCHEMA OF NULLS. The hub cannot attribute one turn's cost. `AgentConfig.model` defaults to `google/gemma-4-31b-a4b` and none of the 18 agents in `agents/_system/agents.yaml` declares a model, so `cost_tracker` meters every turn at the default price row and reports $0.00; an id it does not know is priced from the `default` row with no `priced` flag. `estimated_cost_usd`, the token counts, `api_calls`, `model` and `provider` are therefore `null` with `cost_basis: "unavailable"` rather than measured zeros, and a test pins that they never become numbers. (2) A STOP THAT QUEUES NOTHING IS STILL JUDGED BY TEXT, AND ON A LIVE HUB THAT TEXT IS USUALLY REWRITTEN. The hub reports ids only for approvals queued through the gated Tool-RPC path. The tool loop's own stops are recognised only by containment over the reply. A turn routed to a specialist is not handed back verbatim: the orchestrator sends it through synthesis (`was_synthesized = len(responses) > 1 or "jarvis" not in responses`). With a `jarvis` agent and a router loaded, `jarvis.synthesize` rewrites it through a model; only the fallbacks (no `jarvis` agent, no router, a failed synthesis call) produce the `[athena]: …` join that containment survives. So a specialist's tool-loop stop can come back reworded and exit 0. The table also has no entry for `THINKING_EXHAUSTED_REPLY` (agents.core.llm.base): a comment in the table names it, but no row follows. A reasoning model that spent its whole budget thinking is therefore printed as the answer with exit 0. Also open: `POST /chat` returns no trace, invocation or session id, so `session_id` is echoed only when the caller supplied one; `-z` does not silence hub-side logging; there is no `--output-format` beyond the existing `--json`; a piped body is read whole up to the bound rather than streamed; and `os.replace` onto a symlinked `--usage-file` path replaces the link with a regular file instead of writing through it.

reviews.summary: Bash, zsh și fish primesc completări de comenzi/subcomenzi generate din arborele argparse instalat. Fish parcurge recursiv subparser-ele și tratează literal metadatele, fără apeluri către hub sau executarea CLI-ului la completare. Teste cu fish real acoperă fiecare cale curentă, extensii imbricate, prefixe parțiale, comenzi terminale și substituții ostile; Bash/Zsh rămân identice cu baza. Contractul H004 privește arborele de comenzi, nu completarea opțiunilor ori valorilor argumentelor. Scripturile salvate se regenerează după upgrade. Workdir integration rechecked previously-current evidence against base 837d6d08: the parser adds options without changing the command tree or completion implementation. Existing CLI/completion regression coverage is retained.

reviews.summary: `nerva doctor` rulează `scripts/doctor.py` fără să schimbe nimic, cu un motiv numit pentru fiecare verificare, `--json` și `--smoke`. Are cinci verificări obligatorii (python, venv, locks_in_sync, bind_is_loopback, data_root_writable) și cinci consultative (runtimes, readyz, runtime_resolves, config_sources, smoke; scripts/doctor.py:102-103). Iese cu 1 doar când pică una obligatorie; o consultativă care pică e `warn`. Din HEQ lot 1 (H242), `runtime_resolves` verifică dacă ruta pe care o ia un turn Jarvis chiar se rezolvă la un model utilizabil, nu doar dacă răspunde un runtime. Citește verdictul strict al hub-ului, blocul `model` din `GET /api/onboarding/command-center` (același select_backend, fără generare), cu un singur credențial local: `JARVIS_USER_TOKEN`, altfel `JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, pe care îl trimite doar unui hub de pe această mașină, decis după adresă, nu după ortografie (scripts/doctor.py:286, scripts/doctor.py:333-340). E `ok` doar pe `ready: true` care numește ruta, providerul și modelul. Altfel dă motivul numit (`configured_not_resident`, `route_unselected`, `needs_token`, `malformed_reply` …), iar fără un hub gata e `skip`. `readyz` și această citire folosesc aceeași adresă de hub ca `nerva status` (`NERVA_HUB_URL`, altfel `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_PORT`; o adresă wildcard e apelată prin loopback). Din H273, `config_sources` arată, informativ, din ce strat vine fiecare cheie de configurare (mediul procesului > `.env`-ul repo-ului > `.env`-ul din data home) și ce valori din `.env` sunt acoperite de un strat de mai sus — doar nume, niciodată o valoare. `nerva status` arată același verdict pe o linie `runnable:`, separat de vechiul `model_state`, afișat acum „resident”. Alte diagnostice sunt verbe separate: `nerva desktop status` (ce îi lipsește host-ului pentru operatorul desktop), `nerva security audit` (vulnerabilități cunoscute, prin OSV) și `nerva extensions doctor`.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc jumătățile de reparare și de operare ale rândului: nu există `--fix` (reparări numite, în tier reversibil, cu tot ce atinge credențiale sau postura pus în coada de aprobare), `--live` (rulare continuă) sau `--ack ADVISORY_ID`. Lipsesc și verificările cerute pentru o instalare deja configurată: accesibilitatea serverelor MCP, token-urile canalelor, postura kernel/flag-uri, integritatea lanțului de audit și credențialele/conectivitatea fiecărui provider configurat. `runtime_resolves` judecă doar ruta pe care o ia acum un turn Jarvis, iar o rută cloud trece pe decizia de disponibilitate a routerului, fără un apel care să verifice credențialul la provider.

reviews.summary: `nerva send --channel <id> <mesaj>` livreaza fara thread primit anterior, iar `nerva send --list` enumera destinatiile configurate cu motivul cand una nu e gata. Trece prin POST /api/channels/send (admin), respecta rate-limit-ul de trimitere si se inregistreaza in IntentLog ca `channel.send`. Din 2026-09-16 (H480) corpul poate veni din fișier sau stdin, cu un subiect `-s` purtat ca titlu ntfy sau ca prima linie a mesajului; scara de ieșire 0/1/2/3/4 e declarată în `--help`.
reviews.remaining: Randul cere orice platforma configurata. Nerva expune doar canalele direct-send (telegram, web, voice, ntfy), iar web nu e gata cat timp niciun client nu e conectat la el: HUD-ul nu conecteaza unul, asa ca `nerva send --list` si /api/channels/targets il arata ca nepregatit, cu motivul (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:88). Slack si Discord sunt reply-only prin brokerul channel.reply si nu pot fi adresate de `send`; email-ul e exclus deliberat, ca mailul inbound neincrezut sa nu capete efect SMTP.

reviews.summary: `nerva security audit` inventariază distribuțiile interpretorului curent și pinurile Python exacte ale descriptorilor de extensie numiți, întreabă OSV.dev prin `PluginHTTPClient` (rezoluție DNS pinată, ancorele TLS ale owner-ului, breaker; querybatch în loturi de 1000 cu paginare urmărită + un detaliu per advisory; pleacă doar perechi nume+versiune, anunțate pe stderr), unește oglinzile GHSA/PYSEC ale aceluiași CVE într-o singură constatare cu cea mai mare severitate declarată, numește fix-ul din intervalul care conține versiunea instalată și iese 0/1/5. Un advisory fără severitate declarată pică orice prag; o bază de date de neatins, un lot rămas paginat după 20 de pagini sau un audit care nu se încheie înseamnă exit 5 și nicio afirmație. O distribuție cu metadate nedecodabile e sărită și numită; textul advisory-urilor e curățat de caractere de control înainte de terminal. MCP (comenzi stdio configurate de owner) e listat ca neauditat, cu motivul. Probat live: 48 distribuții curate; un pin `requests 2.19.0` dă 5 constatări după unirea a 5 oglinzi PYSEC. Recenzie adversarială independentă: nouă defecte, toate remediate în același PR.
reviews.remaining: Suprafața MCP nu e auditată: comenzile stdio (`npx …`, `uvx …`) din configurația persistată nu sunt rezolvate la pachete și versiuni. Descriptorii de extensie trebuie numiți pe linia de comandă; catalogul pachetelor achiziționate e pe partea hub-ului și nu e citit offline. Nu există `nerva security` implicit (cli-d.security-default) și nici `--skip-venv/--skip-plugins/--skip-mcp`. Vectorii CVSS nu sunt scorați: un advisory doar cu vector rămâne `unknown` și pică orice prag dacă nu se unește cu un frate GHSA evaluat. Pragul implicit `--fail-on low` e deliberat mai strict decât `critical` din Hermes. Nu există setare de proxy pentru operator (H281). Din procesul CLI nu există mediere kernel și registrul de egress nu persistă. Scara de ieșire e cea Nerva (0/1/2/5), nu 0/1/2 din Hermes. Fără probă pe o mașină fără proxy transparent.

reviews.summary: The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` exits **13**, and since #1177 that arm branches on the port number instead of asserting a cause it cannot know — below 1024 it names the privileged-port rule (root or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; move `JARVIS_PORT` above 1024), at or above 1024 it says outright that this is *not* the privileged-port rule and root/Administrator will not help, then points at the reservations that actually produce it (Windows `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange tcp`, whose Hyper-V/WSL blocks routinely cover the shipped default 8080; an SELinux `name_bind` denial on Linux) plus `JARVIS_PORT`. Both codes are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed; and `IPV6_V6ONLY` on an AF_INET6 probe, so an IPv4 listener on the same port cannot turn a working v6 boot into exit 12. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (the `status` verb in `agents/cli/nerva.py`). 13 `test_probe_bind_*` functions, 16 collected cases (the IPv6-conflict case skips on a box with no IPv6 stack). Both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the sub-1024 `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds; the high-port `EACCES` arm is driven through a stubbed `bind()` that answers `EACCES`, parametrised over 1024/8080/49152/65535, because its real reproduction is a Windows excluded port range that cannot be staged on Linux, and a sibling test pins that port 80 still gets the privileged-port sentence. ENV-122 in `docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md` moves from a message-quality finding to an asserted string plus exit code.
reviews.remaining: Hermes's row is start, check **and stop**, and the stop half is entirely absent: no `stop` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites `hermes dashboard --status/--stop` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has `nerva status`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable `BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: `--isolated`, `--skip-build`, `--no-open`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. **One known limit, in the safe direction:** the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address `getaddrinfo` returns, so a dual-stack name like `localhost` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the `SO_REUSEADDR` choice is read off asyncio's `reuse_address = os.name == "posix"` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so.

reviews.summary: Drumul de la instalare la prima apăsare există acum. `nerva desktop status` citește faptele tri-state ale sondei de gazdă și le redă ca o cale ordonată — sesiune grafică, bibliotecile driverului, granturile de sistem, elevare — cu prima piedică numită explicit; `nerva desktop grant <pas>` deschide panoul unde owner-ul acordă permisiunea și nu acordă nimic el însuși. Un fapt pe care sonda nu l-a putut stabili se redă `unknown`, niciodată `ready`. Tabelul de deschidere e o constantă de modul, verificată prin identitate, deci seam-ul nu poate deveni o cale de lansat orice.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere și jumătatea de instalare pe care Nerva o rezolvă altfel: Hermes are `computer-use install` care aduce și repară un binar cua străin, plus `status` și `doctor` separate. Nerva își construiește propriile drivere, deci nu există binar de adus — dar nu există nici instalarea dependențelor opționale dintr-o comandă (pywinauto/uiautomation/pyobjc/PyGObject rămân în sarcina owner-ului), nici un `doctor` dedicat operatorului, nici o suprafață în HUD pentru aceeași cale. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: containerul e headless, deci calea a fost probată doar pe sonde sintetice — niciun panou de sistem real nu a fost deschis și niciun grant real nu a fost observat schimbându-se.

reviews.summary: `nerva prompt-size` există și raportează costul fix per apel, pe componente, cel mai mare primul — offline, fără hub, fără backend, fără nicio cerere: citește personele de pe disc și cere registrului specurile pe care oricum le declară. Exact asta îl face utilizabil pentru întrebarea la care răspunde („cât plătesc înainte să înceapă conversația") pe o cutie unde hub-ul nici măcar nu rulează. `agents/core/prompt_size.py` sparge costul în: câte o linie per persoană de agent găsită pe disc, câte una per unealtă — costată ca **JSON-ul care chiar traversează sârma**, nu ca numele ei, fiindcă un `input_schema` stufos poate cântări cât o persoană întreagă — indexul de skill-uri randat exact cum îl randează `build_prompt`, și schela de tură pe care fiecare cerere o plătește. Numărul pe care raportul îl scoate în față e **podeaua per apel**, nu suma: cele 18 persoane sunt listate separat fiindcă o cerere reală trimite una singură, a agentului rutat. Prima versiune a raportului aduna toate cele 18 și anunța 71,8 % dintr-o fereastră de 32k, când o cerere reală plătește ~6,5 % — un număr greșit e mai rău decât niciun număr, așa că podeaua per apel e ce se citește primul și un test o fixează. Fără agent numit se folosește persoana cea mai grea, deci cifra e cazul realist cel mai prost, nu unul măgulitor; un agent inexistent nu e taxat tăcut pe seama altcuiva. Raportul spune despre el însuși că cifrele sunt estimări din aceeași funcție pe care o folosește bugetul la runtime, și trimite la H673 pentru singura măsurătoare exactă — cea raportată de provider. Ieșire text tabelară sau `--json`.
reviews.remaining: Rândul Hermes cere și componente pe care Nerva nu le are separate azi: „cele trei tiere de prompt" și „user profile" nu există ca blocuri distincte în asamblarea promptului (`Agent.build_prompt` are soul + skills + agent memory + schelă), iar `<available_skills>` e un index Hermes; echivalentul livrat e blocul `Available skills:`. Memoria nu e costată: e per sesiune și variabilă, nu cost fix, iar a o raporta ca „fix" ar fi exact tipul de cifră greșită pe care livrarea asta o evită. Schemele de unelte sunt raportate doar când i se dau: verbul nu bootează un registru, iar pe o cutie fără hub secțiunea lipsește și raportul **spune** că lipsește, în loc s-o raporteze ca zero. Cost per toolset (grupat) nu e implementat, doar per unealtă. Neverificat pe serviciu real: nicio cerere nu a fost trimisă — cifrele sunt estimări comparabile cu bugetul intern, nu contorul unui provider.

reviews.summary: A message that arrives while a turn runs on the same session waits for that session's turn lease (`Orchestrator.turn_lease`, agents/core/orchestrator.py:1547, taken by `_channel_turn` at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1505 and by the web /chat path at agents/web.py:1149). After `_TURN_LEASE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (180 s, agents/core/orchestrator.py:242) it gets the single busy string `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:244) and no second turn starts on that transcript (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118). `/pause` and `/stop` are owner-only (ADMIN tier) slash commands that engage the e-stop (agents/core/commands.py:319, agents/core/commands.py:320). They say plainly that work already in flight finishes (agents/core/commands.py:227, tests/test_slash_commands.py:124).
reviews.remaining: No busy-input semantics. A mid-turn message cannot redirect or interrupt the running turn. There is no explicit FIFO `/queue`, no `/steer` into the running turn and no configurable mode between these with downgrades. `/stop` is not a hard kill: it engages the e-stop but does not cancel the running turn or unlock the session. It is also dispatched inside `handle_input` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1794), so it waits behind the same lease. While a turn holds the lease past the wait bound, `/stop` itself is answered with `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (named at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3182). There is one busy string, not a set of acks saying whether a message was queued, steered or interrupted. None of the protective demotions exist (running subagent, in-flight compression, photo burst, very fast follow-up merged as the same intent). The lease is the only slot reservation; there is no pending-agent sentinel. `SlashCommand` (agents/core/commands.py:61) carries no `busy_policy`.

reviews.summary: Turns are serialized per resolved session. `Orchestrator.turn_lease` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1547) holds one asyncio.Lock per key, and `_lease_key` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1537) follows `_resolve_session`'s order, so the lease names the session the turn will actually use rather than the routing key. It is taken by channel turns (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1505) and the web /chat path (agents/web.py:1149), and it is re-entrant within one turn. After 180 s a waiting message is answered `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` instead of starting (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118, tests/test_turn_lease.py:104). The lease table is capped at 1024 entries and prunes unlocked locks when full (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1566, tests/test_turn_lease.py:163). The `_active_session` ContextVar (agents/core/orchestrator.py:274) keeps concurrent turns from reading or writing each other's session (tests/test_concurrent_session_isolation.py:93).
reviews.remaining: No run generation lets a late callback from an abandoned turn detect that it no longer owns the session. The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3462), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no `max_concurrent_sessions` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session `SessionState` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares `orchestrator.agents`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:357).

reviews.summary: Channel conversations are designed to be forever-sessions. Orchestrator.channel_handler derives a deterministic key per channel identity with build_session_key (agents/core/channels/session.py:68, called at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1395) and resumes that same session on every turn (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1407). conversation_clock (agents/core/conversation_clock.py) only tells a long-lived session today's date. There is no reset policy, no idle or daily expiry, no reset-trigger phrase and no stall watcher: reset_policy, session_reset, idle_reset and stall-watcher terms have no matches under agents/. The only adjacent mechanism is disk retention. purge_old_conversations (agents/core/retention.py:49) deletes transcripts whose last activity is older than retention.conversation_ttl_days; the 03:30 cron job (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:181) runs it when retention.enabled is on, which is off by default. It does not evict the in-memory session, so it ages records out, the analogue of session_store_max_age_days, but does not reset live context. Tests tests/test_retention.py and tests/test_channel_sessions.py pass.
reviews.remaining:
1. Reset policy: idle-minutes and daily-at-hour resets, overridable per session type (dm/group/thread) and per channel, applied by rotating the channel session to a fresh id while keeping the old transcript.
2. Reset triggers: configurable texts (e.g. /new, /reset) intercepted in channel_handler before a turn runs; they start a fresh session and acknowledge it.
3. Expiry watcher: a scheduled job that applies the idle/daily policies and drops stale _channel_sessions entries.
4. Stall watcher: track inbound receipt against last turn progress per session and notify the owner once when a message has been pending past a threshold with no progress.
5. Tests for each.

reviews.summary: Registrul de comenzi, tierele și catalogul HUD există.
reviews.remaining: Rândul include mai multe comenzi, meniuri și extensii de comenzi decât registrul livrat; echivalarea completă rămâne deschisă.

reviews.summary: Of the outbound-rendering set, only streaming edits exist, and only on Telegram. `TelegramDraft` in agents/core/channels/telegram.py sends the first token as a message, then edits it at most once per `STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL` (1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; `finish()` settles the final text in the edited message, sends the overflow as new messages and retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text. `Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft` opens a draft only for an adapter whose descriptor declares `supports_edit`, while the Settings DB toggle `channels.streaming_replies` is on and the delivery router would send, and never for Slack or Discord: their workspace replies are governed `channel.reply` approvals delivered whole through `render_outbound` after approval (tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py `test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens`, tests/test_telegram_streaming.py). The Telegram chat-action indicator (`send_action`) is sent only while an attachment is read (`typing` in `_read_attachment`) and while a spoken reply is synthesized (`record_voice` in `_speak`).
reviews.remaining: The reduced set the row accepted beyond streaming is absent: no long-running 'still working, N min' message on a chat channel while a slow turn runs (`TURN_BUSY_REPLY` only answers a second message sent while a turn holds the session); no `tool_progress: log` per-turn append-only record of which tools ran; no quiet/show-tools level with a tool-progress message and its cleanup after the final answer, and no `/verbose`-style chat command to switch it (the slash-command registry has help, status, sessions, pause, stop, resume, jobs, remind and voice); no typing indicator on an ordinary text turn; no single RO/EN reply-string catalog: the decision-inbox cards still hardcode Romanian labels (`✅ Aprob`, `❌ Resping`) while channel notes and slash-command replies are English. Neither Slack nor Discord implements an edit call — no `begin_stream`, Slack posts only through `chat_postMessage`, Discord has no message PATCH — although both descriptors declare `supports_edit=True`, so the edit path is missing as well as the approval contract below. Slack and Discord replies are not streamed until one edit stream can be approved as a single `channel.reply` decision (H104). The missing typing indicator on an ordinary text turn is counted once, under H683's acknowledge-at-ingest gap.

reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes. `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta înainte de descărcare, mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor (vorbirea nu atinge discul) și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit; santinelele motorului nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Transcriptul circulă ca o tură obișnuită, nu în gard: sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, iar protecția reală e filtrul de halucinații (H530). Jumătatea rostită: `/voice off|voice|always` e mod per conversație (`voice_mode.py`, magazie JSON `canal:chat`, implicit off, setat de chat pentru chat), `stt_echo_transcripts` e setarea `voice.stt_echo_transcripts` (o linie de serviciu „am auzit: …” înaintea răspunsului, niciodată rostită), iar `spoken_reply.py` transformă textul livrat într-o notă vocală peste motorul TTS al gazdei — doar proza (fără cod, linkuri, marcaje), tăiată la o limită de propoziție, fișierul șters după citire, nimic din text în log. Cârligul stă unde textul chiar ajunge (`send()` și `finish()` al draftului în flux), deci modul nu poate livra ca audio ce ruterul n-ar fi livrat ca text; orice eșec costă nota vocală, niciodată textul; un 400 pe `sendVoice` reîncearcă o dată ca `sendAudio`. `/voice` numește motorul care ar vorbi și spune „cloud” când e edge-tts. Reevaluarea inițială a raportat 15/15 mutanți uciși; numărul nu a fost reprodus la recitirea din 2026-09-22.
reviews.remaining: Consumatorul TTS în flux care începe să rostească propozițiile terminate cât timp modelul încă generează (nota vocală se sintetizează după răspunsul complet). Intrarea/ieșirea dintr-un canal de voce pe Discord e sărită deliberat de rândul original (funcție de comunitate, nu de asistent). Doar Telegram: pe Slack/Discord replica trece prin brokerul `channel.reply`, fără audio. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun mesaj vocal Telegram adevărat, niciun model Whisper încărcat, niciun `sendVoice` real — Telegram acceptă `.mp3` ca mesaj vocal după documentație, iar căderea pe `sendAudio` e plasa pentru cazul în care nu.

reviews.summary: Randarea și împărțirea mesajelor folosesc descriptorul și registrul comun pentru dialectele canalelor Nerva; platformele excluse nu sunt reintroduse.

Edit-based streaming replies exist on Telegram. `TelegramDraft` in agents/core/channels/telegram.py sends the first token as a message and edits it in place at most once per `STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL` (1.2 s), skipping frames whose visible text did not change; the preview is capped below the message limit, and `finish()` writes the first chunk of the final text into the edited message and sends the overflow as continuation messages, retrying rejected markup as plain text and falling back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. `TelegramChannel.begin_stream` returns a draft only for a chat id; `Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft` opens it only when the adapter's descriptor declares `supports_edit`, the Settings DB toggle `channels.streaming_replies` is on and the delivery router would send to that source; observed group messages never open one and a draft that never started falls back to the normal send (tests/test_telegram_streaming.py). Slack and Discord are refused a draft on purpose: their workspace replies are governed `channel.reply` approvals delivered whole after approval, and edit support alone cannot publish unapproved tokens (tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py `test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens`).
reviews.remaining: Neither Slack nor Discord implements an edit call — no `begin_stream`, Slack posts only through `chat_postMessage`, Discord has no message PATCH — although both descriptors declare `supports_edit=True`, so the edit path is missing as well as the approval contract below. Slack and Discord replies are not streamed: both descriptors declare `supports_edit`, but `_begin_channel_draft` refuses them because the row's governance clause requires one edit stream to be a single `channel.reply` approval decision and no such contract exists yet; until it does, their replies arrive whole after approval. The Matrix adapter (`MatrixChannel`, a webhook channel), another edit-capable platform the rationale names, posts whole `m.room.message` events: its descriptor does not declare `supports_edit` and it has no edit (`m.replace`) or draft path.

reviews.summary: Telegram photos are read, not only recognised. `classify` (agents/core/channels/inbound_media.py) recognises the ten attachment kinds in `RECOGNISED_KINDS` and turns a missing file handle, a declared size above the 20 MB bot ceiling or an unreadable kind into a named reason, so the sender gets one plain line from `describe` instead of silence. `InboundImageReader` (agents/core/channels/media_reader.py) describes a photo through a proven-local VLM and hands the description to the turn as data, never as instructions. Locality follows the `screen_locator` rule: `is_local` derives only from `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, `TelegramChannel._read_image` asks `refusal()` before any download, and `_backend_call` checks again against the `VLMBackend` built for the URL it will actually post to, so a non-loopback VLM receives no bytes. `_download_file` bounds the transfer by the bytes that actually arrive, not by the sender-chosen `file_size`, and `_safe_file_path` rejects any `getFile` path that is not Telegram-shaped before it enters the bot-token URL. The description is folded to one line, capped and wrapped in the Wave 5a `fence_tool_result` fence, deliberately without the `spotlight` datamark, which would replace spaces with '▁' and blind the gateway's `detect_injection`; a photo with '<<END UNTRUSTED>>' written on it cannot close its own fence. The caption never reaches the describer: it travels separately as the sender's question. The turn goes through the normal door, so `Gateway._inbound_meta` marks it `inbound:telegram` and runs the detector over exactly what the model reads. Voice notes are read on the other path: a transcript is the sender's own words and travels unfenced as an ordinary turn (`inbound_voice`, row H071). `ChannelDescriptor` separates `recognises_media` from `reads_media` with the subset invariant checked at construction, and `READABLE_KINDS` is exactly {photo, voice}.
reviews.remaining: Only photos and voice notes, only on Telegram. Not delivered: reading audio files, video, video notes, animations, documents and stickers (recognised, answered with 'reading … is not wired up yet'); a disk cache under a media directory so vision tools can open a local path (bytes stay in memory for one call); photo-burst batching and media-group (album) debounce; location and venue pins (recognised as `location`, deliberately not echoed, not read); caching of media from observed group messages and from replied-to messages; media ingestion on WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat and email (those adapters pass text only). Documented limitation, not solved: taint cannot be tracked through the model; what travels is the coarse fact that the turn read untrusted material, and the channel's `inbound` origin is what keeps an action derived from a photo in approval. `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` is not called here because it would be a no-op (escalate-only over an already untrusted origin). UNVERIFIED on real services: the suite is hermetic; no real Telegram message received, no local VLM actually called, `getFile` and the download exercised only against a fake client.

reviews.summary: Channels declare their capabilities, and output is adapted to them after generation, but the model is never told which channel it is on. ChannelDescriptor (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:28) declares each adapter's dialect, max_message_length and supports_edit (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:35). render_outbound (agents/core/channels/render.py:252) re-renders and chunks the reply per dialect after the model has answered. _begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1512) streams edits only when the owner-wide channels.streaming_replies setting is on (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1520) and the adapter declares supports_edit (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1527). Streaming is therefore derived from capabilities: ntfy, email and other non-editable channels never receive streamed partial output, and Slack and Discord are excluded outright. Nothing more of the accepted design exists: there is no platform_hint, no per-channel prompt, no channel-to-skill binding and no display-tier resolver.
reviews.remaining: No descriptor-level platform_hint line is injected into the system prompt of a channel turn. There is no operator-set per-channel or per-topic prompt, stored as admin configuration and never settable from inbound content. There is no channel-to-skill binding that makes a given channel or topic auto-run a skill. There is no display-tier resolver derived from descriptor capabilities (can edit, permanent, length cap) that governs tool-progress, reasoning, interim and heartbeat messages per channel; the only per-channel display decision is the supports_edit gate on streaming.

reviews.summary: Joburile pot selecta un canal și păstrează regulile de prezență și liniște.
reviews.remaining: Rămân routingul origin/thread/all, predarea către alt agent și fallbackurile complete cerute de inventar.

reviews.summary: A burst of messages still becomes one turn per message. Telegram's _poll_loop (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:399) awaits self.receive once per update (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:477), so three fragments run three sequential turns. Gateway.route (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:64) hands every message straight to the handler. It runs detect_injection on each fragment separately, in _inbound_meta (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:168-173). The only concurrency control is the per-session turn_lease (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1547) behind _channel_turn (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1498). It serialises turns, and a turn that waits past the bound gets TURN_BUSY_REPLY (agents/core/orchestrator.py:244) instead of being merged. A scratch probe routed three fragments concurrently through Gateway.route: the handler ran three times, once per fragment.
reviews.remaining: There is no debounce or merge window anywhere in agents/core/channels/. Client-side splits, photo and album (media_group_id) bursts, and text-plus-attachment pairs are not coalesced into one turn. There are no debounce knobs: no window, no hard cap, no per-chat serialisation of the merged turn. There is no guarantee that the injection scan runs on the merged text rather than per fragment.

reviews.summary: All 18 existing HUD modes and 115 console panels now have explicit stable URLs, browser history, titles, unknown-route handling and real lazy chunks with loading/error fallback. Existing rail, palette, hotkeys, desktop and World navigation share URL state. Selected panels receive focus; demo/floating context is preserved. Overlay return destinations are bound to individual history entries and independently verified across historical/nested visits and malformed state. Desktop and Pixel 7 browser smoke passed against a local stubbed backend. Existing route/history/focus smoke remains green after grid sizing and cockpit composer wrapping. Three actual desktop-width regressions and three independent stacked-layout checks verify contained controls; cloud approval/gallery also passes at1280px.
reviews.remaining: Nerva has no global multi-profile switch or plugin route registry; profile-keyed remount and plugin-aware route extension from the full Hermes contract remain unsupported. Current route/demo-context remount does not claim multi-profile equivalence. Browser tests validate navigation with a stubbed backend, not production-host services.

reviews.summary: Același bundle SPA funcționează la rădăcină sau sub un JARVIS_ROOT_PATH validat, cu reverse proxy care elimină prefixul. Bootstrap-ul serverului, navigarea și istoricul, API/SSE/streaming, chunk-urile lazy, fonturile, manifestul și service worker-ul folosesc prefixul; cache-urile PWA sunt separate per prefix. Paginile /map și /mission-control legate din SPA sunt adaptate. Teste prin aplicația reală și proxy HTTP verifică reload, shortcut-uri, cache offline, auth pe POST și lipsa cererilor la rădăcina greșită; coliziunile /v2 și /api au regresii. Sub prefix, /metrics păstrează eticheta de rută (middleware-ul de prefix întoarce scope["route"] către golden-signals, la fiecare mesaj trimis și la eroare), iar căile nerutate rămân <unmatched>. Contractul este pentru browser cu proxy prefix-stripping: wrapper-ul nativ cere prefix gol, /v1 și proxy-urile care păstrează prefixul nu sunt incluse. Fixture-ul dezactivează lifespan/provider startup; nu se pretinde deployment sau probă cu provider live.

Browser HUD, ambient and responsive phone layouts synchronize fixed appearance preferences through a narrow user-guarded Settings DB document. Boot reads never write defaults; stale known values coerce to supported choices. Prefix-scoped immutable edit journals preserve offline changes across tabs, server revision CAS prevents stale writes without Web Locks, and acknowledgements remove exact edits even after unmount. Motion defaults to the OS System preference. Two independent real browser contexts recover saved choices after cache loss. Five fixed local UI font choices now share that normalization, revision and offline journal contract. The HUD applies the body/display override at its root; code and explicitly monospace elements retain their independent font stack. Real root/prefix browser tests verify computed families, persistence in a fresh browser, look independence, offline replay and code font invariance. The separate native application now reads the same owner Settings DB document at boot and foreground entry. Its connection-scoped finite cache, explicit-save hydration epochs and serialized current-record writes prevent stale credentials or appearance from returning. All 19 native consumers react without resetting local component state; code fonts remain independent. The accepted cross-client preference contract is implemented; native authoring and a full curated font catalog are not required by this row. Scope remains one configured owner instance. Unsupported native fonts have explicit platform fallbacks; unavailable storage cannot preserve offline choices across process restarts. Native rendering is covered with real React source and host mocks, not device GUI proof.

Shared browser composer now accepts image selection, paste and drop, with transient previews, removal and eight pending-read reservations. Authenticated composer-specific vision routes validate static PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP bytes and bounded raster decoding before provider dispatch. A random persisted destination revision and one configuration snapshot bind explicit remote consent; stale configuration refuses dispatch. Vision replies identify the actual configured model and remain separate from ordinary agent chat. Cancellation and late-response suppression preserve one active turn; ordinary text payloads remain unchanged. Independent source review, 27 new backend cases, 10 frontend cases and desktop/mobile-browser checks pass.
reviews.remaining: No persisted chat image artifact, native agent multimodal context, native mobile composer or ?learn seed. Vision uses a separate configured VLM turn; no live provider proof. Static images only, at most eight 4 MiB images, 8192 pixels per edge and 16 MP each before downscaling. Destination status stores inert revision metadata in the existing owner Settings DB; this does not provide per-account preferences.

reviews.summary: There is no log endpoint and no log page. No route in agents/core/routers/ or agents/web.py reads the process log (the route snapshot has no `/api/logs` or `/api/admin/logs`), and frontend/src/console-routes.ts has no logs panel. The nearest UI surfaces are `/api/admin/audit` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:301, the hash-chained security log) and `/api/admin/env` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:205); neither is the process log. What exists is the backing file and an offline CLI. `_file_logging_config` (agents/core/log.py:30) turns on a RotatingFileHandler at data_path('logs','jarvis.log'), off by default (`system.log_to_file`). `_install_redaction` (agents/core/log.py:64) puts the H495 SecretRedactionFilter on every handler, so written lines are masked. `nerva logs -n N` (agents/cli/nerva.py:153, `cmd_logs` at agents/cli/nerva.py:918) prints the last N lines on the box, not from the UI, and reads the whole file to do it.
reviews.remaining: The whole row is still owed. (1) An admin-guarded, bounded reverse-read endpoint over the hub log and its rotations, capped at 500 lines, with filters for file, level, component and line count. Redaction must be re-applied at read time, because rotated files and lines written before H495 never went through the filter. (2) A HUD log page with File/Level/Component/Lines filters, level colouring and a 5 s auto-refresh switch with a Live badge. (3) An honest empty state when file logging is off (the default), because there is then no file to tail.

reviews.summary: JobStore/HUD/CLI au creare și editare pentru cele patru acțiuni, constructor vizual de program, 16 blueprint-uri cu formulare tipizate, repeat limitat atomic și livrare per job către canale deja configurate sau doar istoric. Există doctor, incidents (pauze după eșecuri), notepad editabil, status/remove și tick idempotent în fusul scheduler-ului, refuzat când scheduler-ul rulează. Gate-urile task/quiet hours/buget/e-stop sunt păstrate; flush-ul mesajelor amânate verifică acum e-stop. Accesul Automations din bara principală deschide un spațiu dedicat; dialogul nativ de creare gestionează focusul, Tab, Escape și revenirea la buton. Tipurile OpenAPI includ cele patru rute noi. Review: update scrie doar câmpurile cerute și nu poate reseta rezervările atomice; istoricul păstrează textul efectiv pentru brief/remind fără livrare. Scripturile Python locale au acum snapshot de sursă legat de aprobarea fiecărei execuții, rezultate pending persistente și livrare directă no_agent sau context izolat ca date neîncrezătoare. API/CLI disting acceptarea de finalizare; conținutul gol nu apelează modelul. Manual run now persists a bounded receipt and returns HTTP 202; scheduler/offline tick executes through the shared job firing path. Atomic coalescing and portable cross-process locks prevent duplicate execution. Configuration snapshots, pending-script reconciliation, crash-unknown state without replay, and concurrent retention are tested. HUD and CLI restore accepted request status and distinguish queued, waiting and completed execution. Ask jobs now persist effective request-local model/provider pins through CLI/HUD options, with preflight routing, closed lifetimes, approved-model enforcement and resolved context budgets. Unavailable pins fail explicitly; ordinary chat configuration is unchanged. Independent review repaired file_read re-spilling under a pinned window. Owner-authored reminder media IDs now produce actual bounded Telegram file/text delivery with frozen content/recipient bindings, a validated total deadline and durable held/partial/unknown outcomes. CLI/HUD authoring and status expose these outcomes; editing an explicit empty options document clears prior settings correctly. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported. Model-bearing ask jobs now accept enabled_toolsets through CLI and HUD using an explicit installed basic/files/terminal catalog. Missing/null retains defaults; [] disables tool offers. Immutable per-run name sets intersect both runtime/profile offers and ToolRPC intake before preflight, handlers or approval enqueue. Nested scopes only narrow and inherit revocation; ordinary callers and concurrent jobs retain isolated defaults. Unknown/unavailable groups refuse. Existing approvals retain frozen concrete arguments and do not reread job options or revive a request scope. Doctor reports the configured tool-name upper bound, not effective contextual offers. Actual runner/Agent/RPC, queued-edit/restart, cancellation, UI and concurrency tests are evidence; tool selection grants no new authority.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc contextul izolat per job pentru model workdir și skills, agregarea între profile și noul grant schedule.create cerut de original (rădăcină protejată în afara scopului). Opțiunile fără runtime sunt refuzate, nu salvate inert. Nu există probă live pentru scheduler/canale sau autorare nativă mobilă; monitoarele depind de sursele configurate, nu instalează integrări. Cloud pins must match existing policy routing; changed local models require loaded context metadata, and LM Studio currently cannot resolve a changed model. Pinned jobs use deterministic compression and omit auxiliary embedding recall. The initial catalog intentionally excludes dedicated code-runner, delegation and dynamic plugin groups; their transitive restriction contracts remain unimplemented.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 in five rounds. The first round shipped with H200 (critic note 7). After an adversarial review reopened it, the second round added the receiver switch, an event list and a prompt template. After a second review, the third added where a delivery goes (Hermes' Deliver to and deliver only), a description and a receiver switch that fails closed. A third review (review-H153c) found that as shipped, Deliver to reached none of the owner's channels, and the fourth round made a real send reach each offered channel, tested through the real path down to the channel adapter. A fourth review (review-H153d) found that the fourth round's plain-text rendering let one delivery freeze the hub, and rewrote the sender's file names and addresses; the fifth round sends the text as written, bounds every renderer, and fixes the review's minors.

Backend CRUD is admin-guarded, and the store serves every change without a restart:
- GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/webhooks (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:174, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:180, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:193, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:220) list, create, update and delete hooks.
- A create that carries a field it does not know (Hermes' skills, deliver_chat_id) is refused with 422, never silently dropped (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:86).
- WebhookStore.create (agents/core/webhooks.py:434) mints a token and, when signed, an HMAC signing secret. Both are returned once, and every list masks them (agents/core/webhooks.py:583). A save that fails undoes the change in memory.

(1) The receiver card (Hermes' platform-level toggle). The setting webhooks.receiver_enabled is a declared toggle, on by default. It is written through the audited PUT /api/admin/settings/webhooks, and the audit row ends with the value (receiver_enabled=false). A reseed is audited too (agents/core/routers/admin.py:166). When the switch is off, the trigger refuses every delivery with 503. It checks before the body is read and again after authentication, so a switch that lands while a sender streams its body stops that delivery (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:238).
- It fails closed (agents/core/webhooks.py:246):
  - only a literal true is on, and a missing row is the declared default;
  - when the settings store cannot be read, settings_db.read_setting raises instead of answering the default (agents/core/settings_db.py:581), so the last state read or written stays in force;
  - a receiver never read is refused with "the webhook receiver's state cannot be read".
- It is read off the event loop, and by one caller at a time: while a read runs, every other caller gets the last state at once. A caller with no state known yet (the first read after a start) waits for that read, at most two seconds (agents/core/webhooks.py:243), so a burst that arrives while it runs is answered, and a read slower than that is still refused, closed. A state is used for a second before the store is read again. A read that a write, a reset, a reseed or another store overtook while it ran is dropped, a failed one included. A write in this process is seen at once; one from another process (nerva config set) within the second.
- The admin routes keep working, and hooks keep their credentials.
- The panel's receiver row shows on, off, or "not read" with the reason:
  - a failed re-read drops the last state instead of showing it;
  - an answer is shown unless a newer one already is, so an earlier read never overwrites a newer one and a poller slower than its interval still sees each answer (frontend/src/panel-kit.tsx:20);
  - ↻ re-reads it;
  - a stored value that is not true or false is shown as off;
  - a store with no row yet, which the hub answers with its own 404 naming the category, shows the hub's default, "on · not stored", and can be switched off, because the write creates the row (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:196); any other 404 (a proxy's) is a failed read.
- Interop and the /v1 panel show every hook as refused while the switch is off.

(2) The New-subscription modal: name, description, agent or workflow target, target id, HMAC signing (the secret, shown once), an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only. Create is last in the tab order (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:385).
- Events: up to 32 printable names of 1 to 64 characters, no comma, stored stripped and kept once each, ignoring ASCII case (agents/core/webhooks.py:137).
  - The delivery's event comes from the sender's header (X-GitHub-Event, X-Gitlab-Event, X-Event-Key, X-Event-Type, X-Webhook-Event), else from the payload's event or type (agents/core/webhooks.py:121). It is bounded when read but never cut to the 64-character limit, so a longer name matches no subscription.
  - A hook with a list runs only the deliveries whose event is on it. Every other delivery is answered 202 with the reason, never run, and counted as skipped (agents/core/webhooks.py:553). That includes a delivery that names no event, and a list a hand edit broke (null, not a list, an item that is not a name).
- Template: {a.b.0} reads the JSON payload by key and list index, {event} is the event, {payload} the whole body, and {payload.x} a payload key the template reserves (agents/core/webhooks.py:173).
  - Nothing else is read. A missing value is empty, a string is used as is and anything else as JSON.
  - The work is bounded by the caps (agents/core/webhooks.py:157): each path is read once per render, a value is encoded only up to 4,000 characters, and substitution stops at 16,000.
  - A template that renders nothing is skipped, not run. So is an untemplated delivery with no text, which gets its own reason.
- A body over 5 MiB is refused with 413 before it is read whole (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:235).

(3) Deliver to and deliver only (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:323, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:335).
- deliver is log (the default: the reply stays in the sender's response and the session) or one of the owner's own channels that something receives: telegram, voice or ntfy (agents/core/webhooks.py:70). Names are matched exactly.
- web is refused by name: nothing in the hub connects a client to the web channel, so a push there would never arrive. /api/channels/targets and nerva send --list say the same: web is not ready while no client is connected (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:88).
- The reply, or a workflow's last step, goes through send_to_target and ChannelManager.send to the owner's own destination (Telegram's owner chat). send_to_target writes an IntentLog row per send. The text is labelled "Webhook <name> - <event>", and each channel carries the label its own way:
  - ntfy gets it as its title, folded to printable ASCII and cut to 120 characters;
  - telegram and voice get it on the first line.
- The text goes as written: nothing is rendered and nothing is rewritten, so a file name, an address and a Markdown link arrive as the sender wrote them, and a link shows its address. What hides or reorders text is dropped (bidi overrides and isolates, the zero-width space, word joiners, the soft hyphen, the BOM, control characters but a newline and a tab; a zero-width joiner stays), and a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:307). Telegram sends it with no parse mode, no link preview and no voice note, and ntfy unrendered (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:202, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:320, agents/core/channels/ntfy.py:137). Voice speaks it without the markup. A longer text is cut at 4,000 characters with a note that says where the rest is (the session for a reply, nowhere for deliver-only text).
- Nothing on the push path renders, so a delivery costs linear time in its text: one long line cannot hold the event loop. The renderers the rest of the hub uses bound every marker span (a link, bold, italic, a heading line), so one long line costs linear time there too, and a span past the bound is left as written (agents/core/channels/render.py:40).
- The hook is read again after the turn. If it was deleted or switched off, or the receiver was switched off or cannot be read, nothing is pushed and the hook says why; a hook moved to another destination is pushed there, labelled with its name as it is then.
- Quiet hours (ambient.quiet_hours_start/end, 22 to 7 by default, hours taken modulo 24, the jobs' own reading, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:270) keep every push off the phone and the speaker. An hour setting that is not a number (an infinity, NaN, text) keeps its default, for the jobs too (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:82). The push is noted on the hook, not held for the morning as a job's message is.
- A hook makes at most 30 push attempts an hour (agents/core/webhooks.py:370, per process). An attempt the channel refused counts, and the panel says so; a push held by quiet hours spends none. A push over it is noted, not sent.
- deliver_only skips the agent: the rendered text goes straight to the destination, and no turn runs. It needs a channel: deliver-only with the log is refused on create and on PATCH, with the reason (agents/core/webhooks.py:101). A record from before that rule can still be switched off, and its delivery says the text was dropped.
- A workflow delivers its last step's output, or nothing when the run failed or its last step returned an error, never an earlier step's output (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:408). The last step is the last to run, in the pipeline's batch order, not the last listed, and a run that stopped early delivers the last step that ran (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:384). An output the router cannot read is recorded, and nothing is pushed.
- Each delivery's outcome (channel, ok, reason, time) is kept on the hook and shown in its detail pane, and the response carries it too. Every exit after a call is counted is recorded, a missing or invalid workflow and a failed turn included (agents/core/webhooks.py:643).
- A delivery that fails is recorded and answered 200. Every answer is encodable whatever the sender or a step put in it: a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD and a NaN or an infinity null (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:433), so a delivery is never a 500 after its push. A workflow hook answers with ok, the steps that ran and the delivery, never the run's context, which holds the sender's text and every step's output. A failed turn itself still answers 500, so the sender's retry runs it again.

(4) The subscriptions list with per-route enable/disable and delete. PATCH /api/webhooks/{hook_id} (agents/core/webhooks.py:501) takes any of enabled (a strict boolean), events, prompt, deliver, deliver_only and description, and changes them in place. It refuses:
- null (and its schema advertises none);
- an empty body;
- an unknown field;
- a destination the create would refuse.

The schema names the four destinations as an enum. A hook switched off keeps its token and secret. The trigger refuses it with 403 after authentication, from the live record, before the event filter.

Each row has an on/off switch, an HMAC or token badge, an event-count badge, the destination (none for the log) and delete with an inline confirmation. The detail pane shows the description, the calls, the skipped deliveries, where the result goes, how a push goes (on a hook that pushes) and how the last delivery went. It edits all of them and opens at the hook's own destination. After a save focus returns to the hook's row, or to the create form when the hook is gone. The legacy /v1 panel lists, creates and deletes through adminFetch, and shows the receiver as the hub reads it and each destination (agents/web/static/tools.js:310).

(5) The restart banners. Nerva needs no restart for either kind of change: the receiver switch is a setting read at most a second old, and hook CRUD is served live.

Audit: create, switch, update and delete each write a SecurityEvent (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:142). It names:
- the hook id;
- the target as a JSON string;
- the event list;
- the template's length (never its text);
- the destination and deliver only;
- the signed and enabled flags.

It never records the token or secret. A switch alone is recorded as enable or disable; any other change is an update. The receiver switch is audited by the settings route, with its value, and a choice setting's value is in its row (a toggle, a select, a number, a slider). A nerva config set from the shell writes no audit row (H378).

Deliveries: an agent-target delivery goes through handle_input(channel="webhook"). origin_for_channel (agents/core/action_origin.py:36) classifies that channel as inbound, so the payload is tainted and the kernel's GRANT->QUEUE escalation applies. A workflow target runs its pipeline (agents/core/routers/workflows.py:37) under the inbound action origin. The sender waits for the push as well as the turn. A retried delivery runs again: H659 owns idempotency.

Adapted, not copied:
- Deliver to: Hermes offers log, Telegram, Discord, Slack, email and a GitHub comment. Nerva offers the log and the owner's own telegram, voice and ntfy, and refuses the rest by name with a 422 (agents/core/webhooks.py:75):
  - Email is never an outbound side effect of an inbound delivery (the rule ChannelManager.send keeps).
  - A GitHub comment writes to someone else's system, so the hook's agent proposes it through the governed write-back path, one approval each.
  - Discord and Slack are reply-only transports here, with no home channel to address.
  - The web HUD has no push receiver yet.
- Per-subscription skills: a Nerva hook targets an agent or a workflow, and the agent brings its own skills to the turn. Hermes' own modal does not expose skills either.

Tests:
- tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py (54 cases) covers the receiver, the event filter, the template and the update.
- tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (35) covers the switch, the audit and the in-flight race.
- tests/test_h153b_webhook_delivery.py (63) covers the second round with fakes for the send and the clock.
- tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py (80, the fourth round) runs the real path, the router through send_to_target and ChannelManager to a recording adapter per channel. It covers:
  - each channel (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:104), with and without a turn;
  - the real quiet-hours rule on a fixed clock (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:273);
  - the real Telegram adapter's HTTP body (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:229);
  - fail-soft delivery (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:319);
  - a switch thrown during the turn (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:455);
  - the workflow rule (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:534);
  - the push cap, the single-flight receiver (tests/test_h153c_webhook_sends.py:605), and the audit of free text.
- tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py (61 cases, the fifth round) covers:
  - a long line of brackets pushed at once, and the text as written on Telegram and ntfy (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:67);
  - every renderer in linear time on one long line (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:129);
  - the hidden characters, the first-read burst (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:151), the workflow answer and the encodable answers (tests/test_h153d_webhook_review.py:253);
  - the last step as run, the unreadable receiver after the turn, a Telegram refusal, the hour of the allowance, quiet hours and the allowance, the live label, an overtaken failed read, a slider's audited value, the hour settings and web's readiness.
- frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 55 cases, frontend/src/test/use-api-sequence.test.tsx 4 (a poller slower than its interval, loading until the newest answer, an earlier answer never over a newer one, another address), frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx 14 and the /v1 tests/frontend/tools.test.js 18.

Mutation:
- The fourth round: 92 mutants of its guards and of the reviewer's 35 unpinned survivors (70 backend, 20 panel and Interop, 2 /v1). Three no longer applied to the final code; the reviewer replayed the 89 that apply, and each is caught.
- The fifth round: 40 mutants of its guards (32 Python, 8 HUD), each run against its own suites. 39 are caught, one of them (the answer's dict keys) by a test added for it. Four were first written malformed and were rewritten before they counted.
- The fourth review's own 104 mutants left 20 survivors: seven equivalent, one a strengthening (catching an infinite hour, now the code) and twelve unpinned. Each of the twelve now has a test.

The SOUL can be read from the UI but not edited. `GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/soul` (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:86) returns the file that `soul_path_for` (agents/core/agent.py:374) resolves. That is the same file the builder `Agent._read_soul` (agents/core/agent.py:432) gives the model, and the route also returns the H387 guard verdict. The agent Dossier renders it read-only (frontend/src/modes.tsx:70). `PromptsPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2680) drives the prompt-VC store `SoulVersionStore.commit` (agents/core/soul_versioning.py:45) and its admin routes. Those routes cover commit, rollback and preview (agents/core/routers/admin.py:428, agents/core/routers/admin.py:455, agents/core/routers/admin.py:503), plus history, diff and A/B. The store is a side record, not the persona source, and the code says so (agents/core/learning/evolution.py:16-20). The persona is read at construction: `Agent._load_soul` (agents/core/agent.py:501) is called only from `Agent.__init__` (agents/core/agent.py:430). Since H672 it is also re-read on a running hub. `Agent.refresh_soul` (agents/core/agent.py:513) runs the same builder behind a stat probe, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:326) calls it for every agent in the process. The trigger is a context-compaction commit (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3473). So a hand edit of the SOUL file reaches the model at the next compaction without a restart (tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py).
reviews.remaining: (1) No write path to the live persona. Nothing writes a committed or rolled-back version into the SOUL.local.md that `soul_path_for` resolves. A commit in PromptsPanel still changes nothing the agent says until someone edits the file by hand. The H672 refresh reads only that file, never the version store. It fires only when a session's context compaction commits, so it is not a reload the editor can trigger; with no compaction, the edit still waits for a restart. (2) The version store is not seeded from the on-disk SOUL, so its history is empty for any persona never committed through the panel. (3) The commit and rollback routes write no audit event, but the governance requires SOUL edits in the audit log. (4) No description editor and no Auto-generate. `PUT /api/admin/agents/{agent_id}` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:530) only stores display overrides in an in-memory dict, and nothing drafts a description with a model for the owner to accept. (5) The Dossier has no Edit action that opens the current SOUL in the versioned editor.

reviews.summary: The backend is as strong as the row says. `GET /api/admin/settings` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:73) returns every category, alongside per-category GET/PUT. The PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:144) runs `validate_category` and answers 422 before any write, and `_audit_settings_change` records the changed key names, with the new value of a choice (a toggle, select, number or slider; never a secret key or free text, and since the third H153 review a typed model id counts as free text: `_audited_values`, agents/core/routers/admin.py:98). `POST /api/admin/settings/reseed` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:161) reseeds everything, and says so in one audit row. The v2 console `SettingsPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2640) reads that route and shows every declared key (163 in 20 categories at this commit). Among them are the six `llm.openrouter_*` upstream-routing keys HEQ lot 1 added for H583, whose slug lists `_validate_value` refuses when they are not slugs. Its widgets are typed by `settingsField` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2630), and dirty edits are saved in one batch. The standalone /admin app's `GlobalConfigPage` (agents/web/static/admin.js:447) has a search box, but it filters a hand-curated SECTIONS table of 61 keys, not the whole schema. Its only reset is the global reseed (agents/web/static/admin.js:1477). `nerva config list|get|set|check` (`cmd_config`, agents/cli/nerva.py:667) edits single keys offline with the same validation.
reviews.remaining: (1) No cross-key search over every setting: SettingsPanel has no filter, and the /admin search reaches only the 61 keys in its SECTIONS table, not all 163. The six new `llm.openrouter_*` keys, for example, are reachable only from SettingsPanel and `nerva config`. (2) No export of the configuration as JSON for moving it to another box; secret-kind values would need masking or exclusion. (3) No import: no route takes a JSON document, runs every key through `validate_category` first, and then does an all-or-nothing write with an audit row. (4) No per-category reset: only the global `/api/admin/settings/reseed` exists (it writes one audit row, naming no category).

reviews.summary: The classification half exists, but nothing surfaces it as a banner. ResourceProbe (agents/core/autonomy/observer.py:96) reads psutil RAM percent and disk percent and compares them with DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS (observer.py:89: RAM and disk warn at 85%, critical at 95%) through _threshold_signal. ProactiveObserver.evaluate (observer.py:225) acts only on state changes. It submits a READ_ONLY monitor.alert autonomy task on healthy-to-unhealthy (observer.py:307) and a monitor.recovery task on the way back. The orchestrator builds the observer from default_probes() (agents/core/orchestrator.py:912). The autonomy coordinator tick calls observer.observe() (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:307) every system.autonomy_tick seconds, 60 by default (autonomy_coordinator.py:252). GET /ticker (agents/core/routers/dashboard.py:235, get_ticker) reads observer.status() (dashboard.py:244) and turns each unhealthy signal into a WARNING ticker item, marked high priority when CRITICAL. The HUD fetches it in frontend/src/api/loaders.ts:161. The skills/system_monitor skill has its own warn/critical/emergency thresholds for on-demand snapshots. /status still carries only raw ram_used/ram_total from _sys_info (agents/web.py:819), with no pressure field.
reviews.remaining: Missing pieces: (1) The banner. Nothing in frontend/src renders a memory/disk pressure banner, ranks the five conditions (disk critical, memory critical, suspected OOM restart, disk elevated, memory elevated) or shows only the worst undismissed one. Pressure appears only as scrolling ticker lines and autonomy-queue alert tasks. (2) Suspected OOM restart. Nothing reads a boot id, the previous process's exit state or kernel OOM evidence; agents/ has no boot_id, dmesg or oom-kill references outside unrelated modules. (3) Dismissal. There is no dismissal at all, so none is keyed by boot id or re-armed after a restart. (4) Clearing on confirmed recovery. evaluate flips to healthy on the first healthy sample (no hysteresis), so a flapping reading clears and re-raises. Sampling also stops entirely when autonomy.mode is off (autonomy_coordinator.py:302) or ESTOP is engaged (autonomy_coordinator.py:257), which leaves the warning dependent on autonomy being on. The disk probe watches only '/' by default, not the data directory's volume.

reviews.summary:
Built on this branch. Hermes has a Documentation page inside its dashboard with an "open in a new tab" affordance. Nerva's written material (the user guide, FLAGS.md on what each posture flag costs, and the privacy and camera-privacy notes) was only in the repository. The Dockerfile copied it into the image, but nothing served it.

(1) The route. agents/core/routers/help_docs.py is registered in agents/web.py (agents/web.py:1397) and user-guarded on the router (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:27).
- GET /api/help/docs (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:103) lists the allowlist: slug, title, whether the file shipped, and each document's sections.
- GET /api/help/docs/{slug} (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:113) returns the Markdown text, capped at MAX_DOC_CHARS with a truncated flag (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:121).
- The allowlist is the fixed DOCS table (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:31): user-guide, flags, privacy, camera-privacy. A slug is only ever a key into it, never joined into a path, so an unknown slug, '../' or encoded traversal is 404.
- A file must be a regular file under the install root; a symlink is refused (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:85). A file missing from an install reads as "not available", not an error.
- Responses are no-store.

(2) The page. DocsPanel (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:37) is registered in the console's Start group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:6), in PANEL_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/gap.tsx:4770) and in the desktop app's route allowlist (desktop/src-tauri/hud-routes.json:49).
- It lists the documents, disabling one not shipped, and renders the chosen one through the new shared Markdown component (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:98).
- That component emits React elements only (no innerHTML path): headings with anchors, code fences, pipe tables, lists, quotes and rules, plus bold, italic, inline code and links. A link renders only for http(s) or a same-origin path, in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer (safeHref, frontend/src/markdown.tsx:25). Raw HTML in a document stays literal text. There is no regex lookbehind, so older Safari can parse the bundle.

(3) Open in a new tab. Every document is a standalone deep link, /v2/console/docs?doc=<slug>[#section] (docHref, frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:15). The panel offers it as "open in a new tab ↗" with rel=noopener noreferrer (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:67), and a #section is scrolled into view (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:49).

(4) The flag's cost where it is flipped, per the row rationale.
- Each document's sections carry the names their headings document. The hub computes them with heading_anchor (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:44), which one shared fixture pins character for character to the renderer's headingAnchor (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:94).
- The Settings panel links every setting FLAGS.md documents to its section with a "cost ↗" beside the toggle (sectionIndex, frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:20; frontend/src/gap.tsx:2643, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2668).
- The security posture panel links to the flags document (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1010).

The route/auth/OpenAPI snapshots, the HUD parity rules, the API sweep chapter and frontend/src/api/schema.gen.ts are regenerated.

Tests:
- tests/test_help_docs_route.py, 25 cases:
  - the list and each allowlisted document (tests/test_help_docs_route.py:35, tests/test_help_docs_route.py:49);
  - seven off-list and traversal URLs, all 404 (tests/test_help_docs_route.py:67);
