- frontend/src/test/markdown.test.tsx: structure, snake_case kept as text, hostile HTML inert, safe links only, no raw-HTML sink and no lookbehind in the source, the same anchor fixture, heading ids.
- frontend/src/test/docs-panel.test.tsx: registration, rendering, switching and truncation, deep links to a doc and to a section, and the Settings cost link.
All 1,346 vitest cases pass, as do tsc, the e2e typecheck and the build.

Destructive confirmation is implemented in several places with no shared primitive. Markdown now has one shared component, frontend/src/markdown.tsx (built for H165: React nodes only; headings with anchors, fences, pipe tables, bullet and ordered lists, quotes, rules, bold/italic/inline code, and links only for http(s) or same-origin paths with rel=noopener; pinned by frontend/src/test/markdown.test.tsx). Only the Documentation panel uses it so far. Chat bubbles in Conversation (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:75, cockpit.tsx:91) and the shell drawer (frontend/src/shell.tsx:143) render agent text through renderRich (cockpit.tsx:120-124), which handles only **bold**. Lists, code fences, tables, headings and links show as raw characters. frontend/src/artifacts.tsx has a separate MarkdownBody that renders only React text nodes (artifacts.tsx:73-102: headings, bold, inline code, bullet lists; raw HTML stays literal, pinned by frontend/src/test/artifacts.test.tsx:79). It is private to canvas artifacts and has no code fences, ordered lists, tables or links. Destructive confirmation is hand-rolled per panel: forget-me requires a typed FORGET (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3153, gap.tsx:3188); acquisition purge a typed phrase (gap.tsx:3961); trust-ops rotation a typed scope (frontend/src/panels/trust-ops.tsx:215); marketplace removal an arm/confirm pair (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx:203); webhook delete another (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:424); the ESTOP pause a two-step button (frontend/src/modes3.tsx:166). KillSwitchPanel's HALT ALL/disengage toggle (gap.tsx:757) fires on one click through the plain Btn (frontend/src/panel-kit.tsx:115). No component maps a confirmation level to the kernel's RiskTier (agents/core/autonomy/policy.py:26-31).
reviews.remaining: (1) Adopt the shared Markdown component (frontend/src/markdown.tsx, which already covers the required syntax safely) in the chat bubbles and the shell drawer in place of renderRich, and in artifacts.tsx in place of MarkdownBody, keeping the artifacts' 4,000-character bound. (2) A single confirm primitive whose severity tiers mirror RiskTier: reversible gets a one-click or two-step confirm, irreversible/money a typed confirmation. It must replace the hand-rolled confirmations in KillSwitchPanel (including disengage), forget-me, acquisition purge, marketplace removal, webhook delete, trust-ops rotation and the ESTOP pause, so the UI and the approval queue describe risk the same way.

reviews.summary: Host Tauri compilat pe macOS; Cargo.lock și iconul sunt incluse. Pachet .app temporar nesemnat folosit pentru verificare UI locală.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc instalatoare semnate/notarizate per OS și proba distribuției Windows/Linux; .app de validare nu este un release semnat.

reviews.summary: Meniu tray executabil, ferestre main/floating, ascundere la close, geometrie flotantă persistentă și reset/handoff; verificare UI locală macOS.
reviews.remaining: Geometria ferestrei principale, zoom dedicat, translucency/frost, unread badge, find-in-page și distribuția multiplatformă rămân deschise.

reviews.summary: The uninstall model exists and is sound. plan_uninstall (agents/core/uninstall.py:50) is a side-effect-free probe reporting which UNINSTALL_TARGETS exist, and as what kind. run_uninstall (agents/core/uninstall.py:65) removes only those targets and reports what it could not remove. Data erasure is a separate opt-in that runs purge_data backup-first before any target is removed. The CLI _main (agents/core/uninstall.py:127) refuses without --confirm (agents/core/uninstall.py:134). uninstall.sh and UNINSTALL.bat wrap the module. tests/test_uninstall.py checks the targets against install.sh/INSTALL.bat, plan reporting (tests/test_uninstall.py:75), idempotence and purge ordering. The data half is already reachable in-app: BackupPanel's typed FORGET reveal (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3159) calls POST /api/admin/forget (agents/core/routers/backup.py:99), which requires {confirm: 'FORGET'}. The row's kernel gate would plug into agents/core/kernel/registry.py, which has no uninstall action today.
reviews.remaining:
There is no uninstall from inside the app.
- plan_uninstall has no caller outside tests: no --gui-summary flag, no admin route serving the pre-flight summary, and no HUD Danger-zone panel rendering it.
- No route or HUD control runs the software-only or software+data removal.
- The run must cross the kernel at the irreversible tier (approval queue floor) with a typed confirmation.
- It must be executed by a detached cleanup that waits for the hub process to exit before deleting the .venv the hub runs from.

reviews.summary: Execuția guvernată pe altă mașină există. Ținta declarată de owner intră în registrul de politici din aceeași sursă ca detaliile de conexiune, iar o comandă trece hardline → politica țintei → aprobare durabilă → contractul terminal.exec pe rădăcinile remote declarate → Action Kernel înainte să atingă firul. Firul rulează un argv reconstruit cu shlex pe shell-ul remote (niciun string de shell nu pleacă de aici), cu cheia de gazdă pinuită, doar pe cheie, fără ~/.ssh/config, fără agent și fără forwarding. Default-off în spatele JARVIS_TERMINAL_SSH_HOST; cu flagul nesetat inventarul rămâne identic.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

reviews.summary: Fereastră flotantă frameless/resizable cu cerere always-on-top unde compositorul o suportă; controale tray/main, hide/reset/handoff, geometrie fizică persistentă cu recuperare monitor/DPI. Refolosește ChatMode, autentificarea HUD și sesiunea server; refresh la focus/finalizarea unui turn fără suprascrierea streamului. Compilare și verificare UI macOS. Invalidările primite cât timp turnul local este ocupat sunt păstrate și reconciliate la idle; teste cu BroadcastChannel asincron real verifică două ferestre cu turnuri suprapuse.
reviews.remaining: Hermes overlay complet rămâne neechivalat: fără transparency/frost, click-through, press-and-hold composer drag, game-overlay watcher, Hyprland promotion, global chord/move-to-pointer sau citirea ferestrei de dedesubt. Windows/Linux și deconectarea fizică a monitorului neverificate; Wayland declară placement/topmost nesuportate.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no keep-awake or power awareness. There is no power assertion (caffeinate, systemd-inhibit, logind Inhibit or SetThreadExecutionState), no psutil.sensors_battery reading, no power-resume or battery-state events, no battery-aware throttling and no stream-aware webview background policy anywhere in agents/, scripts/, frontend/src, mobile/src or desktop/src-tauri/src. hardware.detect_hardware (agents/core/hardware.py:215) uses psutil (agents/core/hardware.py:224) only for CPU threads and RAM. The Tauri shell (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs) manages windows and geometry and does not own the backend process. A turn enters through Orchestrator.process (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1633), which is where a per-turn assertion would attach. host.control is already KERNEL-mediated (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:52), which is the gate the row names.

Motorul SQLite, CLI și HUD pot crea, edita, porni, pune pe pauză, relua și șterge joburi; există istoric, un constructor vizual de program, galeria de 16 blueprint-uri tipizate (`BLUEPRINTS` din `jobs.py`, bază + `EXTRA_BLUEPRINTS`) și o țintă de livrare per job (`Job.channel`). Reevaluat 2026-09-19: textul anterior spunea „3 blueprint-uri și nicio țintă per job" — ambele expirate.
reviews.remaining: „Deliver to" în Hermes e o listă cu mai multe ținte bifabile; Nerva are o singură țintă per job (`channel: str | None`), nu mai multe. Avertismentul de impact al modelului și toast-ul de confirmare pentru un model scump nu sunt verificate în panou. Crearea unui job trebuie să treacă prin kernel (`schedule.create` nou, sau `goal.approve` refolosit) — kind în `agents/core/kernel/**`, path protejat, sarcina owner-ului. NEVERIFICAT pe scheduler și canale reale.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:186), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:48; frontend/src/gap.tsx:16). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:341). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:174, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:180, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:193, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:220).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:342). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:302); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:144): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:51: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:583).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:142, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:189, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:214 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:226). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:136), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes nothing and answers 404 "webhook not found".

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:348). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

Tests: frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 55 cases. By describe block, 22 are this row's (the panel, the trigger URL and the review round), and 13 of those failed on the pre-review panel: the pending hold, the reload and the ghost row after a switch or delete, the one-POST create and the create held while a secret shows, the hook-named buttons, focus, the alert without the secret, the "copied" live region, the loopback hint and an unencodable id. The other 33 are H153's: the subscriptions, the receiver row and banner, the event list, the template, Deliver to, focus after a hook is gone, the push note and a proxy's 404. frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx (14 cases, 5 of them H153's receiver read) drives the real useLiveModes against admin-guarded mock routes and renders InteropMode. The backend audit and DELETE guards are pinned in tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:353, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:362, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:371). Mutation: 60 mutants of the review round's guards (11 backend, 27 panel, 15 Interop, 7 v1) and 16 of the H153 panel additions were each run against their own suite, and all were caught; before the review round, 12 of the reviewer's 42 mutants had survived.

The installed-tree and registry surfaces are wired end to end. GET /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:29) and the admin-guarded marketplace routes (list, history, rollback, publish, install, install-zip, review, uninstall, pending, approve; agents/core/routers/skills.py:355-580) each have a HUD caller. The console panels are all registered in frontend/src/console-routes.ts: SKILLS MARKETPLACE (review + rollback, frontend/src/gap.tsx:1764), Marketplace Admin (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx: publish, install-zip and uninstall keyed by folder name, which avoids the manifest-title trap), Skills Import, Skill History, Pending Skills and the Security Skills Map. Per-skill usage counters (use_count, last_used_at) are tracked in agents/core/skills/usage.py:34. SkillCurator (agents/core/skills/curator.py:35) archives stale agent-created, unpinned skills on its own schedule. Per-agent scoping exists only as author-declared manifest `agents:` filtering in SkillLoader.prompt_catalog (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1246-1247) and the static agents.yaml `tools:` list (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:50). test_skills_api.py, test_skill_lifecycle_curator.py and test_skill_approval_revoke.py: 37 pass.
reviews.remaining: Both gaps the rationale accepts are absent. (1) Per-agent skill enable/disable as a capability grant: the permission ledger's SURFACES (agents/core/permission_ledger.py:69) has no skill surface. No route or HUD control enables or disables a skill for an agent, there is no All master switch, and neither SkillLoader.prompt_catalog nor SkillLoader.execute (agents/core/skills/loader.py:499) consults an owner-set grant. The manifest `agents:` field is author-controlled and only un-advertises. (2) A 'Disable unused' sweep: usage.py records use_count and last_used_at, but no owner-triggered route or control disables idle skills. The curator acts only on agent-created skills, on its own schedule, and never on imported or bundled ones. The profile-scope selector waits on the profile export/import row.

reviews.summary: Memoria și graful au backend; DW-1 afișează entități și legături reale, cu mostre doar în Demo.
reviews.remaining: Rămân timeline/as-of, paritatea exploratorului și controalele de memorie cerute de rând; o listă de vecini nu închide harta semantică.

reviews.summary: Keyboard handling is a set of hard-coded window keydown listeners. App's handler (frontend/src/app.tsx:198-219) maps digits 1-9 and 0 to modes through a literal object (frontend/src/app.tsx:212), Ctrl/Cmd+K to the palette, and a, m and ` to the ambient, cinema and console overlays. Cinema binds o, n, b and Escape in its own effect (frontend/src/shell.tsx:386-392). Ambient and ConsoleOverlay each bind Escape. frontend/src/test/app-routing.test.tsx pins these fixed hotkeys. The quickbar 'SHORTCUTS' list is chat commands, not key bindings. There is no keybind registry, no shortcuts panel and no rebinding.
reviews.remaining: None of the accepted requirement exists. Missing: (1) a single-source-of-truth action registry (id, category, label, default chord, handler) that app.tsx and shell.tsx dispatch through instead of literal key maps; (2) a Keyboard Shortcuts panel opened by mod+/, with categories (Navigation, View, Composer, Session) and search; (3) click-to-rebind with a 'Press a key…' recorder; (4) per-binding reset and reset-all; (5) an 'Also bound to X' conflict note; (6) persisted overrides; (7) the governance rule that no chord may target an approval or decision action.

reviews.summary: Sessions can only be listed and resumed. GET /sessions (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:26-32) returns CheckpointManager.get_sessions (agents/core/checkpoint.py:341), a plain `SELECT * FROM sessions ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ?` with no archived column or filter. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2374) shows the 12 newest sessions with a resume button; `nerva sessions` and the mobile client read the same list. Deletion exists only for the whole install: POST /api/admin/forget (agents/core/routers/backup.py:99) runs a backup-first purge through agents/core/data_purge.py, and the TTL retention sweep (schedule_retention, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:171, over agents/core/retention.py) prunes transcripts past their TTL. test_retention.py, test_data_purge.py and test_session_continuation.py: 66 pass.
reviews.remaining: No archive tier exists. Missing: an archived flag on sessions; archive/unarchive routes; an Archived Chats view with per-row Unarchive and Delete permanently; a per-session permanent delete routed through data_purge's backup-first path and the irreversible approval bucket (today only the install-wide /api/admin/forget exists); an 'auto-archive stale chats' setting with a scheduler job; and a default project directory setting.

reviews.summary: Spend is measured and capped. cost_tracker records each agent turn against the routed model, persists per-UTC-day rollups and flags unpriced calls (agents/core/cost_tracker.py). apm_summary (agents/core/cost_tracker.py:381) returns {totals, by_agent, by_model} (agents/core/cost_tracker.py:456), served by the admin-guarded GET /api/admin/apm (agents/core/routers/admin.py:363). agents/core/routers/analytics.py adds GET /api/analytics/cost (analytics.py:92), /api/analytics/model-tiers with local/fast/standard/heavy/unknown tiers (analytics.py:99), /api/analytics/locality (analytics.py:151) and per-agent/per-day /api/cost (analytics.py:309). The Trust-mode %-local meter reads /api/analytics/locality (frontend/src/app.tsx:431, derivation in frontend/src/locality.ts). test_h10_16_apm.py, test_cost_measurement_and_cap.py, test_h10_24_cost_trace.py and test_cost_tracker.py: 59 pass.
reviews.remaining: The owner still cannot see where the money went. The only HUD reader, APMPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1858-1865), reads d.runs, d.tokens and d.cost, but apm_summary nests those under d.totals. Every field therefore renders '—', and no per-agent or per-model breakdown is shown. /api/cost, /api/analytics/cost and /api/analytics/model-tiers have no HUD caller. No surface shows a local-vs-cloud split of spend or tokens: the %-local meter counts runs only. The Command Center has no Usage section. There is no per-session context/usage meter (tokens, context used/max/percent, cost): the /chat ChatResponse in agents/web.py carries only reply and pending_approvals, and the CLI usage report hard-codes cost_basis 'unavailable' (agents/cli/nerva.py:1404).

reviews.summary: Mic state is shown only inside the HUD page: the TopBar MIC badge (frontend/src/shell.tsx:58), the wall's MIC footer (frontend/src/wall.tsx:395) and the cockpit mic button. All three are fed by GET /api/trust/status (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:216). Its `mic` field comes from _trust_status (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:180), which derives it solely from the JARVIS_MIC_MUTED env flag (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:193), not from the voice pipeline's listening state. The desktop shell (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs) creates only the main and floating windows and a tray icon (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:244) with a static 'Nerva' tooltip (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:246). VoicePipeline (agents/core/voice/pipeline.py:19) and WakeWordDetector (agents/core/voice/wake_word.py:26) keep their running state private. tests/test_trust_api.py (9 pass) covers the trust-status route only.
reviews.remaining: None of the accepted requirement exists. Missing: (1) an indicator surface outside the main window (a small always-on-top window or a tray icon/tooltip that changes with state) that shows listening state when the HUD is unfocused or hidden; (2) a get/set/on-state API for listening/wake state, since VoicePipeline, WakeWordDetector and the satellite hub publish none; (3) a push of state changes to the desktop shell. The trust-status `mic` value is a static env-flag mute switch, not a live 'I am listening' signal. The indicator must stay read-only: turning the mic on is a device permission, not a control on this surface.

reviews.summary: The data exists behind several separate routes, but there is no single inspector and no view of the resolved system prompt on any surface. The terminal client agents/cli/nerva.py offers three related verbs. `nerva status` (cmd_status, agents/cli/nerva.py:583) prints version, backend, and the model with its /status inventory word, where a legacy `ready` is now shown as `resident`. It also prints a `runnable:` line with the hub's strict route verdict: route → provider/model plus a named reason, read from GET /api/onboarding/command-center by `_runnable` (agents/cli/nerva.py:527). It then prints busy agents, channels and e-stop. `nerva tools` (cmd_tools, agents/cli/nerva.py:739) shows the recent tool-event trail, not the available toolset. `nerva prompt-size` (cmd_prompt_size, agents/cli/nerva.py:1924) shows the offline per-component prompt cost. GET /api/toolrpc/tools (agents/core/routers/mesh.py:170) and /sandbox/status list registered ToolRPC tools. GET /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:29) lists skills, GET /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:51) lists MCP servers, and GET /api/system-map (agents/core/routers/system_map.py:387) serves the component map. Each HUD panel in frontend/src/gap.tsx reads one of these on its own.
reviews.remaining: No inspector payload or view exists. Nothing composes these into one read-only payload: model, agent state and context usage; the tools the tool profile actually offers this principal and agent (ToolProfileResolver output, not the raw registry); the advertised skills catalog; the MCP servers with transport and connection status; and the resolved system prompt (Agent.build_prompt with the core-memory, skills and runtime-state blocks). `nerva status --json` now joins /status, e-stop and the runnable verdict, but only on the client side and with no context usage, tools, skills, MCP servers or prompt. The resolved system prompt appears on no surface. The terminal client has no verb that shows tools, skills, MCP servers or the prompt, and the HUD has no panel reading a shared payload, so nothing guarantees the two surfaces agree.

reviews.summary: Nerva copies Hermes's setup.runtime_check into the owner's terminal. The hub resolves the route with the same llm_router.select_backend call a Jarvis turn makes (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:241) and names its verdict: a local provider/model pair must be resident, and a cloud route (Gemini, Claude, or the cloud-compatible adapter set by llm.compatible_provider) counts only when the router handed back the very backend that route names (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:142, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:278-281). A real HybridRouter pins this for the local, cloud-flash, claude and both cloud-compatible paths (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:493). `nerva doctor` (and `python scripts/doctor.py`) adds the advisory runtime_resolves row: one GET of /api/onboarding/command-center at the hub `nerva status` reads (scripts/doctor.py:234), run only after /readyz answered at that same address and otherwise reported as skip, never ok (scripts/doctor.py:365-369). It sends one credential, the user token when both are set and the admin token only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address (scripts/doctor.py:333-340, scripts/doctor.py:286), never prints it, and is ok only on a ready verdict that names the route, provider and model (scripts/doctor.py:416-420). A refused token, a reply cut off mid-body, a listener that does not speak HTTP, a bad URL or an odd resident list is a named warn, not a traceback (scripts/doctor.py:396-401; tests/test_doctor.py:433, tests/test_doctor.py:458). `nerva status` now labels the old any-model state 'resident' and adds a runnable: line from the same verdict (agents/cli/nerva.py:527); a timeout or reset on that read shows 'unknown — hub_unreachable' and the rest of the status still prints (agents/cli/nerva.py:537). A reply cut off mid-body or a garbled status line on any hub read is HubUnavailable, so `nerva status` reports an unreachable hub instead of a traceback (agents/cli/client.py:151, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:179). Both tools dial a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0, ::) over loopback (agents/cli/client.py:56). An end-to-end test drives both terminal checks against the real app (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:550). Diagnostics stay local: the redacted bundle is served over one admin GET (agents/core/routers/support.py:21), and neither module imports a network client (tests/test_support_bundle.py:67), so the share_nous upload stays refused. The projects/workspaces model was skipped by decision. Known limits the row does not require: the verdict is for the route a short Jarvis chat takes; and a cloud route is judged by the router's own selection, not by a live call.

The local half is admin-guarded and working. `GET /api/models/local` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:103) lists LM Studio/Ollama models and marks the active one. `POST /api/models/local/switch` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:363) switches models, and `POST /api/llm/load` / `unload` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:472, agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:500) load and unload them. The HUD reaches all of this through `LMStudioPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2384). The cloud side is read-only. `GET /api/llm/auth-profiles` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:427) returns masked Anthropic/Gemini pool status, rendered by `AuthProfilesPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2597). HybridRouter builds those pools only from environment variables (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:327, via `AuthProfilePool.from_env` at agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). The shared command catalog the row depends on exists: `GET /api/commands` (agents/core/routers/commands.py:29) with name/description/tier/usage, and `GET /api/quickbar/help` (agents/core/routers/quickbar.py:59). Both are consumed by `QuickbarPanel` (frontend/src/panels/quickbar.tsx:98), which lists commands but does not complete a partial line. Path completion is conditional in the rationale on a terminal client shipping. `nerva` has only the one-shot `nerva chat` and no interactive composer, so path completion is not owed yet.
reviews.remaining: (1) No provider options: no route returns models grouped by provider (cloud and local) with cost hints, and cost_tracker's price table is not shown per model. (2) No save-key: no admin route writes a provider API key to the secret store and returns the refreshed model list. The pools read env vars only, so a key saved at runtime would never reach the router without a pool rebuild. (3) No disconnect: no route removes a provider's credential and rebuilds its pool, so there is no single place to revoke a provider. No audit event exists for either write. `/api/secrets/broker` (agents/core/routers/secrets.py:29, agents/core/routers/secrets.py:56) stores action-time `{{secret:NAME}}` values, not the router's provider keys. (4) No slash completion: neither the chat composer nor QuickbarPanel completes command names or their `usage` arguments from `/api/commands` as the user types.

reviews.summary: The voice primitives exist; per-surface mic arbitration does not. Host side: `WakeWordDetector` (agents/core/voice/wake_word.py:26) runs inside `VoicePipeline`, which `VoiceChannel.start` (agents/core/channels/voice.py:24) starts. That channel is registered at boot with wake words from `general.wake_words` (agents/web.py:479). Browser side: frontend/src/voice.ts captures through getUserMedia, VAD-segments one utterance, and has 'hands-free' and 'ptt' modes (frontend/src/voice.ts:73). TTS and STT are user-guarded routes: `POST /tts`, `POST /api/voice/stt` and `GET /api/voice/capabilities` (agents/core/routers/voice.py:42, agents/core/routers/voice.py:187, agents/core/routers/voice.py:286). Per-chat spoken replies (the `/voice` toggle) are covered by tests/test_voice_mode.py. `config.set` maps to the admin settings PUT, and `ping` maps to `GET /healthz` (agents/core/routers/ops.py:42).
reviews.remaining: The adaptation's one required concept is missing. No arm/pause/resume/stop/status call carries a surface identity. Nothing records which surface (HUD browser loop, mobile, satellite, host pipeline) holds the microphone, so the host pipeline and a browser hands-free loop on the same machine can both open the device. No status call answers who holds the mic. Arming does not pass the capture-consent policy the governance requires; the policy that exists (mobile/src/screens/capturePolicy.ts) covers passive capture only. Arming also writes no audit event, and the host pipeline starts at boot with neither check. The separate open item that no install path installs a voice engine is outside this row.

reviews.summary: Configurația, registrul și comenzile de inspecție au primit corecții.

reviews.summary: Only the unsafe form of reset exists. POST /api/admin/settings/reseed (agents/core/routers/admin.py:161-168) calls init_db(force=True). That runs DELETE FROM settings and re-seeds every category (agents/core/settings_db.py:432-436): global, immediate, admin-token only, with no preview, no approval and no undo. Since H153's second review it leaves one audit row (settings_reseed, agents/core/routers/admin.py:166), so it is no longer silent. tests/test_admin_settings_mutations.py checks that reseed returns ok and requires a token, and tests/test_h153b_webhook_delivery.py that it is audited. Per-category writes go through PUT /api/admin/settings/{category}, which validates with validate_category and audits the key names, with a choice's new value (agents/core/routers/admin.py:144). The HUD SettingsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2640) edits and saves categories through that route, but has no reset, defaults, export or import control. settings.db is deliberately left out of the owner data export (agents/core/data_export.py:39) and only travels inside the full data-root backup.
reviews.remaining: Nothing gives the UI the defaults: there is no GET /api/admin/settings/defaults or other accessor, so the HUD cannot mark keys that differ from their defaults. There is no per-category reset and no preview diff against defaults. Reset still wipes every category at once and does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier. There is no JSON export of the configuration. There is no import that stages values for review before Save (validated by validate_category, with secret values never exported in clear).

reviews.summary: The TTL-deletion half is in place. The retention settings are off by default, and a TTL of 0 means keep forever (agents/core/settings_db.py:370-371, plus audit, ingestion and artifact TTLs). run_retention (agents/core/retention.py:148) deletes session transcript files by last activity and prunes the audit chain through AuditLogger.prune_before, which re-anchors the Merkle chain (agents/core/security/audit.py:336). It also prunes Howard ingestion roots and unpinned binary artifacts. schedule_retention registers a daily 03:30 cron (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:181), and run_retention_purge (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:462) does nothing unless retention.enabled is set. tests/test_retention.py covers old-vs-new pruning, the TTL-0 no-op, chain verifiability after a prune and the default-off settings.
reviews.remaining: There is no reversible archive tier: purge_old_conversations unlinks files directly (agents/core/retention.py:76), with no soft-hide stage, no restore and no exemption for pinned sessions. Nothing runs VACUUM after a prune: prune_before issues DELETE FROM security_events (agents/core/security/audit.py:367) and commits, so the audit database file never shrinks. There is no vacuum_after_prune or min_vacuum_interval setting; the only VACUUM is on the forget path (agents/core/data_purge.py:243). There is no persisted last-run marker and no min-interval gate shared across processes; the sweep is a fixed daily cron in each scheduler process. Changes to retention TTLs or the enabled flag are ordinary admin PUT /api/admin/settings/retention writes. The governance field requires them to go through the irreversible approval tier instead.

reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code, and this re-read retires three claims the row had carried since before H502 (#1174 moved the hash while the text stood still) plus one the text was about to inherit. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:161-173) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. None of it touches a name policy, a writer or the override path, so it moves nothing for this row. The fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) is likewise off-subject: it added tool_patterns_over_bounds (agents/core/mcp/client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ (:407-418) and a bounds refusal for tools_allow/tools_deny in admin_mcp_add (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:167-173); none of it reads or writes an env name, and MCPServerConfig still has no env field, so only line numbers moved (client.py +19 from the new helper on and +31 from that __init__ block on; routers/mcp.py +4 from the filter check on). Inbound (what a surface may persist) does not exist as a policy at all: no ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env symbol anywhere in agents/, scripts/, tests/ or frontend/src/, and no `config.write` kind in agents/core/capability_actions.py. A correction the row must carry, because it shapes the deliverable: Hermes' hijack names are NOT all absent from the code. LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER appear nowhere outside the research docs, but PATH and SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are MEMBERS of the two outbound allowlists — deliberately, because a child needs them as plumbing — and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 pinning that collect_tokens keeps only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. So the two allowlists the rationale points at as the pattern to reuse admit precisely the names Hermes forbids on write; the inbound registry has to be its own list, and "run overrides through the same name policy" is not by itself a fix, since that policy passes PATH/NODE_PATH/PYTHONPATH untouched. Confirmed there is still no env writer to gate: no os.environ assignment in agents/ except the reality harness's JARVIS_STRICT_EGRESS toggle (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:685,714; scripts/qa_audit_probes.py and scripts/install_smoke.py set os.environ only as probe/smoke harnesses); no set_key/dotenv write; agents/core/paths.py:130-134 only copies .env.example verbatim; GET /api/admin/env (agents/core/routers/admin.py:205-217) is read-only and mask-redacted, and its one sibling, GET /api/admin/env/sources (H273), is read-only and returns key names and layers only, so neither writes the environment; the HUD states it in its own copy (frontend/src/panels/workflows-advanced.tsx:48 "There is NO route to change either"). Nerva's actual config writer is settings_db.put_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:718-753), which UPSERTs only DEFAULTS-declared keys and skips the rest (agents/core/settings_db.py:734-744), behind validate_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:696-715) and the 422 at agents/core/routers/admin.py:145-151 — the right shape, but over settings keys, not env names. Three things are nevertheless still owed, so this is not equivalence. (1) The row's own deliverable — a declared-names allowlist at the write boundary, depends_on "the key registry" — is unbuilt, and the rationale defers rather than excludes it ("the moment the config writer lands, this must land with it"). (2) The MCP env boundary is unrefused: MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:128-139) has no env field and sets no model_config, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" SILENTLY DROPS an `env` body key rather than refusing it — reproduced at HEAD both on the model (model_config {} and env absent from model_dump) and end to end through TestClient: POST /api/admin/mcp with {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}} → 200 {"ok": true}, the stored MCPServer.env is {} and to_config() carries no env — and POST builds the MCPServer without one (:177-189). The non-round-trip half IS now pinned — test_per_server_env_has_no_owner_reachable_config_surface (tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522, from #1174) asserts "env" not in MCPServerConfig.model_fields, to_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:798-812) exports no env and load_from_config (:814-849) ignores one — but no test asserts the route REFUSES an env body, and the field it would fill is live: MCPServer.env (:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Reachability today: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449; no add form, nothing sends env) and no CLI or script adds servers, so the raw API is the only path. (3) Per-server overrides still bypass the allowlist in both branches: stdio_env_baseline applies them unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring agents/core/mcp/client.py:253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch — reachable only under JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 since H502 — does merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env) unfiltered (:575-576). Latent, not live: the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names set on the host (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56), and the admin route cannot pass one. Also checked and cleared: scripts/nerva_import.py IS a setup-flow writer that persists foreign env-var names verbatim (docstring scripts/nerva_import.py:31-32, .env lines scripts/nerva_import.py:357-358, JSON walk scripts/nerva_import.py:371, settings.json env block scripts/nerva_import.py:389-393, SecretStore write scripts/nerva_import.py:1022), but _SECRET_NAME_RE (scripts/nerva_import.py:85) is applied on every path and admits only credential-shaped names — tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 is the one existing test that exercises a hijack-shaped name (EDITOR) at an import boundary and pins it dropped — and SecretStore (agents/core/secrets.py) never exports a name to a process env (it reads only JARVIS_SECRET_KEY, :111). HEQ lot 1 moved two cited files without touching this row's subject: settings_db.py gained the H583 openrouter_* llm rows and a slug check inside _validate_value (settings keys, not env names; put_category and validate_category are unchanged), and scripts/nerva_import.py gained H344's skill.install mediation and --update re-import for skills, while its token path (the .env/JSON/settings.json readers and _SECRET_NAME_RE) is unchanged. Tests re-run on the lot-1 head: 55 passed, 0 failed across the four cited files (test_environment_primitives 6, test_mcp_transports 33 — two of them #1179's, test_mcp_admin 8, test_settings_integrity 8), and tests/test_nerva_import.py 44 passed, 1 skipped; none exercises an env-var write boundary.
reviews.remaining:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No ENV_VAR_NAME allowlist/denylist exists anywhere (grep for ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env across agents/, scripts/, tests/, frontend/src/ is empty at HEAD) and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. Of Hermes' hijack names, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER are named nowhere in code or tests — but PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) ARE named, as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:139-143 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :151-152.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:128-139) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: `env` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:798-812) does not export it and load_from_config (:814-849) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an `env` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day `env` becomes operator-settable.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:575-576). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:179-190; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:177-189), and the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56). No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after three adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:353) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:460) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:433) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:
- serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:224). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard.
- The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:415). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:80), and so does agents/run.py before its orchestrator.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:448) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded, with the note, and kept out of the environment.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:84): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:
- A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there.
- A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:663).

The two false read-again entries are fixed:
- The MCP transport reads the user token the way the guard does (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:355), so a token from .env guards it on this machine and lets a remote client in.
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:33), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:190): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:131) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:315) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:282). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

Surfaces:
- GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:220) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included.
- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:582):
  - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:312). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost. and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:286). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:328). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why.
  - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:450).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:688). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:468); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.
  - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why.
  - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash.
- The `nerva` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:93) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only.
- The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:490). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown or unreadable stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection. `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:667).
- The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:256).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.

Tests:
- tests/test_env_provenance.py (61 cases): parity and fuzz (tests/test_env_provenance.py:130), the named pipe, the plugin manager's order and the posture overlay.
- tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py (8): a real redirect and a real proxy, pinning where the credential goes (tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py:93).
- tests/test_h273c_provenance_review.py (56): the import, the names withheld, the bound-mapping scan and the second round's nits.
- tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py (74 cases, the third round):
  - the start measured and the lists by where they are used (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:116);
  - knobs the start reads, in effect from a .env (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:155);
  - the bind guard through serve.py and the lifespan, the redaction floor, one load per process, the refused roots;
  - the MCP transport, the OAuth routes, and the doctor's and CLI's transport rules;
  - hub mode, the names withheld, the widened scan, the reviewer's survivors and the nits.
- tests/test_doctor.py keeps the JSON contract, and frontend/src/test/env-sources.test.ts the HUD mapping and its note.

Mutation:
- The first round's 41 mutants and the second's 29 were each caught, as were the second review's twelve survivors.
- The third review's own 67 independent mutants left 16 survivors, four of them equivalent. Each of the other twelve now has a test: the lists' classification, a mixed-case name, a missing value, the data home's values, the cache key, a commented declaration, a 403, a posture that is not JSON, a third load, and the same-file order. Re-run against the new tests, all twelve are caught.
- This round's 46 mutants (44 Python, 2 HUD) were each run against their own suites: 45 are caught. The survivor drops the IPv4-mapped check in the loopback test. It is equivalent on the test interpreter, whose patched ipaddress already counts ::ffff:127.0.0.1 as loopback, and the check stays for the 3.12 releases before that fix.

No safe mode exists. Grepping for SAFE_MODE, safe_mode, known-good or DISABLE_(PLUGINS|MCP|SKILLS) across agents/, scripts/ and frontend/src finds no boot switch (the one hit is the unrelated D3FEND "Restore" entry, "Return to a known-good state.", in the security-skills catalogue agents/core/security_skills/pack.py), and serve.py/agents/run.py take no such flag. Every customization loads unconditionally at boot:
- PluginManager.build constructs every plugin (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:64).
- The web lifespan loads the persisted MCP servers through _load_mcp_config (agents/web.py:465).
- Orchestrator.load_agents calls self.skills.discover() (agents/core/orchestrator.py:971). SkillLoader.discover appends the data-home skills folder after the bundled tree (agents/core/skills/loader.py:568).
- Agent._load_soul (agents/core/agent.py:501) reads whichever SOUL.local.md overlay soul_path_for selects (agents/core/agent.py:374: data-home overlay, then repo-local SOUL.local.md, then the shipped SOUL.md). Since H672 the same overlay is also re-read mid-session: Agent.refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:513) is called for every agent by _refresh_souls_at_boundary (agents/core/orchestrator.py:326) at each compaction commit (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3473), with no safe-mode bypass either.
scripts/doctor.py can diagnose a broken install (HEQ lot 1 added a read-only runtime_resolves check of the configured model route) but cannot boot it with these layers disabled.
reviews.remaining:
The whole feature is missing. It needs:
1. A single boot flag (e.g. JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1 plus a serve.py/`nerva` switch that sets it) that skips data-home and generated skills (bundled tree only), skips persisted MCP servers without erasing their saved config, skips owner-activated plugins/extensions, and ignores SOUL.local.md/HEARTBEAT.local.md overlays in favour of the shipped templates, both at construction and at the H672 compaction-boundary refresh (refresh_soul), so a safe-mode session cannot pick an overlay back up mid-conversation.
2. A visible indicator that safe mode is on (status/readyz field and a HUD banner).
3. A fail-closed guarantee that safe mode only removes capability: no kernel mediation, approval floor, plugin gate or egress policy relaxes.
4. Tests for each skipped layer and for the no-relaxation property.

reviews.summary:
Nerva has two role-specific model settings, each implemented ad hoc:
- The vision role: resolve_vlm_config in agents/core/llm/vlm.py reads JARVIS_VLM_BACKEND (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:215), JARVIS_VLM_MODEL/URL and JARVIS_VLM_PRESET (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:219). The multimodal router and screen_locator consume it.
- The deep slot: deep_model_name (agents/core/llm/model_config.py:24) reads JARVIS_DEEP_MODEL.
Provider metadata is declared in ProviderProfile (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:28), but no role is bound to a provider profile through it. The action approval queue (ActionApprovalQueue.request/decide in agents/core/autonomy/action_approvals.py) has no model scoring step; items are decided by the human only. There is no video role. Tests tests/test_vlm_h13_1.py and tests/test_llm_provider_profiles.py pass.
reviews.remaining:
1. There is no declared role table (role -> provider profile + model + base URL/key env) that vision, deep and new roles resolve through.
2. There is no approval-judge role: nothing scores a queued ActionApprovalQueue item before the HUD card is shown. The governance also requires that the judge's provider/model identity be written into the item and into the audit entry of the action it scored, and that the judge only annotates, never approves on its own.
3. There is no video role.
4. There are no tests that the judge identity is recorded or that an unconfigured judge leaves the queue unchanged.

reviews.summary: Host detection exists and is richer than Hermes' env sniffing. probe_host (agents/core/host_probe.py:406) turns Accessibility/screen-capture grants, the Wayland portal version, AT-SPI availability and elevated windows into named refusal reasons. detect_hardware (agents/core/hardware.py:215) profiles GPU and RAM. Supervisors get /healthz (agents/core/routers/ops.py:42) and /readyz (agents/core/routers/ops.py:137). The model is told only the live LLM backend and model, through _runtime_state_block (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2467). Neither gap the rationale accepted is closed. Nothing in agents/ reads NOTIFY_SOCKET or sends READY=1/WATCHDOG=1; the shipped unit is Type=simple (deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service:22), and deploy/systemd/README.md:69 says the hub does not emit sd_notify. There is no operator environment-hint variable or prompt block. Tests tests/test_host_probe.py and tests/test_h2311_operability.py pass.
reviews.remaining:
1. sd_notify: when NOTIFY_SOCKET is set, send READY=1 once readiness (the /readyz condition) is reached, send WATCHDOG=1 at half of WATCHDOG_USEC from an event-loop task that stops if the loop hangs, and send STOPPING=1 on shutdown. Ship the unit as Type=notify with WatchdogSec and correct the README note.
2. Environment hint: an operator-authored JARVIS_ENVIRONMENT_HINT, sanitized and length-capped, injected as a fixed block in the system prompt's stable cached prefix, separate from the SOUL persona and labelled as a machine description rather than instructions.
3. Tests covering the socket messages, the cap, the placement and byte-stability across turns.

reviews.summary: Configurația, registrul și comenzile de inspecție au primit corecții.
reviews.remaining: Trebuie închise cerințele complete de acces offline, proveniență, limbă și ceas, nu doar reparate cheile moarte.

reviews.summary:
The install side is well governed: skill.install is kernel-mediated (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:106), with the signing/review gates plus marketplace uninstall and rollback. Narrowing what loads exists only piecemeal and does not survive a restart:
- PUT /plugins/{plugin_id}/toggle (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) flips the in-memory PluginManifest.enabled through PermissionGate.disable (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:723) and is lost on restart.
- MCP servers can be disconnected (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:243) or deleted from the persisted list, but MCPManager.load_from_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:814) loads every persisted server.
- Skills cannot be disabled at all: SkillLoader.discover (agents/core/skills/loader.py:557) loads every directory in the bundled tree and in the data-home skills folder.
There is no declared startup load-set for skills, plugins or MCP servers. Tests tests/test_systems_api.py::test_plugin_toggle_endpoint, tests/test_mcp_admin.py and tests/test_cdx8_skill_quarantine.py pass.
reviews.remaining:
1. A declared, persisted load-set (allow/deny lists in settings or env) naming which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at boot. It must be honoured by SkillLoader.discover, PluginManager.build/PermissionGate and _load_mcp_config, and surfaced in the skills/MCP/plugin status rows.
2. Plugin toggles must survive a restart.
3. Narrowing-only semantics: a name that is not installed or approved is ignored and reported, never installed, never written to the approval store, and never a way around skill.install or the admin MCP add route.
4. Tests for each of these.
Safe mode (H275), which this row depends on, is also missing.

reviews.summary: Provenienta pe tura exista in ContextVar si nu intra niciodata in mediul procesului; K0 a inchis calea sandbox, K1 duce actorul efectiv pana in handler, iar K2 releaga identitatea la fiecare celula — un apelabil capturat intr-o celula anterioara nu poarta mai departe permisiunea ei.

reviews.summary:
Both ideas the row said were "worth taking and cheap" are shipped, proven and correct, and the audit's 2026-09-07 nerva_evidence did undersell Nerva. The row is still not equivalent, because the cron half of Hermes' contract has three clauses that are still unmet.

Shipped and verified at 55d625f. The claim lease with a TTL is `autonomy.running_ttl_seconds` (agents/core/settings_db.py:334, default 3600). The coordinator resyncs it on every tick (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:278-283), and `TaskQueue.reap_stuck_running` enforces it (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:1599-1629) through `AutonomyWorker._reap_stuck` (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:489-503), which `tick` calls first (worker.py:889-891). The crash-grace window is the same mechanism, and it meets the row's governance note exactly: the reaper FAILS the stranded row with `result.error="stuck_running_ttl"` + `stuck_since` and audits `autonomy.reaped`. It never re-queues, so an action that was already authorized is never re-executed. Proven by tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py:91-135 and manual case GOV-224 (docs/test-manual/07-autonomy-governance.md:634). The jobs lane has the same property on its own path: when a manual request is found `running` and its cross-process gate is free, it is recorded as `unknown` / "execution interrupted after claim; not replayed" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:203-209), proven by tests/test_job_dispatch.py:130. Beyond the reaper, the scheduled lane has these guards: a 64-stripe cross-process file gate that every firing must hold (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59 via jobs.py:1325-1333); an identity fingerprint that voids a claim if the job was edited after acceptance (jobs_dispatch.py:15-18, 179-184; jobs.py:1343-1347); APScheduler `max_instances=1`; a workdir allowlist (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_workdir.py); estop/kill-switch seams (jobs.py:1353-1357, worker.py:893-904); and a validated media deadline, `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds` (settings_db.py:260, validated at :664; jobs_media.py:18/257).

Correction to the triage on the claim CAS: `claim_mediated` (queue.py:1240-1311) returns None unless `mediation_mode == "enforce"` (queue.py:1243). `resolve_task_mediation_mode()` returns "off" when `JARVIS_TASK_MEDIATION` is unset (agents/core/autonomy/mediation_head_store.py:195-211, docstring: "shipped-dark default"). In that default posture the worker claims with a bare `transition(task.id, RUNNING)` (worker.py:925-927). `transition` (queue.py:1459-1497) checks only the status edge and does no compare-and-swap on `mediation_execution_id`. So the triage's "a second claimant cannot win" holds only when mediation is enforced.

What is still owed, and why this is partial. Hermes' text names seven CRON_* clauses. (a) The plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. `_fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (jobs.py:1335-1391, 1437-1458, 1460-1499, 1570-1596) contains no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level. The script path already uses that pattern, at jobs_scripts.py:405 (120 s) and :455 (30 s). (b) `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (executor.py:39-42, autonomy_coordinator.py:1139-1142). Out of the box, the only bound on a hung in-process task is the 3600 s reaper. (c) The jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (jobs.py:652-655), while the task queue sets both to 30 s (queue.py:212-214). The row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs, so they do not count against it (they are also covered by per-job `channel`/`deliver` plus `AUTONOMY_OWNER_CHAT_ID` / `autonomy.owner_chat_id`, jobs.py:1570-1625). The ~14-knob Kanban board is still a product decision, not a slice of this row.

Re-run at 55d625f: the five cited test files (tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py, test_job_dispatch.py, test_jobs_media.py, test_executor_budget.py, test_autonomy_worker.py; 95 cases) pass, with zero failures.
reviews.remaining:
Three cron-lane clauses of Hermes' contract are unmet. The Kanban claim-lease and crash-grace asks are done.

1. HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT: the plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. `JobRunner._fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1335-1391, 1437-1458, 1460-1499, 1570-1596) has no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level. In particular, `_send_tracked`/`_send` (jobs.py:1598-1631) awaits the channel adapter bare. A hung Telegram/Discord send therefore holds the job's gate stripe (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59) and its APScheduler `max_instances=1` slot, and nothing breaks it. The script path already does this correctly: `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._ask(...), 120)` at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:405 and `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._send_tracked(...), 30)` at :455. The fix is to apply the same bound to the cron path, ideally as a `jobs.run_timeout_seconds` setting next to the existing `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds`. The overrun should be recorded as a normal failed run through `_failed`, so the 3-strike pause and the incident path still apply.

2. `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:39-42, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1139-1142). Out of the box, a hung in-process queued task is bounded only by the 3600 s stuck-running reaper. Fix: give it a non-zero shipped default, or promote it to a validated `autonomy.*` setting like `running_ttl_seconds`, and add a test asserting the default is finite.

3. HERMES_CRON_SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT: the jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:652-655). The task queue sets `timeout=30.0` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:212-214). jobs.db writers therefore fall back to SQLite's 5 s default, on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings. One-line parity fix.

Out of scope, not gaps: the row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs (_AUTO_DELIVER_PLATFORM / _CHAT_ID / _THREAD_ID, TELEGRAM_CRON_THREAD_ID). The residual ~14-knob multi-agent Kanban board (_BOARD / _WORKSPACES_ROOT / _ATTACHMENTS_ROOT / _GOAL_MODE / _DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY) is a product decision about whether Nerva grows a shared task board, not a slice of this row.

reviews.summary: Profilurile restrang oferta pe agent, principal si tip de suprafata; disponibilitatea backendului nu retrage inca o unealta din oferta turei.
reviews.remaining: Un profil nu probeaza backendul: execute_code, de exemplu, se inregistreaza pe un comutator al owner-ului si refuza la apel cu sandbox_not_isolated cand gazda nu are Docker/WASM, in loc sa dispara din oferta turei. Lipsesc check_fn per-unealta, cache-ul de ~30 s si fereastra last-known-good.

reviews.summary: Tool schemas are static. ToolRPCServer.register_tool (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:166) deep-copies the caller's input_schema once, at registration (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:243). ToolRPCServer.tools() (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:283) returns deep copies of that stored schema (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:290). AgentRuntime builds each turn's ToolSpec list from that output (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:469, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:500) through _specs_for, which copies input_schema verbatim (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:279-282). In registry mode, _registry_metadata (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1068) substitutes the capability record's inputs (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1114), and build_records copies those from the same static tool schema (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:334). The H672 compaction-boundary refresh does not change this. _resolve_offer (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:292) re-reads the same static tools() (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:302), and the specs are rebuilt only when a tool was added or removed or the refresh failed closed (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:546, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:575). So it tracks which tools are offered, not what their schemas advertise. There is no per-tool override hook, no merge over the static schema and no exception fallback. For example, terminal_run advertises target as a free string (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:610) rather than the targets actually registered, and desktop_run's step action is likewise a free string (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:529). The gated speak tool that HEQ lot 1 added (registered only with JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR on) follows the same pattern: a fixed INPUT_SCHEMA whose target is a free string naming a device id, a room or presence:auto, not the rooms and speakers the Media Director actually has. tests/test_tool_rpc_h20_1.py and tests/test_agent_runtime_v2.py exercise only static schemas.
reviews.remaining: Two pieces are missing. (1) A dynamic schema-override hook on tool registration, merged over the static schema on every tools()/ToolSpec build, logging and falling back to the static schema when the hook raises, and applied in both the ToolRPC path and the registry projection. That includes the H672 compaction-boundary rebuild, which today rebuilds specs only when the set of tool names changes. (2) Real overrides on the flag- and hardware-conditional tools the rationale names (terminal_run targets, desktop_run supported actions), and on speak's target (the rooms and speakers actually configured), so that the advertised schema matches the live install.

reviews.summary:
The complete frozen tool-result contract is wired into real tool turns:
