- the threshold precedence: pinned infinity (PINNED_THRESHOLDS: file_read, keyed on READ_TOOL, and since H315's review `todo`, whose store keeps its whole answer under 7,000 bytes), then owner override, the MCP family, tool declaration and the default threshold;
- per-result/per-turn scaling;
- bounded previews with full-file paths, sizes and hashes;
- finalized-file retention;
- centralized byte/line/line-length limits.

Since H661 the spill notice is an exact, followable call. `page_recipe` fills in `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)` with the resolved path, the preview and execute_code stream fields carry it as text and as `read_with` arguments, and `file_read` pages from any offset and returns `next_offset`. The call is checked, not assumed: the store's `read_back` probe is asked about that exact path. The coordinator wires it to three checks: registry + job-toolset allowance, the turn's own offer, and FileTools reach. The spill directory is also a read-only door for exact spill names, and spill names never look like secrets. When file_read cannot page the file from this turn, the notice says the file is kept for the owner and does not name a dead call.

Other guarantees:
- Exclusive per-writer temporary files preserve concurrent stream and whole-result receipts.
- A shape-truncated stream keeps its bytes even when its annotation makes the preview longer.
- Upstream byte truncation and small-output discard still work.

Ordinary Agent and Orchestrator tool paths snapshot configured/cached backend capacity before guardrails. They forward immutable per-turn metadata without unwrapping or bypassing generation. Known capacity and resolved job bounds constrain the completion reserve, initial and later transcripts, schemas, structured tool arguments and finite result thresholds, and file_read never re-spills. Invalid metadata refuses the tool turn. Unknown capacity, including adapters without loaded metadata, keeps the documented model-family estimate, and token accounting remains heuristic.

Re-run at 55d625f: 243 cases pass across tests/test_tool_result_store.py, test_tool_loop_result_spill.py, test_environment_output_limits.py, test_code_tools.py, test_effective_tool_window.py and test_spill_paging.py.

Honest limits:
- A *streamed* spill now has a ceiling, DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES = 5,000,000, which the code calls Hermes' own figure. Past it, the file ends in one explicit '[... spill capped ...]' marker, the result reports capped/kept_bytes/file_bytes, and the stream's end survives only in the inline tail. Whole-result spills are uncapped.
- Retention has a newest-file exception.
- Interrupted captures, orphan cleanup and arbitrary storage failure are not permanent complete-output guarantees.
- This is code equivalence, not live provider/Windows containment proof.
Runtime-ul oprește apelurile identice și seriile de eșecuri, aplică limite per unealtă și înlocuiește rezultatele identice reușite cu referințe.

Oferta este calculată din principal, origine/suprafață și restricțiile agentului; seturile sunt verificate prin snapshot. Catalogul Hermes de platforme excluse nu este copiat. Din H672, aceeași rezoluție (`_profiled`, prin `_resolve_offer`) se reaplică și la granița de compactare din tură, cu eșec închis: un profil care nu poate răspunde retrage toate uneltele în loc să păstreze o ofertă posibil revocată.

file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. It can also open an exact spill-file path through a read-only door when the owner's roots exclude the spill directory, and tool_result_store pins file_read to an infinite spill threshold, so reading a spill never spills again. file_search is a bounded literal content search with case_sensitive, whole_word and a file-name glob filter; it never follows symlinks, prunes secret names and reports which cap stopped it.
reviews.remaining: Paging is by bytes, not lines: file_read output is not line-numbered, there is no 1-indexed line offset/limit window, and there is no per-line length cap, so one long line can fill a page. file_search matches a literal phrase, not a regex, with a Python line scan rather than ripgrep. There is no glob file-finding mode: the glob only narrows which files' contents are searched, a pattern is required, and file_list lists a single directory. Document extraction covers .pdf and .docx only.

reviews.summary: K1, K2 și K3 sunt livrate: execute_code înregistrat pentru model, celule într-un interpreter rezident pe sesiune (K2, `llm.execute_code_sessions`, implicit oprit) și controale de operator peste el. Spill-ul stdout/stderr într-un fișier funcționează pe ambele căi. `_open_stream_spills` (agents/core/code_tools.py:480) deschide scriitorii în flux înainte de rulare. Pe K1, sinks trec prin `ToolRPCSandboxRuntime.run_python` (code_tools.py:449) până la `Sandbox.execute_python`. Pe K2, worker-ul trimite ieșirea celulei în cadre de cel mult 4096 de caractere (agents/core/session_kernels.py:208), iar `_Capture` dă fiecare cadru scriitorului (session_kernels.py:521). Gazda vede deci tot fluxul, iar memoria ei rămâne mărginită: păstrează doar capul și coada. Un flux care a încăput nu lasă fișier; rezultatul unui spill poartă calea, referința, dimensiunea și sha256. Lotul HEQ 1 (H661) a făcut din notiță apelul exact. `_spill_notice` (code_tools.py:191) scrie `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)`, construit de `page_recipe` (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145), și cere paginarea prin next_offset. `stdout_read_with` (code_tools.py:272) apare doar când turei i s-a oferit file_read și sonda `_spill_readable` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:800) confirmă că poate deschide acel fișier; altfel notița spune că fișierul e păstrat pentru owner și nu poate fi paginat din tura asta. file_read primește directorul de spill ca ușă read-only (autonomy_coordinator.py:796). Un spill în flux are acum un plafon: DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES, 5 MB (tool_result_store.py:130, cifra lui Hermes). Peste el fișierul ține primii 5 MB și se termină într-un marcaj explicit (coada fluxului rămâne doar inline), iar rezultatul poartă `stdout_spill_capped`, `stdout_kept_bytes` și `stdout_file_bytes` (code_tools.py:274). tests/test_code_tools.py paginează înapoi tot fluxul pe ambele căi (tests/test_code_tools.py:824) și verifică plafonul (tests/test_code_tools.py:877).
reviews.remaining: Rămân kernelul remote și proba pe un daemon Docker real. Modul `project|strict` al lui Hermes rămâne necopiat deliberat: postura o decide profilul de unelte (agent × suprafață × principal).

reviews.summary: The pointing feature itself is absent; only the Agent Canvas substrate it was meant to build on exists. CanvasStore.post validates and sanitises typed elements through _sanitize in agents/core/canvas.py. ALLOWED_TYPES (agents/core/canvas.py:113) is text, markdown, list, link, metric, table and image_ref, and any other type raises (agents/core/canvas.py:110). POST /api/canvas/post (agents/core/routers/canvas.py:42) is the only producer. The HUD reads GET /api/canvas in frontend/src/artifacts.tsx:223 and in frontend/src/panels/mission-canvas.tsx. There is no pointer, tip or tour element type. The HUD has no element-anchor registry and no overlay that draws an arrow bubble at a panel element. No model-callable tool posts such an element: no ToolRPC registration references the canvas at all. tests/test_h12_18_canvas.py passes and covers only the existing element types and their sanitisation.
reviews.remaining: Three pieces are missing: (1) canvas element types for a tip (target anchor plus a one-line caption) and a tour (a bounded ordered step list paged with Next/Prev), sanitised by canvas.py; (2) an ungated tool the model is actually offered that posts them through CanvasStore; (3) a HUD overlay that resolves the target to an on-screen element, draws the pointer and caption, and pages tour steps.

reviews.summary: Modelul poate căuta și extrage pagini prin egressul existent, cu rezultate limitate și marcate ca date.
reviews.remaining: Rămân cerințe de extracție/paginare/cache/configurare din rândurile complete; x_search exclus nu este reinclus.

reviews.summary: Generare locala din prompt si editare (image-to-image) prin ComfyUI, cu aceeasi aprobare exacta; imaginea de referinta se rezolva doar printr-un ID opac de artefact. Reevaluat 2026-09-19: alegerea backend-ului există pe cerere (`backend` — ComfyUI local implicit sau `openai`, `media_backends/openai_image.py`, în spatele aceleiași aprobări), upscale 2× (singura valoare acceptată de `comfyui.py`) și până la 4 imagini de referință ca ID-uri opace de artefact, validate înainte de dispatch.
reviews.remaining: Video lipsește în întregime. Upscale doar 2×, fără alt factor. Editarea și generarea nu sunt probate pe un ComfyUI sau un endpoint OpenAI real; ruta cloud trimite promptul owner-ului în afara cutiei și stă corect în spatele aprobării, dar nu are probă live.

reviews.summary: The model can decide to say one short text aloud on one room's device, and can do it again. register_speak_tool (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:603) adds a ToolRPC `speak` tool with gated=True, trusted execution and its own gated intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:630, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:636). It is registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:616), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it with the broker kernel and the governed enqueue (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:462, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1318). It reaches the same Media Director instance the media routes use, so the owner's device registry and session board apply (agents/core/routers/media_director.py:272). SpeakTool.preflight (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:307) runs at proposal and again before the approved run. It refuses text over the spoken-reply cap and code-only text (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:313, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:315). It resolves a room to that room's one announce-capable default device, so the card title and the persisted args name the speaker (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:235, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:386). It raises no card the run could only refuse: unified API off, kernel off or unbound, no media root, no speech backend, no driver for the device, or no configured presence room each refuse by name (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:334, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:329). SpeakTool.intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:364) shows the kernel the exact toolrpc.speak row it enqueues. Under the production composition (worker.kernel_gate over MediationKernelBridge, agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:220, agents/core/kernel/binding.py:108) that decision binds as the row's intake evidence, and a DENY raises no card (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:390). Only the human-accepted durable toolrpc.speak row runs. The kind is trusted (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:66) and the executor routes it to the trusted rail (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1339-1342). ToolRPC re-runs the preflight and requires the trusted execution context (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:460, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:488), and the handler refuses a row of any other kind (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:460). SpeakTool.execute (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:455) synthesizes the clip through SpokenReply on the host TTSEngine in the owner's configured voice (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:471, agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:242, agents/core/voice/tts.py:144). It writes the clip owner-only under the first media root (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:558, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:572) and presents it only through CapabilityActionAPI.perform('action:media.present') in announce mode (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:511, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:516). The facade asks the Action Kernel before the handler runs (agents/core/capability_actions.py:168) and refuses on a DENY (agents/core/capability_actions.py:175), so the kernel authorizes the effect and the tool never reaches a driver. A kernel QUEUE on that present is honoured as the accepted row and audited as speak.durably_approved (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:419, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:441). A DENY becomes kernel_denied with the kernel's reason (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:533). The Media Director treats an announce as a one-shot notice (agents/core/media_director.py:738): it never blocks the next present and costs no interrupt budget (agents/core/media_director.py:890), and whatever it cut into stays the restore point (agents/core/media_director.py:992). Because the tool is gated, tool_profiles offers it only to the owner on the operator surface (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:184, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:188), and the snapshot pins this (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json:40, tests/test_tool_profiles.py:202). Tests cover: registration and postures (tests/test_speak_tool.py:170, tests/test_speak_tool.py:196); named preflight refusals that enqueue nothing (tests/test_speak_tool.py:271, tests/test_speak_tool.py:320); and the card naming the device (tests/test_speak_tool.py:286). With the real kernel.authorize, AutonomyPolicy and KillSwitch behind worker.kernel_gate, an approved speak is mediated and audited, and an engaged kill switch refuses both the run and the card (tests/test_speak_tool.py:520, tests/test_speak_tool.py:543, tests/test_speak_tool.py:576). Three back-to-back normal speaks on one device all play at no budget cost (tests/test_speak_tool.py:591). Speaking over music needs high urgency, pays once and keeps the music as the restore point (tests/test_speak_tool.py:608, tests/test_media_director.py:762). A kernel DENY, a missing TTS backend, a missing media root and a driverless device each refuse by name with no playback, and an engine that yields no audio refuses as tts_failed with nothing presented (tests/test_speak_tool.py:681, tests/test_speak_tool.py:469, tests/test_speak_tool.py:666, tests/test_speak_tool.py:703, tests/test_speak_tool.py:716). A row of another kind cannot speak (tests/test_speak_tool.py:753), and the clip spool stays bounded (tests/test_speak_tool.py:779). Known limits outside the accepted adaptation: an accepted speak runs at the next autonomy tick (default 60 s, floor 15 s, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:253), like every gated tool. A presence:auto card names the sentinel, because only play time knows whether the owner is in the presence room. Audible output needs an owner-wired speaker driver (the in-repo NullMediaDriver refuses and LocalFileMediaDriver is a reference), the same host seam as every media.present. The speech-backend gate needs edge-tts or Kokoro installed, like the spoken-reply channel. An announce of any length, including one sent through POST /api/media/present, no longer holds its device, as docs/FLAGS.md states. Hermes's tts.provider, custom command providers and tts.speed are outside the accepted adaptation, because Nerva's TTS subsystem was already ahead.

The read half has shipped. register_search_memory (agents/core/memory/rag_tool.py:446) registers `search_memory` ungated (agents/core/memory/rag_tool.py:489), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it over orch.memory.recall (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:827). It appears in the resolved owner, inbound-owner and internal tool profiles (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json). Every hit is injection-scanned, flagged hits are redacted, and `tainted` raises the turn's recall taint. Hermes's two injected stores exist as the LivingMemory `core` (agent facts) and `user_core` (user profile) rings in agents/core/cognition/memory.py. render_core_block (agents/core/learning/core_block.py:54) renders them into every prompt, and Orchestrator._living_core_memory_block freezes them per session. The model decides writes only indirectly: the post-turn BackgroundReviewer (wired at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1007, off by default via cognition.review_enabled) makes one structured local LLM call. Code then writes up to learning.review_max_facts facts per store through _put_facts (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:261) after an injection scan. The only memory-write tool is the MCP-server route tool `memory_remember` (agents/core/mcp/route_tools.py:534), which is offered to external MCP clients and not to Nerva's own tool loop.
reviews.remaining: The model is offered no memory-write tool during a turn. The ToolRPC registry holds search_memory and session_search, but nothing that adds or removes a core or user-profile fact or stores a vector note. The accepted adaptation requires a model-initiated write that is reversible-tier and visible. That means an operations array applied atomically to the stores that are actually enabled (the target enum narrowed to those stores), injection-scanned text, an audit-chain record for each write carrying what is needed to undo it, and any graph write crossing the kernel-mediated `kg.write`. BackgroundReviewer._put_facts calls CoreMemory.put with no audit record and is off by default, so it does not meet this.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after three adversarial reviews. The model keeps a checklist of its own work and re-reads all of it on every change. The owner can read the same list, with who wrote each item and whether its text is trusted, before any approval card it leads to.

The tool. agents/core/todo_tool.py registers `todo` on the ToolRPC server, ungated (agents/core/todo_tool.py:564), with the schema {todos: [{id, content, status, parent?}], merge} (agents/core/todo_tool.py:90); the optional parent is H666's.
- Items use Hermes' four statuses: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled. A call with todos replaces the list. With merge=true it updates items by id, changing only the fields sent, and appends new ones. A call without todos reads the list. Every call answers with the whole list and its counts.
- TodoStore.apply (agents/core/todo_tool.py:295) is bounded: at most 50 items, content of one printable line up to 200 characters, ids of 1 to 64 characters, 7,000 bytes for the whole list in the UTF-8 the tool sends it in, and at most one item in progress. A merge that only moves statuses is never refused as too long.
- Control and format characters are dropped, text is NFC, each character keeps at most three combining marks (enclosing marks included), and whitespace runs collapse. Text that renders blank (only fillers or marks) is no content; punctuation or a symbol alone is content (agents/core/todo_tool.py:136). So what the owner reads is what was written. Two ids that are canonically equal are one id; look-alikes from another script or width stay two.
- Every refusal is named, and each comes with a sentence the model can act on: todo_too_many, todo_content_too_long, todo_content_required, todo_bad_status, todo_bad_id, todo_duplicate_id, todo_one_in_progress, todo_bad_list, todo_bad_item, todo_bad_merge, todo_no_session, todo_unknown_field (a key the schema does not have, top level or item), todo_plan_too_long and todo_shared_session. A refused call changes nothing, because a merge is built on a copy.

Whose plan it is. The coordinator passes the session, the turn's posture and whether the turn runs on the shared default session (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:851; Orchestrator.on_shared_session, agents/core/orchestrator.py:793). A turn keeps the answer it got when it resolved its session (agents/core/orchestrator.py:280), so an owner resuming another session does not let an in-flight turn in. A turn that binds no session of its own runs on that shared session, and the plan kept there is the owner's. Such turns include the HUD, the web widget (its route binds none), voice, rooms, notes, workflows, MCP ask_*, a webhook, a job, a subagent and a direct POST /api/toolrpc/call.
- On it, only an owner's turn keeps a plan. Anyone else is refused todo_shared_session and is never read the plan (agents/core/todo_tool.py:535). Neither the turn's offer nor a script's reach includes the tool for them (SESSION_SCOPED_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:229; agents/core/code_tools.py:362). Voice carries no identity, so even the owner's voice is a guest's turn there and keeps no plan.
- A turn on any other session keeps that session's plan, whoever it is. That covers a chat of its own and an explicit session a user token continues. Text written there by a turn that is not the owner's (a household member, a guest) is untrusted to the owner, and the owner's next turn reads it as DATA (agents/core/todo_tool.py:548).
- Otherwise it is offered like any ungated tool. An inbound guest reaches it through `llm.guest_tools`, whose default is now echo, time and todo (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:82). An install that still holds the old default (echo, time) gets the new one once, at start (agents/core/settings_db.py:474). A list the owner changed is left alone. An owner who empties it keeps guests off the tool loop entirely.
- At most 256 plans are kept in memory. The one the agent least recently wrote or read is dropped first, and an empty list frees its slot.

Where its text came from. Each item records three things: the posture of the turn that set its text (by), which turn that was, and whether it was untrusted (tainted). A turn is untrusted when it came from an inbound channel (the owner's own Telegram DM included), is not the owner's, or had already read untrusted content.
- A status set by an untrusted turn taints the item too. A clean rewrite of the text keeps the taint, because the id came from whoever wrote it first. The same text again is no write: the item keeps its writer, its turn and the plan's labels (agents/core/todo_tool.py:370).
- A call that answers with a tainted item another turn wrote says so (agents/core/todo_tool.py:561). The loop then fences the answer as DATA and raises the reading turn's taint. An item the reading turn wrote itself is its own argument, already in its transcript, and is not fenced (agents/core/todo_tool.py:446; the loop gives each run a turn token, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:342).
- So the owner's HUD turn that reads a plan written from Telegram is tainted by it. That follows the kernel's inbound policy, and the HUD tags such items "untrusted source".
- A script's own writes cannot launder text into the plan (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:35). The broker for an execute_code script's calls reads an answer as the loop reads a result (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:97): it raises the origin once a tool that declares untrusted_output answers ok, an answer says tainted, or the injection scanner flags an answer. A refusal, or a tool that raised, taints nothing. Every later call of that run then writes tainted items.
- A script's calls belong to no model turn (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:87), so what it wrote is data even to the turn that ran it.
- A session kernel that has held untrusted text taints every later cell's calls until a reset replaces its record (agents/core/session_kernels.py:674). It has held it once a cell read it, or ran in a turn that had. Each interpreter gets a mailbox directory of its own, removed with it (a reset, a crash, an idle expiry, an eviction), and a start clears what an earlier process left (agents/core/session_kernels.py:940, agents/core/session_kernels.py:960), so a file a tainted kernel wrote there never reaches the clean kernel after it.
- A run's result says tainted whenever it printed anything, read untrusted text, or ran on a kernel that held some (agents/core/code_tools.py:604), so the loop fences its output and raises the turn's taint whether the run succeeded or failed. A plan therefore cannot carry an injected instruction into a later, clean turn as the tool's own words, and the web tools' taint refusals and the kernel's queueing apply to the turn that ran the script.

The loop. It never replaces the answer with a "same as call N" stub, and never counts a todo call against a per-tool cap (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:125). The cap setting's label says so (agents/core/settings_db.py:180), and a start gives a stored row the current label (agents/core/settings_db.py:460).
- The repeat detector keys a todo call on its arguments and on the plan the model last saw (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1553). A read after the plan changed is the tool doing its job. The same call with nothing changed in between is stopped like any other repeat: the third is refused and the fourth ends the turn. A failed call leaves the plan the model saw unchanged. A script that made tool calls of its own may have changed the plan behind the model's back, so the next read after it is a new call (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1546).
- The answer is never cut: 7,000 bytes fits the smallest per-result budget, and the tool is pinned whole even after the turn's allowance is spent (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:100).
- The description asks the model to mark the item it starts in_progress, and completed when it is done.

The owner's view:
- A write leaves a todo_updated event in the tool trail (agents/core/todo_tool.py:458). It carries the session, the statuses, the position of the item in progress and the total. It never carries the text or the ids, which are free text too. A read or a refusal leaves no event.
- GET /sessions/todo and GET /sessions/{id}/todo (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:42, agents/core/routers/sessions.py:51) are user-guarded and no-store; an invalid id is a 400.
- Each item carries its by and tainted, never its turn. The recent list puts first the plan the agent most recently wrote or read. A plan's labels (when, which agent, whose turn) move only when its list changes.
- `nerva todo [SESSION]` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1207) prints the plans with [ ] [>] [x] [-] marks and each item's tags (agents/cli/nerva.py:1165): guest turn, household turn, background turn, untrusted source. A bad session id exits 2 before any request. A malformed reply, a non-object item included, exits 1.
- The Decision Inbox shows the plans with open work under the decisions (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:65, mounted at frontend/src/gap.tsx:3069). It shows at most three plans of eight items each, how long ago each plan was written, and every tag of each item (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:39). A failed read is shown as failed, with its reason, not as "no plans".
- The capability registry calls the tool reversible session state with a compensating rollback: a later call can write back what a call replaced, and the tool keeps no copy of it (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:283).
- A forget clears every plan (agents/core/data_purge.py:547) and lists todo_plans in live_stores_cleared. A turn already running when the purge starts can still write its plan afterwards, just as it still saves its reply.

Adapted: Hermes classifies todo as mutating in its loop guardrails. Here it is ungated because it writes only its own session's list: the shared session's list only for the owner's turns, and every item's origin is kept and shown.

Tests: tests/test_todo_tool.py (36 cases) covers the store, the tool, the loop, the routes, the purge and the CLI.

tests/test_h315b_todo_review.py (56 cases, first review) covers:
- the shared session through the real routes. A widget visitor, a webhook (tests/test_h315b_todo_review.py:187), a subagent and a direct tool call (tests/test_h315b_todo_review.py:216) neither read nor replace the owner's plan;
- a later turn tainted by text copied from an untrusted page (tests/test_h315b_todo_review.py:353);
- status updates between steps, which never end the turn (tests/test_h315b_todo_review.py:395).

tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py (37 cases, second review) covers:
- scripts in the real subprocess sandbox (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:115). A script that read an untrusted tool or a tainted plan writes tainted items, and a clean one writes clean items. Its write is data even to the turn that ran it;
- the real session kernel (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:241). A later clean cell writes tainted items, and a reset kernel's record starts clean;
- the upgrade migration and the label refresh (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:328);
- the pinned shared verdict (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:381);
- a turn's own plan unfenced (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:413);
- the repeat detector's revisions (tests/test_h315c_todo_review.py:482);
- a household member's text, the status and rewrite taint, the labels, the status-only cap, the byte measure, the mark cap, punctuation content, the resolver default, the script's reach, the capability record and the CLI's non-object items.

tests/test_h315d_todo_review.py (26 cases, third review) covers:
- a script and a kernel cell that read a page and fail, printed or silent, through the real loop: fenced, the turn tainted, the plan write tainted (tests/test_h315d_todo_review.py:90);
- a kernel's files gone after a reset, a crash and a restart (tests/test_h315d_todo_review.py:183);
- the broker's rule (a refusal, a raising tool, a scanner flag), a same-text merge, an untrusted turn's status, the posture rule, the coordinator's wiring, a failing shared-session getter, bind's default, a channel session that is the default, and the repeat detector after a script (tests/test_h315d_todo_review.py:257).

frontend/src/test/plans-in-flight.test.tsx (10 cases) covers the inbox section: the admin credential, marks with spoken names, every tag of an item, the plan's age at its boundaries, the caps, cancelled items struck through, a failed read with its reason, and reload.

Mutation, second round: 48 mutants of its guards (42 backend, 6 HUD), each run against its own suites. 38 were caught at once. Of the other ten:
- Two were code with no effect, and were removed: a broker per script run (the service loop's one context already carries the raised origin) and the kernel's mark before a cell (the broker and the mark after the cell cover it).
- One is equivalent: the HUD's clamp at zero, since a negative age already reads "just now".
- Seven got tests that now catch them. The tests also catch one new mutant: a broker that keeps its flag without marking the context.
- The second review's own set left 12 mutants no test caught. Re-run against this code, all 12 are caught. One of them, the resolver's fail-closed default, is now the code itself, and flipping it back to fail-open is caught.

Mutation, third round: 15 mutants of its guards, each run against its own suites. 12 were caught at once. Three were caught once a test was tightened or added: a cell's taint when it printed nothing (twice) and a script that made no tool calls. The third review's own 76 mutants left 11 that are not equivalent; each now has a test but one the round made equivalent: a same-text merge is no write now, so the labels' comparison cannot see a turn move. A raising tool now taints nothing by design, and that is pinned too.
session_search este oferit modelului și poate citi conversații salvate.
reviews.remaining: Acoperirea tuturor suprafețelor, căutarea completă și contractul canonic sesiune/date trebuie închise; probele sintetice nu definesc un ACL.

reviews.summary: The governed skill system is intact: loader, proposals, approval, signing, marketplace, curator and usage. Listing is covered by injection, not by a tool. SkillLoader.prompt_catalog (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1164) builds bounded rows (skill, command, description, at most 20) gated on signature and injection, and Orchestrator._prompt_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2949) adds them to every agent prompt unless llm.skills_in_prompt is off. Authoring reaches the governed pipeline only through the post-turn BackgroundReviewer, which is off by default. A new skill goes through SkillLoader.generate_skill quarantine (_dispatch_new_skill, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:284). A patch lands as a pending SkillProposalStore proposal plus an approval request (_dispatch_patch, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:298) and never touches the live skill. The model is offered no tool to list or read skills: the registry (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json) has no skills_list or skill_view, and GET /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:29) is an HTTP route.
reviews.remaining: There is no `skill_view`. During a turn the model can see only a skill's one-line catalog row; it cannot read the full SKILL.md or any linked reference, template or script file. There is no queryable `skills_list` tool either: the injected catalog is capped at 20 command rows. The accepted adaptation needs both as ungated read-only ToolRPC tools. They must apply prompt_catalog's trust gates (no sandboxed, quarantined or signature-mismatched skills; injection scan with taint), be bounded, and be confined to the skill's directory. An in-turn authoring request should route into SkillProposalStore or generate_skill quarantine (propose, never write SKILL.md).

reviews.summary: Catalogul mărginit de skilluri este injectat în prompt.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc părți ale scării L0/L1/L2, cacheului și deduplicării încărcărilor cerute de inventar.

reviews.summary:
The SKILL.md frontmatter contract Hermes parses (agent/skill_utils.parse_frontmatter and tools/skills_tool_plugin.py) now lives in one shared module, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py, used by both the loader and the importer.

Parsing. split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:47):
- drops a leading UTF-8 BOM before the fence check (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:56);
- takes the closing fence at column 0 only, as Hermes' `\n---\s*\n` does, so an indented `---` inside a block scalar is content (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:63);
- falls back to key: value lines for a block that is not valid YAML (_naive_key_values, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:83), instead of demoting the file to the heading dialect.

The fallback is stricter than Hermes' line split:
- only column-0 keys count, so a nested `name:` cannot replace the skill's own;
- a value wrapped in matching quotes loses them;
- a fallback that finds neither a name nor a description counts as no frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:77), so a heading-dialect file framed by fences keeps its heading parse.

Identity decisions pass lenient=False (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:72), so a name only the fallback can find never decides one: the Hermes pin gate (agents/core/skills/importer.py:268) and the migration and rescan slugs (agents/core/skills/importer.py:1178, agents/core/skills/importer.py:1354).

SkillLoader._parse_manifest decodes with utf-8-sig on both the snapshot and the path read (agents/core/skills/loader.py:746, agents/core/skills/loader.py:748). A manifest the normaliser cannot read registers under the directory name instead of failing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:763).

The manifest:
- The name is capped at 64 characters and stripped after the cut (agents/core/skills/loader.py:782; the caps are at agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:28-29).
- The description is capped at 1024 characters with an ellipsis, quotes kept (cap_description, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:351). When none is declared, it is the first non-heading body line, as Hermes' listing reads it (agents/core/skills/loader.py:784-785).
- A list-valued author or license is joined (agents/core/skills/loader.py:787).
- agents and requires read a YAML list, `[a, b]` or `a, b` as plain strings (agents/core/skills/loader.py:774-775).
- Command entries are reduced to JSON types (agents/core/skills/loader.py:859).

contract_fields (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:359), merged into every frontmatter manifest (agents/core/skills/loader.py:794), keeps the keys Hermes recognises:
- homepage and compatibility;
- platforms, read as Hermes matches them (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:204): a list, or one string as one name. Each name maps through PLATFORM_MAP and matches the OS whose sys.platform starts with it, so darwin and win count and osx and win64 do not. An unmatched name is kept, so a gate refuses it everywhere, as Hermes hides it;
- environments and requires_apps, where a string is one item (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:224, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:234);
- triggers and dependencies;
- tags and related_skills, where a declared metadata.hermes value wins over the top-level key (skill_view's `hermes_meta.get(k) or frontmatter.get(k)`);
- setup, prerequisites and required_credential_files;
- required_environment_variables (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:256), which matches Hermes' _get_required_environment_variables: it merges the declared list, setup.collect_secrets and the legacy prerequisites.env_vars, first entry wins, names are validated, and `optional` is read for truth;
- metadata.hermes.{tags, category, upstream_skill, supersedes, session_platforms, requires_toolsets, requires_tools, fallback_for_toolsets, fallback_for_tools, config} (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:340). A config entry needs a key and a description.

Skill exposes platforms, environments, requires_apps, required_env (names only; no value is read) and hermes_meta, and to_dict carries them (agents/core/skills/loader.py:432, agents/core/skills/loader.py:475, agents/core/skills/loader.py:483, agents/core/skills/loader.py:487, agents/core/skills/loader.py:493).

Imported frontmatter is third-party text:
- json_safe (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:128) bounds depth, width, string length and total nodes, with a 2,048-node budget per value (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:134). A 2 KB YAML alias bomb that would expand to 64^6 nodes parses in about 0.02 s.
- Dates become ISO strings, and NaN, infinities and integers past 64 bits become null or "". A hex integer past Python's str() limit no longer raises (_scalar_text, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:112), so the security-posture route serialises Skill.to_dict with allow_nan=False.
- discover() skips a skill whose load raises and keeps the rest, while the signing misconfiguration still stops discovery (agents/core/skills/loader.py:580-585).
- A second skill taking an occupied registry name is logged: a warning within one tree (e.g. two names sharing their first 64 characters), info for a user skill replacing a bundled one (agents/core/skills/loader.py:589).

Deliberate differences from Hermes:
- A closing fence at end of file with no trailing newline is accepted, as Nerva always did.
- The registry is last-writer-wins with that log line; Hermes' listing keeps the first.

Tests: tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py has 51 cases, including the alias bomb (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:286), a hex integer in seven fields (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:306), NaN and huge numbers through to_dict (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:315), one broken skill among others (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:328), the fallback rules (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:354), Hermes platform matching (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:406), the strict identity parse (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:434) and the snapshot BOM path (tests/test_skill_frontmatter_contract.py:482).

A mutation pass over 25 mutants (first-wins, precedence, the depth, width and node caps, both utf-8-sig decodes, the fence, the fallback rules, optional, the strict gate, NaN and big ints, the discover guard, the collision log, the platform string, author join, quotes, the body-line fallback, name strip, command sanitising, requires_apps) killed all of them.

454 tests across 28 skill, import, marketplace, migration and posture files pass.

Gating on these fields is not this row: H328 (visibility) and the setup rows consume them.

No conditional skill visibility exists. SkillLoader.discover (agents/core/skills/loader.py:557) loads every directory under the bundled and user roots unconditionally. prompt_catalog (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1164) hides a skill only for sandboxing, an untrusted signature, an injection-flagged row, or a declared agents list that excludes the caller. parse_command (agents/core/skills/loader.py:886) and Skill.execute accept any loaded skill. Since H327 the parser keeps platforms, environments and metadata.hermes.* (session_platforms, requires_toolsets, requires_tools, fallback_for_*) in normalised form (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py) and Skill exposes platforms, environments and hermes_meta, but nothing consults them. A probe on this head parsed a SKILL.md with `platforms: [macos]` on linux: the manifest carried platforms == ['macos'], and prompt_catalog still returned its row. There is no per-channel session_platforms gating (the turn surface known to agents/core/tool_profiles.py is not consulted by the skills catalog) and no requires_tools/fallback_for_* gating. Outside the parser and those read-only Skill properties, nothing under agents/core/skills/ reads these keys.
reviews.remaining: All four gates are missing. platforms: a hard gate that hides the skill and refuses explicit invocation with readiness_status unsupported. environments: soft hide only. metadata.hermes.session_platforms: per-channel hiding. requires_toolsets/requires_tools/fallback_for_toolsets/fallback_for_tools: checked against the tools actually offered this turn. A soft-hidden skill stays invokable by name, and every hide is logged. The widened parser (H327) now supplies the inputs; the gates themselves are the work.

reviews.summary: There is no reversible per-skill off switch. The skills router (agents/core/routers/skills.py) exposes list, import, marketplace install/review/rollback/uninstall and pending/approve routes but no enable/disable. The settings skills category (agents/core/settings_db.py:307 onward) holds only auto_generate, sandbox_enabled, max_skills and import_source. SkillLoader.prompt_catalog (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1164) and parse_command consult no disabled list, and no HUD control or CLI toggles a skill. The only ways to take a skill away are destructive. POST /api/skills/marketplace/uninstall (agents/core/routers/skills.py:515) calls SkillMarketplace.uninstall_skill (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:640), which deletes the directory; the route then revokes the owner approval bound to that path (agents/core/routers/skills.py:556-559). The curator's move is _archive_skill (agents/core/skills/curator.py:115). permission.grant is registered as a kernel-mediated kind (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:110), but no skill re-enable path exists to use it. HEQ lot 1 (H503) changed only how a package is installed: install_from_zip now extracts through the capped archive_safe module into a staging directory and renames it into place, so a rejected update no longer deletes the installed version. It adds no disabled state.
reviews.remaining: Missing: a persisted global skills.disabled list and a per-surface skills.platform_disabled list; hiding disabled skills from prompt_catalog and refusing explicit invocation with a named reason; an essential-skills floor that cannot be disabled; admin routes plus a HUD per-skill and per-category toggle; an audited direct write for disable; re-enable routed through permission.grant so the audit carries an approver; tests proving usage history, signature and approval survive a disable/enable cycle.

reviews.summary: The verified-pin fetch path exists and is unchanged. SkillImporter.import_from_hermes (agents/core/skills/importer.py:204) accepts only slugs present in agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json (78 entries). It fetches the exact commit URL with follow_redirects=False (agents/core/skills/importer.py:221). _fetch_verified_hermes_skill (agents/core/skills/importer.py:245) then rejects three things before _save_skill writes the exact bytes plus a provenance sidecar: a final-URL mismatch, a sha256 mismatch (checked with hmac.compare_digest, agents/core/skills/importer.py:264) and a frontmatter-name mismatch. scripts/nerva_import.py adds a one-command local migration from ~/.hermes, ~/.openclaw and ~/.claude, quarantined with PENDING_REVIEW. Since HEQ lot 1 (H344), every skill write that CLI makes crosses skill.install, including the new --apply --update re-import. ImportRunner._install_skill (scripts/nerva_import.py:744) first checks SKILL_IMPORT_CONTRACT (scripts/nerva_import.py:754), then calls the real kernel.authorize with the kill switch read from disk (scripts/nerva_import.py:606). A DENY writes nothing. The external origin keeps a GRANT at QUEUE. The write is bound to the probed digest. The front door that the accepted adaptation asked to change is unchanged. POST /skills/import (agents/core/routers/skills.py:309) is still user_guard plus the DEV_MODE gate (agents/core/routers/skills.py:314-315), and it never builds a skill.install action. skill.install is KERNEL-mediated (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:106). It is enforced from SkillMarketplace._enforce_skill_contract (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:185), from acquisition promotion and now from the local migration CLI, but never from this route. tests/test_skills_api.py:57-61 pins the DEV_MODE 403. The pin still names release v2026.8.27 (agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4). tests/test_hermes_import.py passes. It covers the pin inventory, digest and identity failures before any mutation, and bulk verify-before-write. tests/test_skills_api.py passes. tests/test_nerva_import.py passes, including the test that the CLI crosses the real kernel and honours the kill switch (tests/test_nerva_import.py:1220).
reviews.remaining: (1) POST /skills/import does not cross skill.install. No kernel action is built or decided before the network fetch or the write, so the permanent owner-approval floor never applies to this path. The local CLI's contract-then-kernel crossing is not reused by the route. (2) The DEV_MODE gate at agents/core/routers/skills.py:314-315 is still the only restriction; the adaptation replaces it with governance. (3) The non-hermes branch (agents/core/routers/skills.py:326) imports from any GitHub repo the caller names, through _import_from_github with follow_redirects=True (agents/core/skills/importer.py:306). That import is unpinned and unmediated. (4) Fetches use a raw httpx.AsyncClient instead of the SSRF-guarded PluginHTTPClient egress seam in agents/core/http_client.py. (5) The pin was not refreshed to v2026.8.31: agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4 is still v2026.8.27, and the PIN_* constants in tests/test_hermes_import.py match the old pin.

reviews.summary: Nothing substitutes template variables into a skill body. SkillLoader._parse_manifest splits the frontmatter with _split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/loader.py:405). _manifest_from_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/loader.py:767) uses the body only to parse commands (agents/core/skills/loader.py:777-778) and, when no description is declared, to take its first non-heading line as the description, as Hermes' listing does (agents/core/skills/loader.py:784-785); the manifest it returns carries no body. The only model-facing skill surface, SkillLoader.prompt_catalog (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1164), renders one bounded command/description row per advertised command and never includes a body. Skill.execute (agents/core/skills/loader.py:499) returns an empty string for a SKILL.md-only skill, so a body never reaches the model at all. agents/core/skills/ has no handling of ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}, ${HERMES_SESSION_ID}, a Nerva equivalent or skills.template_vars (a grep over agents/ for these names returns nothing). A scratch probe parsed a frontmatter SKILL.md whose body contained ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/x.sh: the manifest came back without the body and nothing was expanded. The existing frontmatter tests in tests/test_hermes_import.py pass. The H351 catalog-scan tests added to tests/test_skills_in_prompt.py concern injection scanning of catalog rows, not body substitution.
reviews.remaining: Load-time substitution into the skill body is missing. It should cover a fixed skill-dir variable and a session-id variable (Nerva names, plus the ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}/${HERMES_SESSION_ID} spellings used by imported skills) and owner-configured skills.template_vars (literal non-secret values only, never environment variables). The substitution must happen at the point the body reaches the model. No such point exists today: the body is discarded at parse time and no skill-view surface delivers it (see H326).

reviews.summary: Import-once stays the only way a Hermes / OpenClaw / Claude Code skill enters Nerva's skills tree (no live-scanned external_dirs tier; SkillLoader.discover() is unchanged), and a re-run of `python scripts/nerva_import.py` now notices upstream movement instead of reporting a blanket skipped/exists. Each imported skill is re-detected against the absolute source_path and sha256 recorded in its manifest.json (importer.py:941, importer.py:986): unchanged; changed, with the old and new digests plus a bounded line diff shown by --json; moved to another folder of the same install and followed (importer.py:920); removed; renamed; unreadable; or source_untrusted when a record names a file outside the install, which is then never read (importer.py:1268). The default run is a dry run. `--apply --update` re-imports only changed skills that this source imported (importer.py:1051): the current copy is backed up under data/imports/skill_backups, PENDING_REVIEW is written before the new bytes land, SKILL.sig and the legacy approval marker are cleared, and the owner's approval is revoked. A linked control file, an unusable backup dir or a refused save fails closed, and the write is bound to the probed digest. Every import and re-import crosses skill.install through the real Action Kernel at the shipped CLI (nerva_import.py:577, bound at nerva_import.py:1032 and as the ImportRunner default at nerva_import.py:682), behind SKILL_IMPORT_CONTRACT (nerva_import.py:145). The persisted kill switch is re-read on every decision, so an engaged halt refuses an import or re-import before a byte moves. The external origin keeps a policy GRANT at QUEUE, and only GRANT or QUEUE writes (nerva_import.py:764), so every write lands quarantined. The human summary names a local edit that --update replaces (with its backup path), a failed revoke, and moved, untrusted and refused rows (nerva_import.py:938). Tests in test_nerva_import.py: 44 passed and 1 live-gated skip under python 3.11 and 3.12. They include test_cli_skill_writes_cross_the_real_kernel_and_honour_the_kill_switch, test_runner_default_authorizer_is_the_kernel_for_skills_and_queue_for_memory, test_source_moved_within_the_install_is_followed_not_reported_removed, test_apply_update_reimports_changed_skill_into_quarantine_and_revokes_approval, test_rescan_never_follows_a_record_outside_the_install and test_reimport_refuses_a_linked_control_file_and_never_writes_through_it. Two known limits sit outside the accepted requirement. (1) The CLI binds no durable audit sink, so each kernel decision is recorded only on its report row (kernel/kernel_reason) and in the in-process kernel metrics. (2) A record written before this change with a cwd-relative source_path (relative --home) is not rewritten by an unchanged re-run. From another directory it reads skipped/exists plus source_untrusted until a changed source is re-imported with --apply --update, which records the absolute path.

No SKILL.md validator or linter exists. _split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/loader.py:405) now delegates to split_frontmatter in agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py (H327): a YAML error falls back to top-level key: value lines as Hermes does (a fallback that finds neither a name nor a description counts as no frontmatter), but a block that parses to a non-mapping, or a fence that never closes, still returns (None, content), and _parse_manifest then falls back to the heading parser (agents/core/skills/loader.py:765), producing a skill named after its directory with an empty description — silently, with no error. An over-long name or description is truncated to 64/1024 characters rather than refused. None of the write paths validates the document. SkillLoader.generate_skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:914) writes a fixed heading template (agents/core/skills/loader.py:993) after only the injection scan and _safe_command_name. SkillProposalStore.apply writes the approved proposed text verbatim (agents/core/skills/proposals.py:129). SkillImporter._save_skill (agents/core/skills/importer.py:403) checks only the slug. The H344 local re-import that HEQ lot 1 added (_reimport_local_skill) writes through the same _save_skill with no document check. SkillMarketplace.publish_skill (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:345) and install_from_zip (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:772) require only that a SKILL.md exists (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:356; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:797 calls _find_manifest, which raises at agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:750). install_from_zip now extracts through archive_safe with package member and byte caps (H503) into a staging dir before placing. Those are archive-safety limits on the package, not validation of the SKILL.md document. There is no advisory lint script.
reviews.remaining: Two pieces are missing. (1) A hard validator that returns field-level errors: fence present, YAML mapping, name present and a safe slug, description present and within the length cap, non-empty body, size cap. It must block the write at every entry point: import (_save_skill / _import_local_skill, including the H344 re-import path), marketplace publish and install_from_zip, agent generation, and proposal apply. (2) An advisory authoring linter (a CLI) for the standards the hard validator does not cover.

reviews.summary: **The discovery surface, not the one the row names — and the row says so.** `SkillLoader.prompt_catalog` produces the "Available skills" block that `Agent.build_prompt` renders **verbatim** into every system prompt, and both of a row's fields (`command`, carrying the manifest's `args`, and `description`) come out of a SKILL.md frontmatter that may have been imported from a foreign install. Write-time scanning already refuses to *generate* an injection-flagged skill and flags imported ones — nothing stood between an already-on-disk manifest and the prompt. Two gates close that, and both only ever narrow the block. **(1)** A skill shipping a `SKILL.sig` that does not verify here is not named at all; `unsigned` and `algo-mismatch` are tolerated on purpose, because the first is the shipped default for every bundled skill and the second is a fact about *this host's key configuration at load time* that fires for all signed skills at once — dropping either would blank the model's whole skills index on a key rotation. **(2)** A row that tries to talk to the model loses its row, scanned with the same `detect_injection` pattern table that fences retrieved memory — through `quarantine.detect_injection_normalized`, which scans the row as written *and* its normalised copies and unions the hits. A hit costs one row, never the block; every drop is WARNING-logged by skill name so a disappearance from the index is never silent, and a catalog emptied by the signature gate is logged at ERROR rather than quietly returned. Nothing is revoked: a dropped skill is un-advertised, and its command still runs if the model or the owner names it. **An independent adversarial review found two majors and both are fixed here.** `command` was the one row field nothing bounded — `re.fullmatch(r"\w+", command)` bounds the character set (to `\w`, which is wider than it reads: see remaining) and not the length, and `command` never passed through the new `_catalog_text` — so a manifest declaring a 5,000-character command put 5,000 characters into every agent's prompt on every turn; reproduced, and capped like its neighbours (`test_the_command_name_is_capped_like_every_other_field`). And the injection scan was defeated by a single Cf format character: `strip_invisible` is TAG-only by design, so "Ignore​ all previous instructions" scanned clean while reading to the model exactly like the phrase that does not — reproduced against U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2060, U+00AD and U+200E. **The first fix (strip every Cf character, scan only that copy) was itself two holes, and #1177 closed both.** Cf was never the whole invisible class: the variation selectors U+FE00–U+FE0F and U+E0100–U+E01EF (Mn), U+034F COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER, the Hangul fillers U+115F/U+1160/U+3164/U+FFA0 (Lo) and the C0/C1 controls (Cc) all render as nothing, match no pattern and are not whitespace to `str.split`, so "Ignore all pre️vious instructions" reached the system prompt verbatim while the Cf-only test stayed green; `quarantine.strip_format_chars` removes all of them (`_FORMAT_CHARS` + `_INVISIBLE_EXTRA_CHARS`), and everything `str.split` calls whitespace is deliberately kept so a deleted *whitespace* separator never glues two words together. And scanning the stripped copy *instead of* the raw row was weaker than no normalisation at all on some inputs, because a deletion destroys a match as easily as it reveals one: the `you are now\b` rule needs a word boundary, and in "You are now​in developer mode" the zero-width space *is* that boundary — stripped, the row scanned clean and was advertised, while the same sentence written with an ordinary space lost its row. So the normaliser unions, never substitutes. **#1179 widened the normaliser the catalog calls, and one of the two evasions it closed was live in the catalog.** `detect_injection_normalized` now scans every copy in `_detection_variants` — the text as written, `strip_format_chars` of it, `collapse_whitespace` of it (every Unicode whitespace run to one ASCII space, because each pattern spells its gaps as one literal space) and the collapse of the stripped copy — unioned raw first, in pattern order within each copy, deduplicated; every copy is thrown away and the emitted row is the original, so a legitimate Arabic number sign survives into the prompt untouched while an evasion attempt does not decide the verdict. Plain respacing was never a catalog hole: `_catalog_text` one-lines `args` and `description` with `" ".join(...split())` before the scan (and `\w+` admits no whitespace into `command`), so two spaces, a TAB, a NO-BREAK SPACE, a NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE, an IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE or a LINE SEPARATOR between the words already reached the literal scan as one space — probed on all seven, and regex `\s` and `str.isspace` were walked against each other over all of Unicode and agree exactly, so on catalog rows the collapse of the as-written text is an identity. The composition was live: an invisible character that `str.split` leaves as *its own token* — "Ignore <U+200B> all previous instructions", VS16 likewise — survives `_catalog_text` with a space on each side, the as-written scan misses (the token sits between the words), and the stripped copy is "Ignore  all previous instructions" with a double space the single-space pattern does not match. Reproduced against the pre-#1179 module through `prompt_catalog`: the row was advertised; at HEAD the collapse of the stripped copy folds the double space and the row is dropped. **That is no longer the normaliser's whole reach, and the placement this row carried as open is closed here.** Deleting was never the only right answer to an invisible character: beside a space it has to go, *instead of* the space it has to become one. `_detection_variants` now yields a third rewrite — every strip-table character replaced by a space, then collapsed — unioned like the others rather than substituted (so `pre<U+200B>vious`, which needs the deletion, keeps matching through the deleted copy), and every copy again over the NFKC fold, because fullwidth `\uff29\uff47\uff4e\uff4f\uff52\uff45` renders as the word and is a different code point to every pattern until it is folded. The strip table also gains U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK and the private-use planes. Probed end to end through `prompt_catalog` on this head against `main` at 97ee1835: `Ignore<U+200B>all previous instructions`, the same phrase with every gap spelled U+3164, U+FE0F, U+FFA0 or U+2800, a `command` spelled `ignore<U+3164>all<U+3164>previous<U+3164>instructions`, and the fullwidth phrase were all ADVERTISED by main's catalog and all lose their row here; `Ignore <U+200B> all …`, `pre<U+200B>vious` and the plain phrase were dropped by both; an English, a Romanian, an Arabic, a Japanese, an emoji-with-tag-sequence and a fullwidth-punctuation description keep their rows on both. The catalog is where this row is paid, so each of those cases is pinned HERE and not only at the scanner: all 32 catalog tests passed while the previous placement was advertised, which is exactly how a regression of the variant set would hide. #1179 also added `injection_spans` (positions, not only hits) — used solely by the SOUL persona scan in `agent.py`, never by the catalog — and left `_INJECTION_PATTERNS`, `strip_format_chars`, both character tables, `prompt_catalog` and `_catalog_text` byte-for-byte as #1177 left them. The Cf half of the table is hardcoded to keep import cheap and pinned against `unicodedata` by `test_the_format_char_table_matches_unicodedata`, so a new Cf character in a future Python fails there rather than silently widening the hole; the extra classes are pinned per character by `test_the_strip_reaches_past_cf_into_every_invisible_class`, the kept separators by `test_the_strip_keeps_the_separators_that_segment_words`, the union in both directions by `test_detect_injection_normalized_unions_the_two_scans`, the collapse against every `str.isspace` code point by `test_collapse_whitespace_folds_every_separator_python_calls_whitespace`, seven respacings by `test_no_respacing_hides_a_phrase_from_the_normalized_scan`, the strip-then-collapse composition by `test_the_normalized_scan_composes_both_rewrites`, and the catalog end to end by `test_a_stripped_copy_may_not_replace_the_scan_of_the_row_as_written` (equality with the spaced sentence, not merely "something fired") plus the nine-character `test_no_invisible_character_smuggles_a_row_past_the_catalog_scan` (character inside a word). Two overstated test docstrings were corrected rather than left to read as guarantees. Re-verified on this head: 75/75 pass across tests/test_skills_in_prompt.py (49; 32 unchanged since #1177, seventeen added here for the placements above and for six legitimate multilingual descriptions that must keep their rows) and tests/test_h17_1_quarantine.py (26). The scanner-side pins for the same rewrites are in tests/test_instruction_files_read_side_scan.py (47).
reviews.remaining: **This is not the surface H351 asks for.** The row wants a *load-time* warning on the skill BODY: a skill whose file sits outside the trusted roots, or whose content matches `_INJECTION_PATTERNS`, flagged in the `skill_view` result so the model sees the warning beside the content, with the body fenced as data the way `rag_guard` fences recall. None of that is here, and #1179 did not add it. This slice hardens the *discovery* block — the row's declared dependency ("model-facing discovery, row 1") — so a manifest cannot address the model through the skills index. Nerva has no `skill_view` equivalent: a skill body reaches the model with nothing re-checking it after import and nothing spotlighting or datamarking it. **What the two gates are worth, stated plainly rather than implied.** The signature gate detects corruption and accidental drift in a skill that ships a sidecar; it does not stop an attacker. Anyone with write access to a skill directory — exactly the access needed to edit SKILL.md — deletes `SKILL.sig` in the same operation, the skill verifies as `unsigned`, and it is advertised again on its new description. That evasion is pinned by a test on purpose (`test_deleting_the_sidecar_evades_the_trust_gate`). Closing it needs two things this repo does not have: a signed skills tree, and a record kept OUTSIDE the tree of which skills were once seen signed. The review raised a second, simpler evasion that is also real and is recorded here rather than fixed: at the shipped default, with no `JARVIS_SKILL_SIGNING_KEY`, the "signature" is a plain sha256 anyone can recompute (`agents/core/skills/signing.py`, SEC-B2). The injection gate is a ten-entry phrase table: it costs a row to a description that spells "ignore all previous instructions" in the words the table lists *and* in a placement the normaliser reaches, and not to one that says the same thing in words the table does not list — the normalisation (invisible-strip, whitespace-collapse and their composition, since #1179) widens what the table *sees*, not what it *lists*, and it does not see everything. It raises the floor on copied-in manifests; it is not a filter a motivated author cannot write around. **The invisible-character placement this row carried as open is closed, and what is left of it is narrowing, not a hole.** The spaced copy plus the NFKC fold close the in-place-of-a-separator placement in both row fields, including the `command` door: `re.fullmatch(r"\w+", command)` still admits the four Hangul fillers U+115F, U+1160, U+3164 and U+FFA0 (category Lo, letters to `\w`), so a command can still be *spelled* with them — it is now detected and the row dropped, pinned per character. Narrowing the gate to ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_]` remains worth doing as defence in depth: it costs none of the 34 bundled commands, all ASCII today (re-checked on this head), and it would keep the field bounded independently of what the phrase table happens to list. What the widened normaliser still does NOT reach is unchanged and stated plainly: a Cyrillic or Greek homoglyph, a combining overlay, markdown emphasis inside a word, and a phrase split across two rows or two fields all scan clean — that is a confusables table and a cross-field pass, neither of which is here. **The catalog-level pins that were missing are here, and the docstring drift is corrected.** The own-token placement (`Ignore <U+200B> all previous instructions`), closed by the collapse-of-the-stripped-copy variant but pinned only at the quarantine layer, now has its own catalog case, as do the five in-place-of-a-separator spellings, the four filler spellings of `command` and the fullwidth phrase; each was run against the pre-slice module and fails there. `loader.py`'s `prompt_catalog` docstring and the comment above the scan described a two-copy scan and called the table "eleven-entry" against ten; both now name `_detection_variants` as the source of the copy set and the count is right. **One thing deliberately left narrow:** `strip_invisible` stays TAG-only for `strip_invisible_deep`, which runs over tool results and MCP payloads where a BOM or a bidi mark can be part of data a caller expects back unchanged. Those paths still run no `detect_injection_normalized` (#1179's `mcp/client.py` change is the stdio cwd disclosure, not a scan); whether they should is a separate slice with its own blast radius — and the normaliser now has a second consumer, the SOUL persona scan in `agent.py` (switched by #1179 from a strip-only scan), so any further widening of it, the separator-replacement copy above included, is paid for there too.

reviews.summary: Backend-urile cloud Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter/compatibil și adaptoarele Responses API-key (OpenAI gpt-4.1, xAI Grok) declară `supports_tools = True` și vorbesc nativ protocolul de unelte, deci bucla guvernată din `agent_runtime` rulează și pe ruta cloud: Claude traduce istoricul în blocuri `tool_use`/`tool_result` (id-uri invalide înlocuite consecvent, rezultate paralele comasate, cache pe sistem + ultima unealtă, controale de efort prin `_fit_to_wire`); Gemini trimite `functionDeclarations` și re-emite `thoughtSignature`; OpenRouter/compatibil folosește dialectul OpenAI; xAI păstrează raționamentul criptat pe durata invocației. Streaming SSE există pe calea de text (Claude, Gemini, Responses). Eșecurile sunt ture degradate, nu excepții. Regresii: tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, tests/test_openai_responses.py, tests/test_xai_responses.py.
reviews.remaining: O tură cu unelte nu e streamuită: `generate_tool_turn` nu primește callback de token pe niciun wire, iar bucla din agent_runtime o așteaptă întreagă; streamingul există doar pe calea de text. Pe Claude, blocurile `thinking` ale unei ture cu unelte nu sunt păstrate pe ToolTurn și nici redate înapoi: `anthropic_messages` convertește doar text + `tool_use`. Codex nu e implementat (OAuth/abonament, rezumate de raționament, replay criptat pe OpenAI): adaptorul Responses e API-key și servește doar gpt-4.1, fără raționament. Nu există adaptor Bedrock Converse: `host_protocol.py` doar refuză cererile de alt protocol trimise către hosturile bedrock-runtime. Nu există probe cu provideri live.

reviews.summary: Compatible adapter now carries an explicit ProviderProfile; supports_prompt_cache_key defaults off and gates a hashed session-stable key on text/tool requests. Agent request identity is ContextVar-local, restored on exit. Existing Anthropic cache accounting is preserved. Reasoning integration was reviewed against previously-current grid33165622 evidence: request-shaping refusals/empty controls do not change this row's cache, session or context/usage semantics. Existing focused regressions are retained. Ordinary Claude text and streaming requests now reuse the existing single ephemeral cache breakpoint for nonempty system text, matching tool-turn prefix caching. Empty system serialization, exact content, auth retry bodies, version headers, reasoning/refusal and sampling rules, cache-read/write usage and streaming callback/error semantics are preserved. Two actual mocked HTTP requests failed before the two-expression fix; 12 focused regressions and independent review verify the repair. An explicitly selected API-key OpenAI Responses adapter now serves only gpt-4.1 and its reviewed dated ID at the fixed public endpoint. Stateless store:false text/function transcripts use hashed request-session cache keys and finite in_memory or24h retention. Actual guarded/mock HTTP tests cover routing, cache serialization, call_id replay, bounded streams and no automatic retries. This is public API-key access, not Codex subscription authentication. A separate fixed xAI Responses adapter reuses the bounded transport without changing OpenAI cache behavior. Its profile does not advertise prompt-cache-key support, and xAI requests deliberately omit prompt_cache_key and retention fields. This integration adds no xAI cache-hit, discount or Codex authentication claim.
reviews.remaining: Named Codex OAuth/subscription authentication is not implemented by the public API-key Responses adapter. Live cache-hit percentages and billing are not claimed. Compatible chat-completions cache support still requires explicit declaration; unknown endpoints do not gain parameters. store:false is not a claim of zero provider retention. Existing cache-write pricing approximation is unchanged.

reviews.summary: Existing Anthropic ladder extended to exact reviewed Gemini 2.5 budget models and Gemini 3 level models, with operator model declarations and normalization on text/tool/stream payloads. Admin settings can construct an OpenRouter/custom compatible cloud adapter with explicit wire capabilities and canonical clamping; local-only policy and approved-model checks remain in force. Review repair: per-backend immutable vocabulary snapshots prevent stale removed settings and cross-instance overrides. Reviewed repair now refuses below-minimum effort before HTTP/retry/usage, and explicit empty declarations suppress all reasoning controls. Budget-only mappings remain distinct from native effort fields; canonical clamping and constructor/registry empty precedence are verified. CLI chat now accepts canonical --reasoning for one invocation and sends the optional HTTP/SSE request field without writing settings. Compatible/OpenRouter, Gemini and Anthropic adapters consume request-local overrides on text, stream and structured turns while shared backend defaults remain unchanged. Missing/null preserves configured defaults; explicit none retains existing provider-specific disable/refusal semantics. Nested null frames retain explicit ancestor revocation, and expired scopes cannot issue subsequent retries. Actual CLI-to-HTTP-to-mocked-provider, SSE lifetime, concurrency and stdlib-only CLI regressions pass independent review. The new API-key Responses profile is restricted to non-reasoning GPT-4.1 exact IDs and declares an empty reasoning vocabulary, emitting no reasoning controls. It preserves cloud/local-only and approved-model gates. Both real HTTP dispatch paths check invocation lifetime, including prebuilt payloads and nested null scopes; unsupported models refuse before HTTP. Fixed xAI Responses now supports exact grok-4.6 and grok-4.5 with declared low/medium/high/xhigh and low/medium/high vocabularies, respectively. Canonical invocation effort uses nearest-weaker resolution, below-minimum local refusal and explicit-empty omission. Actual text/stream/tool requests preserve encrypted native reasoning and function-call order only inside a revocable backend/model/session-bound invocation. Mismatched, missing, expired, oversized or truncated replay refuses before HTTP/tools; no plaintext reasoning or replay state enters persisted conversation history. Existing local-only and approved-model policy remains authoritative.
reviews.remaining: The referenced providers.flags-model-overrides contract still lacks invocation-only chat --model and --provider authoring (HTTP/CLI); --reasoning is implemented. Named vendor declaration/translation coverage from the referenced ladder inventory, such as Kimi, DeepSeek and GLM, is not produced by the generic owner-supplied compatible declaration mechanism. Future mappings require verified current supported schemas and must preserve H679 no-escalation rather than copy historical stronger-level overrides. The xAI adapter supports only exact Grok4.5/4.6, not unverified legacy aliases or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Unknown models remain undeclared/refused as appropriate; explicit none may locally refuse when disabling cannot be honored. No live-provider acceptance or billing proof.

reviews.summary: Nerva does not read provider quota headers. A grep for x-ratelimit, anthropic-ratelimit and retry-after across agents/ finds only Nerva's own inbound HTTP throttle. Provider rate limits are handled after the fact. _ROTATABLE_STATUS (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:28) treats a 429 like an auth failure. The Anthropic backend reads only the status code (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:115) and calls report_failure (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:117), which benches the key with exponential cooldown up to _MAX_COOLDOWN of 900s (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:31). The only visibility is AuthProfilePool.status (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:178) through GET /api/llm/auth-profiles (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:427), which shows failures and health per key, not remaining quota. The cooldown lives in per-process memory, so other processes do not share a 429.
reviews.remaining: No tracker captures x-ratelimit-* or anthropic-ratelimit-* headers, or retry-after, from provider responses. There are no usage bars or /usage surface in the HUD, CLI or channels showing remaining requests or tokens and reset times. There is no cross-process 429 guard in a shared file that the gateway, cron/autonomy and CLI processes consult before requesting. No router input uses the forecast.

reviews.summary: Nerva enforces who may use which model but shows no cost or data-training warning when a model is chosen. The allowlist is _enforce_approved_models (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:485), called in select_backend (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:507); it raises ModelNotApprovedError under strict JARVIS_STRICT_MODELS. LOCAL_ONLY_AGENTS (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:93) is a local-only floor the registry cannot override. The daily spend cap is set by set_daily_cost_cap (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:631) from the llm.daily_cost_cap_usd setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:175) and checked in _cloud_permitted (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:643). Per-million prices exist in cost_estimator MODELS; claude-fable-5 is priced at $10/$50. None of this is consulted when the model is chosen. llm.claude_model (agents/core/settings_db.py:149) and llm.compatible_model (agents/core/settings_db.py:167) are free text. The admin settings PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:144) runs validate_category (agents/core/routers/admin.py:148), which accepted claude-fable-5 and a ':free' compatible model with no confirmation. ProviderProfile (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:28) has no data-retention or training field. HEQ lot 1 (H583) added one request-time data-policy control, for the OpenRouter route only. llm.openrouter_data_collection is seeded deny (agents/core/settings_db.py:165; agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:41). HybridRouter hands the backend a reader of the openrouter_* rows (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:395), and OpenRouterBackend attaches OpenRouter's provider object only under the openrouter profile (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:70). By default OpenRouter may therefore route a request only to upstream providers that do not store or train on prompts. tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:192 pins the deny default, and tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:287 pins deny for openrouter and no provider object for openai-compatible. This filters where a request is served, not what the owner selects. A model served only by data-collecting upstreams is still accepted at selection and fails at request time with a 404 that is logged against the setting (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:128).
reviews.remaining: There is no cost guard: selecting a very expensive model through the admin settings PUT, the CLI `nerva config set`, or a job pin does not require an explicit confirmation showing its $/M input and output price. There is no data-training-tier field on the provider profile or model catalog, so no selection surface can tell the owner that a vendor tier trains on prompts. The H583 data_collection knob covers only OpenRouter's upstream routing; the Claude, Gemini, xAI, openai-compatible and openai-responses routes carry no data-policy fact. There is no warning or acknowledgement when a vendor tier trains on prompts: switching llm.openrouter_data_collection to allow is an ordinary validated select write through the admin PUT or `nerva config set`, with no confirmation. There is no consent event written to the audit log for that acknowledgement; the SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row now records a choice's new value (llm.openrouter_data_collection=allow, since H153's second review), but as an ordinary write, not an acknowledgement, and `nerva config set` writes no audit row. There is no single selection-guard registry run server-side before persistence on every model-selection surface.

reviews.summary: No code proves that a configured cloud key works before a real turn uses it.
