reviews.summary:
H456 re-read against 55d625f. The 2026-09-07 evidence ("no per-item toolset allowlist") is stale, but the row stays partial.

The enabled_toolsets half of the contract is shipped and well built. agents/core/job_toolsets.py holds:
- an immutable CATALOG (:7-11: basic/files/terminal);
- a strict `validate()` that refuses unknown, non-list or duplicate ids (:14-21);
- `resolve()`, which refuses a group whose members are not all registered ('enabled_toolsets contains an unavailable toolset', :30-37);
- `toolset_scope()` (:63-79), whose nested frame is `parent.names.intersection(names)` (:72) with a shared _Lifetime, so a closed parent raises 'job toolset scope expired' (:66-67) instead of falling back to defaults. Intersect-never-union is enforced.

It is enforced at three boundaries, not one:
- the offering boundary (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:220,228 `allowed = allows(name) and _posture_allows(...)`, narrowed again by agents.yaml patterns at :231-232);
- the runtime filter before and after the profile (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:259-268), re-applied at the in-turn compaction boundary by `_resolve_offer` (H672);
- RPC intake, ahead of preflight and handler (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:328-330, reason `job_toolset_not_allowed`).

Store boundary: agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:363 lists the option, :366-370 validates it and refuses it with `no_agent`, validate_action:310-311 refuses it on non-`ask` actions, and create and edit both re-resolve it (:1199, :1268). Fire time: jobs.py:1470-1472 `with toolset_scope(self._toolset_names(job.options)), selection_scope(job.options)`. Doctor reports the catalog, each job's `toolset_upper_bound` and a `toolsets_unavailable` problem (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:51-55, :113). Reachable from the CLI (`--toolsets default|none|<ids>`, agents/cli/nerva.py:179,189,970-976) and the HUD (frontend/src/panels/job-builder.tsx:35-49). PATCH /api/jobs/{id} refuses an unavailable toolset with 422 (tests/test_job_toolsets.py:327-328).

Hermes' two removal rules are met structurally. Every register_tool on the production server was enumerated: agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:442-774 (image_generate, H313's `speak` at :455-471, desktop_run, terminal_run, desktop_plan, operator_plan, osint_enrich, echo, time) and :778-867 (session_search, file_*, web_search/web_extract, search_memory, execute_code), plus H315's `todo`, registered after the tool profile (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:911), which writes only its session's own checklist (on the owner's shared session, only an owner's turn keeps one). None creates a job, and no `schedule.create` kernel capability exists. None is a messaging/clarify tool that needs a live human. The new `speak` announces into a room, but it is registered only with JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR on and is gated (ask-tier card, trusted execution only from an owner-accepted row), so it is never offered off the owner posture.

Verified green at 55d625f: 27 cases in tests/test_job_toolsets.py and 28 in tests/test_job_model_pins.py. The HUD cases in frontend/src/panels/job-toolsets.test.tsx were not re-run in this pass.

What keeps the row open is the contract's second half: a job cannot pin reasoning effort.
- Selection carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25).
- validate_options rejects any unknown option (jobs.py:363), so the pin cannot be stored; neither jobs.py nor job_selection.py mentions reasoning at 55d625f.
- _ask never enters `reasoning_scope`, so every scheduled run inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read in agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:338,351,389,418-419.
- The closed-lifetime transport machinery already exists (agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72), but only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1148, :1201).

Secondary gap: the bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~18 tools the server can register. A job that needs web_search, execute_code or search_memory must run unbounded on the default net, a residual that docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names itself.
reviews.remaining:
(1) The per-job reasoning-effort pin (Hermes' `.cron-reasoning`, rolled into this row) is not implemented:
- `Selection` carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25), and `validate_pins` (:35-43) never sees an effort.
- `validate_options` rejects any option outside the known ten (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:363), so the pin cannot reach the store.
- `JobRunner._ask` (jobs.py:1470-1472) enters `toolset_scope` + `selection_scope` but never `reasoning_scope`. A job therefore always inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read at agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:338, :351, :389, :418-419.

The transport half already exists and is clamped: agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72; agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:81-86 with per-model overrides; agents/core/llm/gemini.py:134; agents/core/llm/xai.py:73; agents/core/llm/provider_request.py:46 and :54. Only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1148, :1201). Work owed:
- accept `reasoning` in validate_pins/validate_options against LADDER;
- enter `reasoning_scope(...)` in `_ask` beside the other two scopes;
- expose it on the CLI/HUD/doctor like the model and provider pins;
- test it in tests/test_job_model_pins.py.

(2) The bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~19 tools the production server can register. CATALOG (agents/core/job_toolsets.py:7-11) covers echo/time, the five file tools and terminal_run. These belong to no group: web_search, web_extract, search_memory, session_search, execute_code, desktop_plan, desktop_run, operator_plan, osint_enrich, image_generate and (with the Media Director on) speak, registered at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:442-774 and :778-867. A job that needs any of them must leave `enabled_toolsets` unset and run on the full default net. H315's todo is not among them: a job runs on the owner's shared session, where only an owner's turn keeps a plan, so no job uses it, with or without a group. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names this residual itself ("does not claim ... arbitrary plugin/delegation/code-runner groups"), and doctor reports the upper bound, not the effective offers.

(3) Minor: Hermes' middle precedence tier has no equivalent. That tier is a per-platform `cron` tools config that sets defaults for every scheduled job. Here, only the per-job list, the internal posture (`llm.internal_actuation`) and the agent's agents.yaml `tools:` patterns narrow an unattended run.

reviews.summary: The pieces around the feature exist, but nothing binds a standing instruction to a conversation. HeartbeatScheduler (agents/core/heartbeat.py:180) schedules per-agent routines from HEARTBEAT.md or agents.yaml, with MIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL 3600 s (agents/core/heartbeat.py:52) and 15–30 s jitter. Since H506 it also refuses a HEARTBEAT front-matter that its injection scan flags. Admin routes /heartbeat/{agent_id}/start|stop|run (agents/core/routers/heartbeat.py:27) and the HUD HeartbeatPanel drive it. Owner-armed jobs accept plain-words schedules, can be paused, resumed and deleted, and include an `ask` action that sends a prompt to an agent. That prompt goes through a one-shot Orchestrator.process call on channel 'job' (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1478), and the reply goes to the owner's channel, not into the originating chat's history. The only chat slash commands are /help, /status, /sessions, /pause, /stop, /resume, /jobs, /remind and /voice. CommandContext (agents/core/commands.py:50) carries no explicit session id, but its principal is a Principal with channel and chat (agents/core/commands.py:37-46), and ctx.orch.session_id already resolves to the bound channel session because the channel handler sets the active session before handle_input dispatches a command. Turns are serialized per session: Orchestrator.turn_lease (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1547) keeps a per-session asyncio.Lock table with a re-entrant held set. But nothing records an idle boundary or consults that lease before firing a heartbeat. Existing heartbeat and jobs tests pass (tests/test_heartbeat.py, tests/test_heartbeat_actions.py, tests/test_owner_jobs.py).
reviews.remaining:
Every accepted part is missing:
- No `/heartbeat every <interval> <prompt>` entry point, and no pause/resume/clear/status for it.
- No per-session persistence binding a standing prompt to a session_id and originating channel/chat.
- No idle-only firing: turn_lease serializes turns but no heartbeat consults it, and no idle boundary is recorded (row H460's idle-boundary rule, also missing).
- No fire record written before the injected turn runs, so a long turn could double-fire.
- No coalescing of missed ticks with the anchor reset to now.
- No floor specific to this lane.
- No 'any DB failure degrades to no heartbeat' guard.
- No injection of the prompt as a user turn into that conversation's history, where its effects would cross the kernel normally.

reviews.summary: Only the human-wait restraint exists. ScheduleRuntime.due (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:163) returns a skip reason from SKIP_REASONS (schedule_runtime.py:50): terminal, stopping, blocked, budget_spent, not_due or at_capacity. A `blocked` run, one waiting on an owner ask, is not ticked (schedule_runtime.py:170). CompanySupervisor.tick short-circuits on blocked before planning or judging (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:182), so no step is spent. The only deadline on a work run is a budget bound: once passed, the run is exhausted (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:541). It is not a 'wait until' barrier. RUN_STATUSES has no waiting state. Judgement (agents/core/autonomy/work_judge.py:67) is pass/fail only and has no `wait` verdict. No background-process registry exists for a judge to see. Tests tests/test_schedule_runtime.py, tests/test_company_supervisor.py and tests/test_work_run_ledger.py pass and cover the blocked skip and deadline exhaustion.
reviews.remaining:
All three accepted barrier kinds are missing from the work-run ledger and supervisor: wait on a pid until the process exits, wait on a registered session or trigger until it fires, and wait until a wall-clock time. The mechanics around them are also missing:
- No short-circuit in ScheduleRuntime.due or CompanySupervisor.tick while a barrier is active, which would skip without a tick, a plan, a step or a judge call.
- No `wait` verdict or action that a planner or judge can return to set a barrier.
- The judge gets no live background-process list.
- No stale-barrier clearing: a dead pid, a fired trigger or an elapsed deadline should clear the barrier on the next check so it cannot wedge the run.

reviews.summary: The review engine exists; the on-demand, focused command does not. BackgroundReviewer (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:138) is a per-turn learning distiller. It makes one structured, strict-local LLM call (the backend is router.local_backend, agents/core/orchestrator.py:993) over a snapshot of recent history. It proposes user and agent core facts (injection-scanned), corrections, new skills through the quarantine pipeline, and skill patches as pending proposals plus an ActionApprovalQueue request. It runs as a separate call, so the live session is not mutated. The reviewer is spawned after each completed turn by _spawn_background_review (orchestrator.py:3015) and _background_review_task (orchestrator.py:3037). Spawning is gated on cognition.review_enabled and throttled by should_run (background_review.py:173), a cadence plus daily-budget gate. Results are only logged and exposed read-only via GET /api/cognition/learning (agents/core/cognition/api.py:68). The manual triggers that exist are POST /api/reflection/run (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:278), which forces the nightly reflection pass, and POST /api/learning/propose, both with HUD buttons. Neither reviews the current conversation. Tests tests/test_background_review.py, tests/test_review_strict_local.py and tests/test_daily_reflection.py pass.
reviews.remaining:
The `/refine [focus]` equivalent is missing:
- There is no chat command, route or HUD control that runs the memory/skill review now, against a snapshot of the current conversation.
- BackgroundReviewer.run (background_review.py:195) takes no focus argument and the prompt has no focus slot.
- There is no refusal while a turn is in flight in that session. The marker exists (Orchestrator.turn_lease's per-session lock), but /refine does not consult it, and a plain lock check would also refuse the command's own turn, which already holds that session's lease; the check has to exclude the caller's held lease.
- The new or updated memories and skill proposals are not reported back into the chat. They only go to the log and /api/cognition/learning.
- The only snapshot is the last 6 turns truncated to 300 characters each, taken per turn. There is no whole-conversation snapshot on demand.

reviews.summary: No implementer→reviewer review state exists anywhere in the work model. TaskStatus (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:76) is proposed, approved, running, blocked, done, failed, rejected, deferred or quarantined. The strict transition table (queue.py:96) has no review edge. MissionStatus (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:49) is planned, active, paused, done, failed or cancelled. Work-run RUN_STATUSES (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:68) have no review or changes-requested state either. agents/core/routers/review.py is an output-quality queue (/api/review/flag at review.py:34, vote, add-to-dataset), not a work handoff. The decision inbox offers a one-party approve/edit/reject/defer on a single task. None of these units has an assignee or reviewer, and none has a claim to guard, which is the missing board of row H466. A grep for request_review, request_changes, reopen_review, changes_requested and kanban over agents/ and frontend/src returns nothing. The existing queue tests pass (tests/test_autonomy_queue.py, tests/test_h10_25_review_queue.py).
reviews.remaining:
Every accepted part is missing:
- A `review` status that is explicitly not a block, so ready-queue accounting does not count it as blocked.
- request-review, with an optional reassign-to-reviewer and a recorded summary plus structured handoff metadata.
- request-changes, the reviewer's verdict: it returns the item to its implementer with concrete required changes recorded as an event and a comment.
- reopen-review.
- A live-claim guard that refuses to move a running, claimed item without force.
- Entry points for all of the above: routes, CLI or HUD controls.

reviews.summary: The delivery foundation exists, but it only carries approval decision cards; nothing subscribes a chat to a work item's completion. EscalationRouter (agents/core/autonomy/escalation.py:96) is a governed, allowlisted, contract-bounded multi-channel fan-out. AwayNotifier (escalation.py:142) adds presence-aware routing through OwnerPresence (agents/core/autonomy/presence.py:104). AutonomyWorker._maybe_push (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:857) pushes under the daily interrupt budget (INTERRUPT_BUDGET_PER_DAY at worker.py:44, InterruptBudget over the attention ledger) and uses is_night_window (worker.py:78). These tests pass: tests/test_h12_11_escalation.py, tests/test_h34_2_presence.py and tests/test_autonomy_worker.py. When a task finishes, the worker only transitions it to DONE and audits (worker.py:970). No listener or subscription fires on terminal task, work-run or mission events. A grep for notify_subscribe, last_event_id and subscription in agents/core/autonomy returns nothing relevant.
reviews.remaining:
The completion subscription itself is missing:
- No way to subscribe a chat (platform, chat_id, optional thread) to a work item's terminal events (task done/failed, work run succeeded/failed/exhausted/stopped, mission done/failed).
- No delivery modes notify, notify+wake or wake. In wake mode the agent should be woken in that chat to read the full context and answer in its own voice, spending interrupt budget and respecting is_night_window.
- No per-subscription last_event_id cursor advanced transactionally, so a restarted notifier would have no way to avoid re-notifying.
- No auto-subscribe of the creating chat.
- No 30-day pruning of finished subscriptions.
- No entry point: no command, route or HUD control.

reviews.summary: H477 re-reviewed against live code on 2026-09-18; the inherited 2026-09-07 "missing" verdict is wrong and last night's "already equivalent" triage is also wrong. Nerva does have a real capability-discovery surface, under /api/* not /v1/*: GET /api/capabilities (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:243, user_guard) returns capability_registry.snapshot() (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:503), whose build_records() (:475) merges seven sources — _missing_records (:189), _plugin_records (:127), _action_records (:231, every ACTION_CAPABILITY_MANIFESTS kind joined to kernel/registry.ACTION_REGISTRY), _acquired_records (:425), _tool_records (:310), _component_records (:359), _skill_records (:390) — each record carrying inputs/risk/requires/supports/verification/rollback plus a missing→seam→wired→verified→ga readiness state Hermes has no analogue for; GET /api/metrics/capabilities (analytics.py:227) is the open legacy twin. Skills enumerate at GET /skills (routers/skills.py:29) and /skills/imported (:333); tools at GET /api/toolrpc/tools (routers/mesh.py:170, from ToolRPCServer.tools(), tool_rpc.py:283 — a surface the triage missed); health at GET /healthz (routers/ops.py:42) + GET /readyz (:137) + GET /api/health/components (routers/status.py:65) + /status (:76) + /api/status (:108). Tests pin it: 95 passed, 1 skipped (the IPv6-stack case at tests/test_h2311_operability.py:758) across tests/test_capability_registry.py (11), test_capability_readiness_matrix.py (6), test_h27_capability_verification.py (11), test_route_auth_matrix.py (5), test_h2311_operability.py (38 + 1 skipped), test_hud_v2_parity.py (13), test_endpoints.py (11); the count moved from the 80 of 2026-09-18 because #1168 (+10) and #1177 (+5) added probe_bind port-diagnosis tests to test_h2311_operability.py — #1177's two additions pin serve.py's EACCES arm (the privileged-port sentence only below 1024, a symptom-plus-remedy message at or above it, exit 13 either way) and touch none of the discovery or health endpoints above. Re-checked on main at 6578cd3c after #1187 and #1188: the only cited file they touched is agents/web.py, where five added lines of Telegram pairing wiring in the lifespan shifted the ChatRequest, reasoning_scope, POST /chat and GET /v1 citations five lines later; no discovery, health, skills, toolset or model-routing surface changed, and the seven suites still give 95 passed, 1 skipped. Re-checked on the HEQ lot-1 head (origin/hermes/heq-lot1 at cbe66ce5): its agents/web.py change (H691 forwarded-proto middleware, the lifespan's trusted-proxy announce, a rate-limit exemption keyed on the real client host) moved the ChatRequest, POST /chat, reasoning_scope and GET /v1 citations 56 lines later and touched no discovery, health, skills, toolset or model-routing surface; H583's OpenRouter upstream-provider settings are global and leave ChatRequest unchanged. The seven suites give 94 passed, 2 skipped there: the extra skip is the EACCES privilege-drop case (tests/test_h2311_operability.py:602), whose uid-65534 child could not import serve from a checkout under a 0700 sandbox path, a premise skip rather than a failure. But it is not equivalent. Within the row's own narrowed scope ("copy the discovery half only"), /v1/toolsets has no counterpart — /api/capabilities lists individual tools, never toolset groups; the only group catalogue is job_toolsets.CATALOG (basic/files/terminal) exposed inside admin-guarded GET /api/jobs/doctor (autonomy/jobs_health.py:116) and scoped to jobs — and /api/capabilities answers "what can the agent do" while Hermes' /v1/capabilities also answers "what does this API support" (features/endpoints/auth/session-header/idempotency/browser-control contract), a block Nerva has nowhere; /openapi.json is served open and covers the endpoint list only incidentally. Outside that scope, four rolled-up children were never checked by the triage and three are absent: no browser-control registration at all (rg over agents/ for browser_control|controller_id|extension_control returns nothing; browser_transport.py is SSRF resolver pinning for in-process Chromium, not an external controller), no platform-event normalization (rg reaction|message_edited over agents/ hits only food-diary prose in agents/frigga/HEARTBEAT.md and agents/frigga/SOUL.md, no code; POST /api/channels/{id}/inbound is message ingress), and no per-request model/provider override (ChatRequest, agents/web.py:972, is extra="forbid" and takes only agent/reasoning/session_id — the reasoning third of the clause is satisfied via reasoning_scope at web.py:1148, model_routes precedence is not). POST /v1/chat/completions and POST /v1/responses are out of scope by the row's own rationale and governance note, not gaps: Nerva's governed chat is POST /chat (web.py:1119) through the kernel/session/approval path, which is what the row requires of any façade. Side note for whoever builds this: GET /v1 is already the legacy HUD HTML (web.py:1081), so a future /v1/* API namespace must be reconciled with it.
reviews.remaining:
Discovery half (the row's own scope), still owed: (1) a `/v1/toolsets` equivalent — `GET /api/capabilities` and `GET /api/toolrpc/tools` enumerate individual tools only; the toolset groups in `agents/core/job_toolsets.py` CATALOG (basic/files/terminal, with `available`) are reachable only inside admin-guarded `GET /api/jobs/doctor` (`agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:116`) and are jobs-scoped, not the agent's platform toolsets with `enabled`/`configured`/expanded `tools`; (2) the API-surface half of `/v1/capabilities` — `snapshot()` (`agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:503`) returns no `features`/`endpoints`/`auth`/`session-header`/idempotency/protocol-version block, so an external UI cannot feature-detect the server; `/openapi.json` partly covers the endpoint list but is not declared a stable client contract anywhere in docs/.

Rolled-up children with no Nerva surface at all: `.api-browser-control` — no `POST /v1/browser-control/register`, no single-use TTL ticket, no controller websocket, no server-side controller capability allowlist (`rg 'browser_control|controller_id|extension_control'` over agents/ returns nothing; `agents/core/browser_transport.py` is SSRF resolver pinning for in-process Chromium); `.api-platform-events` — no normalization of platform-native reactions/edits (`rg 'reaction|message_edited|platform_event'` over agents/ returns no code, only food-diary prose in agents/frigga/*.md; `POST /api/channels/{channel_id}/inbound` is message ingress).

Partially satisfied children: `.api-model-routing` — `ChatRequest` (`agents/web.py:972`) is `extra="forbid"` and accepts only `agent`/`reasoning`/`session_id`, so per-request `model`/`provider` and `model_routes` alias precedence (including the 400-on-provider-conflict rule) do not exist; only the `reasoning` override is governed and live (`agents/web.py:1148`). `.api-models` — no `/api/model/options` provider-aware picker payload with refresh/cache-bust semantics; `/api/models/local` and `/api/models/info` (`agents/core/routers/models_llm.py`) are both behind `admin_guard`. `.api-artifacts` — `agents/core/routers/artifact_store.py` is bounded, quota'd and guarded, but performs no server-side SHA-256 digest validation and binds no artifact to the scope that created it.

Out of scope by the row's own rationale, not gaps: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (explicitly refused) and `POST /v1/responses` (same chat-façade family; any façade must re-enter the governed `POST /chat` path at `agents/web.py:1119`).

Namespace note for the build: `GET /v1` is already the legacy HUD HTML (`agents/web.py:1081`), so a `/v1/*` API prefix has to be reconciled with it or the discovery surface stays on `/api/*`.

reviews.summary: The inbound half exists with the governed posture. A2ARegistry (agents/core/a2a.py) allowlists peers and returns each peer's HMAC secret only once (add_peer / list_peers / remove_peer). receive_task (agents/core/a2a.py:224) checks the signature over the raw body in constant time, runs the a2a.inbound contract and parks every verified task in a bounded pending inbox. decide (agents/core/a2a.py:262) only flips the status ('Approval does NOT execute it'); test_decide_is_terminal_and_does_not_execute pins this. In agents/core/routers/a2a.py, POST /api/a2a/task stays off unless JARVIS_A2A_ENABLED is set, and peer CRUD and inbox decide are admin-guarded. Both have HUD callers: peer add/remove at frontend/src/gap.tsx:1648 and inbox approve/reject at frontend/src/gap.tsx:1744. NodeMesh.dispatch (agents/core/node_mesh.py:134, POST /api/nodes/{id}/dispatch in agents/core/routers/mesh.py) is kernel-mediated (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:34). It only enqueues an ask-tier task for a node client, and none exists.
reviews.remaining: Nothing sends outbound. Peer records store no endpoint, and no code signs a task and POSTs it to another machine's /api/a2a/task, so this box has no `peer dm` equivalent. An approved inbound task has no execution path: decide only changes the status, no turn runs and no reply reaches the sender. The accepted async handle is missing: there is no start/status/stop for an approved remote turn and no peer-authenticated status/result poll. Without them the sender cannot collect a result without holding a connection open. The row depends on H476 (Runs API), which is itself partial. Any execution must stay behind owner approval and node.dispatch/kernel mediation, and no peer-side grant may skip the pending inbox.

reviews.summary: `nerva send` trimite un mesaj către o destinație configurată fără apel de model, cu corpul rezolvat ca la Hermes: argumentul MESSAGE, altfel `-f PATH` (`-` citește stdin), altfel ce e legat pe stdin — un terminal nu e citit niciodată, nici cu `-f -`; un stdin închis e eroare de utilizare, nu traceback; se citește cel mult limita plus un caracter, iar un BOM UTF-8 e eliminat. `-s LINE` e un subiect pe o singură linie *imprimabilă* (orice caracter de control sau separator de linie Unicode e refuzat), purtat de ntfy ca titlu nativ — ASCII imprimabil, cel mult 120, refuzat cu motiv în loc să fie trunchiat tacit de adaptor — și de celelalte canale ca prima linie (subiect, linie goală, mesaj — forma Hermes); `-q` nu tipărește nimic la succes; `--list CANAL` filtrează țintele: un nume care nu poate fi canal direct-send e eroare de utilizare decisă offline, iar un canal pe care un hub mai vechi nu-l listează e exit 1 cu ce listează numit; un argument MESSAGE gol înseamnă „fără mesaj” și cade pe `--file`/stdin. Scara de ieșire e declarată în `--help`: 0 trimis · 1 nelivrat (hub-ul a refuzat sau transportul a eșuat) · 2 utilizare · 3 fără hub · 4 neautorizat. Un fișier binar la `-f` e refuzat cu îndrumarea pentru atașamente, fără să-i reflecte octeții; limita de 4.000 de caractere e regula seam-ului (`carried_length`: subiectul contează unde devine prima linie, nu la ntfy) și CLI-ul aplică aceeași regulă înainte de orice cerere; șirurile venite de la hub sau tastate sunt curățate de caractere de control înainte de terminal. `POST /api/channels/send` primește `subject` opțional (o linie, ≤200), iar seam-ul outbound aplică limita la ce se livrează efectiv. Rate-limit-ul și înregistrarea în IntentLog rămân pe drum. O recenzie adversarială independentă a găsit cincisprezece probleme (două majore: două pin-uri existente din `tests/test_nerva_send.py` rupte), toate remediate în același PR, fiecare cu test.
reviews.remaining: Atașamentele `MEDIA:<path>` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: `nerva send` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare `platform:chat_id[:thread]` / `platform:#canal` ca la Hermes: `--channel telegram` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața `--file`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul `hermes send:`. `JobRunner._send` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false.

reviews.summary: **The variant-expansion half of the row.** `hardline_match` no longer screens one spelling: the old single-pass body becomes `_scan_one`, and the public function screens the command in every spelling `_detection_variants` yields — as given, unwrapped from a shell wrapper (`_shell_c_payloads`, recursively to `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH = 2`), and de-obfuscated (intra-word quotes and escapes collapsed, so `mk""fs` reads as `mkfs`), type-preserving so an argv stays an argv. A non-string command is materialised ONCE up front, which fixes a real one-shot-iterator drain that turned `hardline_match(iter(["rm","-rf","/"]))` from a refusal into a miss. The original slice changed nothing in HARDLINE or the contract, so that pass was additive: an 80,000-case differential fuzz against the pre-slice module returned `refusals_cleared_by_slice = 0`. **That invariant no longer describes the module after PR #1177** (re-assessed 2026-09-19 against the diff 1c5054ea→494a13b2): HARDLINE itself changed — `_CMD` and `network_to_shell` now carry a `_PATH_PREFIX`, so a command word and any wrapper in front of it are read by basename (`/sbin/mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda`, `/usr/bin/sudo /sbin/mkfs.ext4`, `curl … | /bin/sh` all refuse where they returned None; `_recursive_root_removal` compares basenames through `_command_name` too, so `['/usr/local/bin/rm','-rf','/']` refuses instead of only the two literal `/bin/rm` spellings) — and #1177 clears refusals in BOTH directions. Two false-positive classes are cleared on purpose (a `case` label; a heredoc body that quotes a catastrophe), and #1177's mechanisms for them ALSO cleared TRUE refusals the pre-#1177 module gave — **both closed by this slice (H481, branch `hermes/h481-cleared-refusals`, 2026-09-22).** `_strip_case_labels` acted on the flat text of any `case…esac` span and its first-label rule fired after any word-initial `in`, so `(echo case in; reboot); echo esac` — which /bin/sh, dash and bash all execute — went `power_cycle`→None, and the `$IFS`-spliced `(echo case in; mkfs.ext4$IFS/dev/sda); echo esac` / `wipefs$IFS-a$IFS/dev/sda` went mkfs/wipefs→None; the strip now fires only inside a real command-position `case WORD in … esac` region (a `case` keyword, confirmed per match by `_in_command_position`), so all three refuse again — and, made symmetric, a single-line `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` refuses through the segment path too while `case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` still does not. `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` looked only LEFT of `<<`, so `cat <<EOF | sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` and `cat <<'EOF' >x.sh; sh x.sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` went `recursive_root_removal`→None although both hand the body to a shell that runs it; it now also reads the heredoc's own pipeline stages AFTER the redirection and a file the body is written to that a shell later runs, so those refuse, while `bash <<EOF` and a heredoc written to a plain file (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'`) are unchanged. Each shape was reproduced against /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash first (harmless `echo RAN` stand-ins) and pinned red-first. **An independent review of that closure found nine items — three blocking, three major, two minor, one nit — and all nine are fixed in the same branch, each reproduced against the three shells first:** (1) the rewritten `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` counted a shell UPSTREAM of the heredoc's pipe stage (`bash -c echo | cat <<EOF` was `power_cycle` although every shell prints the literal body); (2) it took ANY word of a later shell statement as the run file (`cat > x.yaml <<'EOF'` / `shutdown: graceful` / `EOF` / `bash run.sh x.yaml` was `power_cycle` — the exact config case the heredoc-as-data rule exists for); (3) it read an `xargs`-reached shell as a consumer (`cat <<EOF | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rm -f {}'` with a `reboot.log` line was `power_cycle`; xargs hands lines to the shell as arguments); (4) `_in_command_position` read the compact `if true;then case $1 in` as the word `true;then`, skipped the strip and refused the label (`;then case` / `;do case` were `power_cycle`, label-only in every shell); (5) the new `_CASE_BLOCK_RE` (`\bcase\s+WORD\s+.*?\bin\b.*?\besac\b`) was super-linear on ordinary prose — 4000 chars of case/in prose 10 → 531 ms, eight argv items of it 0.28 → 128 s; (6) the redirect-target branch re-tokenised every later line for every heredoc — 400 `cat <<E >x` blocks in 4000 chars 25 → 2,471 ms, 33.6 KB 109 ms → 97.5 s; the first pass's '78.7 → 78.4 ms' held only for input with no `case` word and never entered that branch; (7) the named-shell file-exec claim was overstated: `(sh x.sh)`, `{ sh x.sh; }`, `if true; then sh x.sh; fi`, `cat x.sh | sh`, `sh -c '. x.sh'`, `. x.sh`, `source x.sh`, `tee x.sh <<EOF; sh x.sh` and a quoted `> "x.sh"` target all ran the body and returned None; (8) this row still said 'eleven across two reviews'; (9) the report said 11 items were red before the fix when 12 were, and the `case WORD in` tightening was pinned by nothing. Fixes: the consumer test looks only at the heredoc's own stage and the stages downstream of it, and a stage counts only when its shell reads its stdin as the script (`_interpreter_call`: a `-c` line, a file operand and an `xargs`-reached shell are data — unless the `-c` line itself launches a stdin-reading shell, so `bash -c sh <<EOF`, `sh -c 'eval "$(cat)"' <<EOF` and `sh -c '. /dev/stdin' <<EOF` still refuse, verified); the file test looks only at the operand a shell RUNS (`_script_runs`: `sh x`, `. x`, `source x`, the same behind `(`/`{`/`then`, a file piped into a stdin-reading shell, a `-c` line that runs it), collects `tee` operands and quoted targets, and the statement lines after a heredoc are tokenised once, lazily, shared across heredocs and decided last heredoc first; the `case` region is found by three single-purpose searches (`case WORD `, then the first `in`, then the first `esac`), each starting where the last stopped, and the keyword-before test accepts the compact `;then`/`;do`. A 671,995-case differential fuzz against origin/main (the suite's 275 pinned literals recombined with 14 statement prefixes, 10 suffixes, 17 heredoc heads, 13 pipe tails, 4 upstream stages, 18 same-line and 10 later-line follow-ups, plus 60,000 seeded-random recombinations) returns refusals_added = 55,059 and refusals_cleared = 22,304 — so the first pass's 'refusals_cleared = 0' is withdrawn, not restated. Every cleared case is explained by one of the two changed mechanisms and belongs to a class no shell executes, each verified with `echo RAN` stand-ins: 19,311 by the consumer rule — a heredoc redirected into a shell that carries its own script or `-c` line, or into `xargs sh` (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`; main refused both, every shell prints the body) — and 2,993 by the command-position rule — `case` used as an ARGUMENT followed by `label) …` (`echo case $1 in`, `x=1 case …`, `sudo case …`: a parse error in every shell) or a `case … esac` quoted inside heredoc DATA, where main's unconditional strip put a `;` in place of `in label)` and so invented a command position the shell does not have (disabling main's strip makes every one of them None on main too). Every added refusal is explained by the same two mechanisms (33,619 consumer, 21,434 command position, 6 in garbage recombinations with unbalanced quotes reached through the de-obfuscated variant) and adds an executing shape of the kind pinned in the tests. Two false refusals main had are therefore cleared on purpose and pinned as such (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`). The cleared classes are still cleared on purpose: a `case` label (`case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` was `power_cycle`; `_strip_case_labels` drops the pattern inside `case … esac` while keeping the branch body a command position, so `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` still refuses) and a heredoc body that merely quotes a catastrophe (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'` / `rm -rf / will destroy the box` / `EOF` was `recursive_root_removal` because `segments` ignored the body flag `text` honoured; a body line is now narrowed to its `$()`/backtick substitutions via `_substituted`, so `cat <<EOF` / `$(rm -rf /)` / `EOF` still refuses). **An independent review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed here, and every one was reproduced against a real shell first.** **(1)** The payload was taken as the token immediately after the first `-c`-shaped flag, and the search then stopped — but a shell keeps parsing options until the first non-option operand. `/bin/sh -c -x 'echo RAN'` runs, and `sh -c -x 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'`, `sh -c -- 'rm -rf /'`, `sh -c -e …`, `sh -c -u …` and `sudo sh -c -- 'wipefs -a /dev/sda'` all returned None. One decoy character defeated the entire mechanism, reachable end to end at the transport's spawn seam. The scan steps over options to the first operand now, `--` included. **(2)** A `sh -c` payload is a shell SCRIPT, and a newline separates statements exactly as `;` does — but the newline was squeezed into a space before segmentation, so nothing ever occupied a command position on line 2 and `sh -c 'echo hi` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'` passed the floor. **Pressing Enter was the bypass.** Unquoted newlines are separators now, quote-aware so a newline inside a string literal stays data and ordinary prose is not screened as a command. #1177 closed the way that screening could be switched off again: any `<<` opened a heredoc and an unmatched delimiter swallowed every following line as body, so `grep "<<<<<<< HEAD" src/x.py` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` returned None; `_heredoc_open` is now quote- and `$(( ))`-aware, skips `<<<` here-strings, and a delimiter that never comes back opens nothing. **(3)** `_CMD`'s command-position anchor learned four more shapes a shell steps over, each a live miss: a brace group (`{ mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda; }`), a compound-command keyword (`if true; then mkfs.ext4 …`), an assignment prefix (`FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …`) and `env FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …` — and, with #1177, a fifth: a directory prefix on the command word or on any wrapper before it, spelled as deterministic `component/` chunks with `=` excluded so `FOO=/sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an assignment and `echo /sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an argument. **(4)** `busybox` was named as a shell but not as a command-position wrapper, so `busybox mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` — the standard shape on exactly the container targets this module says it keeps the floor on — walked straight through. Four documentation claims were corrected rather than left standing, including the one that said the known-gap list was complete (the first review found five entries missing from it; #1177's second review found six more — a re-expansion budget filled with decoys, a path in front of the command word, a `<<` that opens no heredoc, a heredoc a shell reads as a script, a heredoc body screened as argv, and a `case` label — so the docstring now says twenty-two across four reviews) and the one that said an over-matched flag shape can never clear a refusal (it could: `powershell /c -Command Stop-Computer` returned None where `powershell -Command Stop-Computer` refused — fixed by the same change as (1)). A test whose NAME promised a bound on work it never measured was renamed to what it actually pins, which is the opposite: that depth-3 nesting is a deliberate miss (`test_nesting_past_the_depth_cap_is_a_miss_and_that_is_the_pin`, still present and green). **#1177 also removed the only breadth cap:** `_MAX_SHELL_EXPANSIONS = 8` bounded how many level-1 payloads were unwrapped again, in encounter order — an order the caller writes — so eight cheap `sh -c ok;` decoys in front of `sh -c "sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'"` returned None where seven refused, and padding a payload past `MAX_ARG_CHARS` had the same effect; every payload is now re-expanded and `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH` is the only cap, with breadth bounded by the fact that each level's payloads are disjoint substrings of the level above. And the heredoc-as-data rule from the earlier review gained the exception it was missing: `bash <<EOF`, `sh <<'EOF'`, `bash -s <<EOF` and `cat x | sh <<EOF` hand the body to a shell that RUNS it, and `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` now keeps those lines as statements (`bash <<EOF` / `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` / `EOF` was None). All 303 tests in tests/test_local_transport.py pass (up from 206 on the #1177 module: 18 items for the two closures and 54 from the review round, which pin eleven false-refusal shapes and three own-stage data shapes as None, fourteen file-exec spellings, seven payload-launched-shell shapes and four downstream stdin-reading shells as refusals, the compact `;then case` (four), the `case WORD in` opener, four disclosed gaps as still-misses, and six wall-clock bounds two orders of magnitude above the fixed cost; every fix was neutered once — thirteen mutations, each turning its test red). Measured 2026-09-22. **Second adversarial pass (2026-09-22, round two).** A bypass hunter ran 64 shapes under /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash with a PATH-shim stand-in that touches a sentinel and found three the floor cleared while every shell (or bash alone) ran the body: a subshell as the final pipe stage with no `;` (`cat <<EOF | (sh)`, `( sh )`, `(exec sh)` — `_stage_words` left the trailing `)` and `_interpreter_call` read `sh` as running a script named `)`), a `<<<` here-string into a stdin-reading shell (`sh <<< reboot`, `cat <<< reboot | sh` — `_heredoc_open` skipped `<<<` as having no body and nothing modelled the WORD), and a heredoc opened inside a `<(...)` process substitution a leading `source`/shell runs (`source <(cat <<EOF …)`, `sh <(…)`). All three refuse now: `_stage_words` drops trailing group closers, `_herestring_scripts` screens a here-string WORD (dequoted) when its own or a downstream stage is a stdin shell, and `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` gains the process-substitution case; each pinned red-first with the exact bytes. The `_detection_variants` disclosure that the pipe machinery "misses two more pipe shapes" was an undercount and is corrected; the six disclosed gaps that remain (bare `./x.sh`, a variable-carried name, `BASH_ENV`, a heredoc inside `$( )`, `xargs -I{} sh -c '{}'`, `| (cd /tmp; sh)`) were each confirmed to execute exactly as disclosed.

reviews.summary: The durable, multi-surface half is in place. Blocked tasks survive restarts in the SQLite TaskQueue. They are decided from the HUD (POST /autonomy/tasks/{id}/decision in agents/core/routers/autonomy.py, called from frontend/src/gap.tsx), from Telegram buttons (DECISION_ACTIONS and build_decision_card in agents/core/autonomy/inbox.py:21 and :31) and from the CLI (`nerva approvals accept|reject|defer|edit` in agents/cli/nerva.py). ActionApprovalQueue.await_decision (agents/core/autonomy/action_approvals.py:89) returns 'timeout' separately from 'rejected' (:105). BrowserAgent passes that status back as the step reason (agents/core/browser_agent.py:231-233). PendingRequests.classify (agents/core/autonomy/pending_requests.py:176) never turns silence into approval. None of the three accepted gaps is closed. (a) No surface accepts a free-text reason. AutonomyDecisionBody (agents/core/routers/autonomy.py:143-145) has only action and payload. The worker's reject branch (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:1127-1130) records only decision='reject'. ActionApprovalQueue.decide (agents/core/autonomy/action_approvals.py:74) takes only a boolean. (b) No coalescing: ActionApprovalQueue.request (:41) mints a fresh uuid for every call, and identical governed tasks each get their own card. (c) A timeout never marks the item expired. The item stays 'pending' in the HUD, and a late approve records 'approved' for an action whose waiter already gave up. Chat-turn tool calls get only reason='approval_required' (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:385); no later rejected or expired result is sent back to the model.
reviews.remaining: (a) Add an optional, bounded (≤280 chars) human reason to a reject on every surface: the HUD body, the Telegram reject flow, `nerva approvals reject --reason`, and ActionApprovalQueue.decide. Store it on the task or item and pass it verbatim into the model-visible result: the browser step reason, the PendingRequests 'refused' step detail, and the tool result. (b) Coalesce identical pending asks, same agent, tool or kind, and canonical args/fingerprint, onto one leader card, and fan the leader's decision out to every waiter. (c) Persist a distinct 'expired' state when an await times out, so the HUD stops offering it and a late approve cannot flip it. Surface 'expired, unanswered' separately from 'rejected by <who>' in the model-visible result.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no single switch that neutralizes all owner customization. A grep for safe-mode, clean-boot or diagnostic-mode spellings across agents/, scripts/, frontend/src/, mobile/src/ and desktop/ finds no real hit (only a safeModelId helper in the frontend), and the `nerva` CLI (agents/cli/nerva.py) has no such flag. Each extension point loads unconditionally or behind its own flag. Persona resolution prefers the data-home and repo SOUL.local.md overlays (soul_path_for, agents/core/agent.py:374), and that persona is now also re-read mid-session: Agent.refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:513) re-resolves the same overlay at every context-compaction commit (H672), so a later safe mode has two SOUL entry points to honour. Skills are discovered at boot (agents/core/orchestrator.py:971). The MCP manager is wired in the orchestrator (agents/core/orchestrator.py:60). agents/core/file_tools.py does not inject instruction files: it classifies writes to them (SOUL/AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/HEARTBEAT, their .local overlays, .cursorrules) as their own approval class. At runtime Nerva reads the SOUL overlay above and HEARTBEAT.local.md, whose front-matter becomes cron-scheduled agent runs (agents/core/heartbeat.py); that front-matter is now injection-scanned and a flagged file is refused, but a clean owner overlay still wins over the shipped template with no switch to ignore it. Nothing in agents/ loads AGENTS.md or .cursorrules into a prompt. Plugins, memory recall and the WorldView graph each have their own flags. agents/core/product_posture.py composes intelligence flags upward only; it has no 'everything off' position. enforce_boot_posture (agents/core/boot_guards.py:324) is where such a posture would be enforced, and agents/core/env_config.py is the flag layer it would be read from.
reviews.remaining: Add one safe-mode switch: a JARVIS_SAFE_MODE env flag plus a `--safe-mode` launch option. When it is set, every customization extension point skips itself: SOUL/HEARTBEAT .local overlays fall back to the shipped templates (in soul_path_for, so both Agent._load_soul and the compaction-boundary Agent.refresh_soul honour it, and in the heartbeat loader), and any instruction-file injection a later change adds honours the switch; installed skills and marketplace skills are not loaded; plugins, MCP servers, shell hooks and outbound webhooks are off; memory recall and WorldView context injection are off; runtime-settings autonomy overrides fall back to the built-in approval defaults. Credentials in .env stay loaded. The mode is reported in /api/security/posture, logged at boot and shown in the HUD, so the owner knows they are in a reduced posture. It must never loosen any gate.

reviews.summary: The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests at landing. **#1177 (2026-09-19) closed a log-integrity hole inside this same control, re-assessed here rather than refreshed:** the in-place path used to give up and flatten the record to `msg`/`()` whenever a secret straddled the boundary between the format string and an argument ("correctness beats shape"), and flattening is exactly what DELETES a uvicorn access line — `AccessFormatter` unpacks five `record.args`, raises on an empty tuple, and `Handler.handleError` swallows it. `password_assignment`'s `\s*[=:]\s*` jumps the space uvicorn's `'%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` puts between the request path and `HTTP/`, so `/login?pwd=` is inert on its own — 11 characters, so the 10-char floor does not even apply; `password_assignment` needs at least six unquoted (four quoted) non-space characters after the separator and the bare argument has none — and a match once rendered: any unauthenticated client could erase its own access-log entry by appending `?pwd=` to a path. `SecretRedactionFilter._mask_joined_args` now replaces whole arguments — one at a time first, then cumulatively for a secret assembled from several — the cumulative pass can also mask an innocent argument that sits between two culprits (`"%s HTTP/%s and %s HTTP/%s"` with two `?pwd=` paths loses the `1.1` between them): over-redaction, never a leak, and the arity still holds — — until the re-rendered line is scanner-clean, keeping the tuple's arity, putting an argument back when its conversion refuses the mask (uvicorn's `%d` status code stays an int), and naming the mask after the pattern the scanner reports, `[REDACTED:straddling_secret]` when it cannot. Flattening survives only for a straddle no masking can clean, i.e. the secret sits in the format string itself (`pwd=%s`). Seven tests were added — four of them through uvicorn's real `dictConfig` plus `setup_logging()`, asserting the access line for `/login?pwd=`, `/admin?password=`, `/x?passwd:` and `/z?api_key="12345678` survives with the straddling text gone (three are `password_assignment` straddles; `/z?api_key="12345678` is `generic_api_key` matching `api_key="12345678 HTTP/1.1"`, the access line's own closing quote completing the quoted value) and the client, verb and status kept — and the earlier straddle test was inverted to assert `args == ("[REDACTED:anthropic_key]",)` instead of `()`. `agents/core/log.py` did not change and still installs the filter from `setup_logging()`. `tests/test_log_redaction.py` collects 64 tests, all green on 2026-09-19. Nothing in #1177 touches the other six paths the row names; the still-owed list below stands.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses. **A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:** the scanner's `high_entropy_secret` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under `-n auto --dist loadfile` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as `truncated: [REDACTED:high_entropy_secret].md`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, `setup_logging()` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: `agents/run.py` calls `setup_logging()` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; `agents/web.py` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in `tests/conftest.py` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by `isinstance` and silently did nothing: `agents/` is on `sys.path`, so `core.security.log_redaction` and `agents.core.security.log_redaction` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct `SecretRedactionFilter` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed.

reviews.summary: **Gap (a) of four, plus the row's `chmod 0600 atomic writes` clause.** Both pairing credentials stop being written in the clear: `SenderPairing._code` becomes `_code_hash`, and each deeplink entry moves from being keyed by its raw token to being keyed by an opaque 8-byte id with the token's salted digest inside the entry. Verification hashes the candidate and `hmac.compare_digest`s two fixed-length hex digests, so neither the length nor any prefix of the stored credential leaks and the deeplink failure reasons stay indistinguishable. A one-time migration accepts a pre-H497 plaintext file, rehashes it in memory and rewrites it, preserving each link's channel, `created_at` and `expires_at` — an upgrade never locks the owner out nor resurrects a spent link. `_digest` encodes with `surrogatepass` so a lone surrogate (from a hand-edited store, or from the body of the one pairing route a stranger is meant to reach) misses instead of raising. `atomic_write_json` lands every JsonStore file owner-only. **The review found three false claims and all three are corrected — two of them by changing the code rather than the prose.** (1) The module docstring said the store "holds nothing that can pair anybody". True of a 192-bit deeplink token; **false of the pairing code**, which is whatever the owner typed: a four-digit code was recovered from the file by exhausting 10,000 candidates in **0.006 s** and then used to pair. The code is now stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 240,000 rounds, `kdf` and `rounds` stored beside each digest so raising the count later cannot lock an owner out, and a record written by the first cut is upgraded in place on the next successful pair — the one moment the plaintext is in hand — while a FAILED guess leaves it untouched. The deeplink token stays on plain SHA-256, deliberately: `redeem_deeplink` hashes once per outstanding link, so a slow hash there is a CPU lever for any stranger sending `/start junk`, and at 192 bits there is nothing for stretching to buy. (2) The salt comment defended leaving the code unstretched by pointing at the store-wide guess budget — an ONLINE control held in memory, which has no bearing on an attacker who has read the file, the exact threat at-rest hashing answers. Rewritten to say what stretching does and does not promise. (3) `atomic_write_json` claimed its chmod-before-replace ordering left no readable window. It left a shorter one: `write_text` creates the tmp at `0o666 & ~umask` and the whole payload is in it before the chmod runs. The tmp is now created EMPTY through a descriptor opened 0600 and closed again (json_store.py:74) before the unchanged `Path.write_text` call at json_store.py:78 opens that existing file — a mode `write_text` leaves alone — so no byte of a pairing digest ever lands in a file whose mode the umask chose; pinned by a test that neutralises `os.chmod` and still requires 0600. **#1179 (adversarial wave two) touched only this row's test file; `pairing.py` and `json_store.py` are byte-identical to the #1171 state.** The review claimed every inbound `/start` costs 240k rounds outside any budget. It does not, for two reasons worth keeping apart. First, `/start` never reaches the code KDF at all: a Telegram `/start <payload>` is routed by `TelegramChannel._maybe_pair_deeplink` (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:486-524) to `redeem_deeplink`, which is one plain-SHA-256 `_digest` per outstanding link, and every other chat message reaches `gate_inbound` through `ChannelGateway.route` with `code=kwargs.get("pairing_code")` (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:82), a kwarg no channel in the tree ever sets — so the one path on which a stranger can spend a KDF run is `POST /api/channels/pairing/request`, the route the new test's docstring names (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:469). Second, on that path the KDF sits behind a budget: `_code_guess_budget_spent` (pairing.py:599) is store-wide and is consulted at pairing.py:580, BEFORE `_code_matches` at pairing.py:585, so a stranger rotating sender ids — the per-sender bucket is keyed on an id the caller chose — buys at most `_MAX_CODE_GUESSES_PER_WINDOW` = 10 KDF runs per 10-minute window however many ids they present, and a request presenting no code never reaches the KDF at all. `test_the_kdf_a_stranger_can_trigger_stays_inside_the_guess_budget` (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:466) now pins that by counting `_stretch` calls rather than timing them, so a slow CI box cannot fail it: 60 requests from 60 fresh ids → 10 runs with 50 turned away `rate_limited` (with the budget check removed it is 60 runs and 0 refusals — re-reproduced at this re-verification), and zero runs for a code-less request. That is the code-side counterpart of the deeplink decision above — the token stays unstretched because nothing budgets `redeem_deeplink`'s per-link compare; the code may be stretched because its compare sits behind one. Nothing in #1179's persona-scan (`agent.py`, `quarantine.py`) or MCP-stdio (`mcp/client.py`) work touches this row. **Second slice (2026-09-22) — one store per process, and the one-use claim made true for the deeplink path.** The module promised a deeplink is "one use, ever", and inside one instance it was; production held two. The orchestrator registers the long-lived `sender_pairing` (the gateway gates on it, the pairing router mints and revokes on it) and `TelegramChannel` was built in `web.py` without one, so `_maybe_pair_deeplink` opened a throwaway `SenderPairing()` per `/start <token>`. A `JsonStore` reads its file once and every save writes the whole in-memory state back, so the two were two stores, not two views of one: a token redeemed over Telegram was spent in the throwaway and still outstanding in the orchestrator's copy, whose next save — any save; a stranger knocking is enough — wrote it back to disk, where the next throwaway redeemed it again and paired a second sender. With a relocated data root the two did not even share a file (the registry spelled a cwd-relative `memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`, the throwaway used `data_path(...)`), so under `JARVIS_HOME` no link ever redeemed. Fixed by wiring, not by hardening the store: `TelegramChannel` takes `pairing=` and `web.py` passes `gateway.pairing`, the same object by identity; an adapter handed nothing refuses to pair rather than building one (same reply as a bad token, a warning naming the cause, the message still swallowed); the registry entry spells the path through `data_path("sender_pairing.json")`. Five tests in `tests/test_telegram_pairing_shared_store.py` pin the resurrection with two instances over one file as the premise, a spent link staying spent after the owner's store saves, `revoke_deeplinks()` reaching the live adapter, an un-wired channel building nothing, and the real lifespan handing the channel `orch.sender_pairing` under the data root; red-proofed against the unpatched sources.
reviews.remaining: **The row names four hardening gaps; (a) is closed, (c) is closed for the deeplink path, (b) and (d) are open.** (c) *revocation reaching live adapters*: `revoke_deeplinks()` and `unpair()` now act on the one object the Telegram adapter redeems from and the gateway consults on every message, so there is no second copy for a link or an approval to survive in — pinned by `test_revoking_on_the_shared_store_reaches_the_live_telegram_adapter`. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) *no lockout after N failed attempts* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) *no admin-vs-user command split on channels*, so any paired sender gets every command; the row wants a split with an always-allowed floor of `{help, whoami}`. **Unaddressed from the Hermes column:** pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via `secrets.choice`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); `unauthorized_dm_behavior` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in `is_allowed`/`gate_inbound`. **Two honest limits of the second slice.** The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (`JARVIS_HOME`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in `<cwd>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). **And the limit carried from the first slice.** Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and **nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types** — `PairingCodeBody` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented.

reviews.summary: The network half is stronger than Hermes. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py:123) refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it. enforce_boot_posture (agents/core/boot_guards.py:324) runs from the app lifespan, together with fail-closed parse checks; HEQ lot 1 added one more of those (uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist, H691), which is a network check, not a host check. scripts/doctor.py reports the same bind state in check_bind (scripts/doctor.py:186). GET /api/security/posture (agents/core/routers/security.py:282-283) reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. The host half the row accepted is absent. Nothing in doctor, boot or the posture endpoint checks running as root; lot 1's new doctor check, runtime_resolves, reads the running hub's model route and inspects nothing about the host. The only geteuid read is _process_elevated (agents/core/host_probe.py:329) inside the desktop-operator probe: probe_host skips permission checks on a headless host, warns only on Windows (agents/core/host_probe.py:457-459), and on Linux merely records the value (:481). No code reads sshd_config or sshd_config.d for PasswordAuthentication. No code detects a container whose data root is not on a persistent mount; check_data_root (scripts/doctor.py:212) only proves the directory is writable.
reviews.remaining: Add three read-only, non-blocking host checks, each logged once at startup and reported in both run_doctor and /api/security/posture. (1) The process runs as root (euid 0), or elevated on Windows, on any host, including headless. (2) sshd accepts passwords: parse /etc/ssh/sshd_config and its Include'd sshd_config.d fragments with sshd's own precedence, treating absence as the default 'yes'. (3) Running in a container (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv or cgroup markers) while data_root() is not on a volume or bind mount in /proc/self/mountinfo, which means memory, vault and keys vanish on restart.

reviews.summary: **`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE` flips from opt-in to default-on**, so a spawned stdio MCP server is handed the `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` baseline plus its own `env` instead of `os.environ.copy()` — API keys, tokens, proxies and every `JARVIS_*` setting withheld. A second flag, `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, is the owner-reachable migration remedy: a comma-separated list of host variable names that pass the baseline even when `_SECRET_LIKE` matches them. `_merged_env()` emits one INFO line per connect counting host values the child does not receive, carrying **no variable name and no value**. `GET /api/admin/mcp` rows gain `env_baseline`. And Nerva's own WorldView MCP server is handed its `WORLDVIEW_API_URL`, which the flip would otherwise have silently replaced with the built-in `http://localhost:4000`. **The review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed.** **(1)** `routers/mcp.py` asserted an invariant the code did not hold: the comment said a row that spawns no subprocess reports `None` "rather than a badge it has not earned" and enumerated two cases. A third exists and is the only one an owner can create today — `POST /api/admin/mcp` does no command validation, so a row with a whitespace-only command or a shell metacharacter persists, and `connect()` answers `unsafe_command` from `_command_argv()` **before** `create_subprocess_exec`. Such a row reported `env_baseline: true` for a child that never existed; the row now calls the same `_command_argv()` `connect` does, so the two cannot disagree, and the guard test carries both spellings. **(2)** `BACKLOG.md` still shipped the pre-flip claim and therefore stated the OPPOSITE of the code — "opt-in, default-off … keeps working until the owner opts in" — in the one file `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to query for what is delivered. That is exactly the misreading the slice's own documentation work exists to prevent. Corrected, and `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` now covers BACKLOG.md too, including a check that the "opt-in, default-off" wording is gone. Two wording corrections went with them: the `env_baseline` field describes the live FLAG, i.e. the posture for the NEXT spawn, not the environment the running child holds (`_merged_env()` runs once at connect, the row is read per request); and the migration note steered the reader at auth failures only, when the flip also withholds `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` — plumbing whose absence produces an ImportError, a hang or a connect timeout, nothing resembling an auth error. **#1179 (cda4e19d, adversarial-review finding 4) widened the DISCLOSURE, not the guarantee, and touched two of the five cited files.** `agents/core/mcp/client.py`: the module docstring now names a SECOND route by which a hostile child recovers the withheld keys — not only `/proc/<ppid>/environ` but the **filesystem**, which the baseline narrows not at all: `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` in the child reaches the very file `plugin_manager.build` read those keys from (`client.py:17-36`). New `_CWD_SECRET_FILES = (".env", ".env.local")` and `cwd_secret_files(cwd)` (`client.py:215-242`; `None` → `Path.cwd()`, the inherited default; unreadable and missing both count as absent) report which of them the child can open, and `_merged_env()` calls it right after the withheld-count INFO line — only when something WAS withheld (`:555`) and such a file is readable — emitting one WARNING per connect, "withholding is undercut — .env readable in the server's working directory", carrying **filenames only, never a variable name** (`client.py:565-571`), because a variable name enumerates which providers the box holds while `.env` tells the owner nothing new. Deliberately not a refusal: refusing to spawn over a `.env` breaks every dev checkout and re-pointing `cwd` breaks every server that resolves a relative path, so the module's posture stays *withhold and say so*. `tests/test_mcp_transports.py` gains `test_cwd_secret_files_reports_what_the_child_can_open` (`:830`; a directory named `.env.local` is not a file) and `test_the_withheld_count_is_not_announced_alone_when_a_dotenv_is_reachable` (`:854`; WARNING level, `OPENAI_API_KEY` absent from the line, silent when no file is reachable). Everything else above is as assessed: the default-on flag (`client.py:90`, `:190`), `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST`/`_SECRET_LIKE` (`:161-176`), `stdio_env_extra_allowed` (`:197-208`), the count-only INFO line (`:556-559`) are untouched, and `worldview_write.py` and `tests/test_mcp_admin.py` are byte-identical to the prior stamp. **The later fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) touched two cited files without touching this slice:** `client.py` gained `tool_patterns_over_bounds` (`client.py:138-154`) and a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (`:407-418`), and `admin_mcp_add` now also refuses a `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` over the 64-pattern / 128-char bounds (`routers/mcp.py:167-173`); neither reads the environment, the baseline flags or `env_baseline`, so the env code above only moved (+19 lines up to `MCPServer.__init__`'s filter block, +31 after it). The docstring pin `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` (`test_mcp_transports.py:554`) survived the rewrite because both strings it asserts remain (`/proc/<ppid>/environ` at `client.py:21`, "defence in depth, not a security boundary" at `:30`). 41/41 cited tests green (33 + 8), re-run at the bounds-change head.
reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field (`routers/mcp.py:128-140`, no `model_config`), `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` (`client.py:798-812`) nor `load_from_config` (`:814-849`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at `client.py:41-45`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV` (`:92-98`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (`client.py:169`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (`_SECRET_LIKE` at `:174-176` matches the `AUTH` in `XAUTHORITY`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (`client.py:17-36`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`; and the baseline narrows the **filesystem** not at all — `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which `cwd_secret_files()` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, `client.py:565-571`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the `/proc` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — `client.py:33-36`), which is not shipped. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", `client.py:34`), and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still stores `req.command` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (`routers/mcp.py:142-192`, `:184`); the only shape check is `_command_argv()`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (`client.py:519-529`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:558, agents/core/backup.py:627). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:795). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515).
