A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:85); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:41). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:375, agents/core/backup.py:380). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:434). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:365). It is also used by publish_skill (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:371), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:217). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:394, agents/core/backup.py:418; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:585; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:834, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:844). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:192). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:752; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:201). Restore stays an operator CLI action. It prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:676) and 'nothing restored' only for a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:682). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no product module, script or subprocess caller reaches it. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:442), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:636, tests/test_backup.py:675). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:559, agents/core/backup.py:602; tests/test_backup.py:651). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design.

Plugin egress now has a validated trust anchor. tls_verify (agents/core/http_client.py:185) reads JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE, or SSL_CERT_FILE as the fallback (:181-182, :197). It adds the bundle to certifi through an SSLContext and, on a missing or unloadable file, logs a warning and keeps the default store rather than downgrading (:200-203). PluginHTTPClient uses it with trust_env=False (:328-329, :498). tests/test_plugin_egress.py covers these cases. The accepted requirement is only partly met. (1) There is no startup validation. The check runs lazily per plugin client, logs no copy-pasteable repair hint, and never validates REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE or certifi. The warning also names JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE even when the bad value came from SSL_CERT_FILE. (2) LLM egress bypasses tls_verify. llm_async_client (agents/core/llm/egress.py:76) builds a plain httpx.AsyncClient; HEQ lot 1 gave it a host-protocol refusal hook (H368) but no verify or trust_env setting. For the Anthropic, Gemini and OpenRouter backends (e.g. agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:59), trust_env stays on, so SSL_CERT_FILE replaces certifi and JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE is ignored. Constructing the client with SSL_CERT_FILE=/nonexistent.pem raised a bare 'FileNotFoundError [Errno 2] No such file or directory' that names no file (re-run on the lot-1 head): the opaque first-call failure Hermes guards against. The OpenAI Responses and xAI clients (agents/core/llm/responses.py:53, agents/core/llm/xai.py:48-49) set trust_env=False without tls_verify, so they trust certifi only. (3) No per-target verify resolver exists, and there is no explicit, logged per-URL 'off' position. docs/FLAGS.md documents verification as always on.
reviews.remaining:
1. Add boot-time validation, run from the lifespan beside enforce_boot_posture, of every set CA variable (JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE) and of certifi. Each must exist, be a file (or a directory for SSL_CERT_DIR), load into an SSLContext and yield at least one certificate. The error must name the variable and give a copy-pasteable repair command.
2. Route every LLM backend client through the same trust resolver, so JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE applies to model egress and a bad SSL_CERT_FILE cannot surface as an unnamed FileNotFoundError.
3. Add an explicit per-target (per-provider or per-base-URL) verify resolver. Its opt-in 'off' position logs a loud WARNING naming the base URL whenever a client is built with it. A bad CA path never turns into verify=False.

reviews.summary: **The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. A sandboxed script cannot label its own write nor strip the label off one: the classifier is registrar-owned and `handle()` returns `approval_required` before the handler is ever reached. **The review found one major and it is fixed here.** The roster omitted `HEARTBEAT.md` and `HEARTBEAT.local.md` — the files in this repo that *literally* schedule future runs: `core/heartbeat.py` scans every agent directory for them, prefers the gitignored `.local` overlay exactly as `SOUL.local.md` does, and turns what it finds into cron-scheduled agent runs. Reproduced against a real `ToolRPCServer`: a write to `HEARTBEAT.local.md` produced `class=None` and the generic title "Tool 'file_write' via RPC" — a card byte-identical to a write to a scratch note, for an action that installs a cron expression driving every later run. Both names are in the class now, and the roster is pinned against `heartbeat.py`'s own source rather than restated, so a loader that learns a new name fails the test instead of silently escaping the class. The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. Tests: `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_floor.py` (44) pins both sets exactly (the six base names and the eleven derived ones), derives the overlay requirement from the roster in `test_every_name_in_the_roster_brings_its_local_overlay` so a name added later brings its overlay or fails, keeps the heartbeat.py-derived pin, and exercises `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` through `write_file` with the kernel off; `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_class_toolrpc.py` (18) proves the durable card for `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` carries `class=agent_instructions` and the notice in its title, and that nothing reaches disk before approval. **The read half, first piece (2026-09-22), and its review round.** `agents/core/heartbeat.py` — the loader that turns HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md into cron-scheduled runs — refuses a flagged entry at parse time. `scan_heartbeat_config` runs `detect_injection_normalized` over every string in the YAML front-matter, keys and values, nested to a bound of 16, and the walker fails CLOSED: a container at the bound (`nesting-too-deep`, a `&x [*x]` alias cycle included), a `!!binary` value (`unscannable-value-type:bytes` — decoded so the verdict names what it hid, refused regardless) or any type `yaml.safe_load` never produces is a refusal, not a leaf the walker had nothing to say about; `!!set` values are walked; YAML's own scalars (bool, number, null, date) are inert. It decodes and scans a TAG-plane payload so it is named rather than merely deleted, excusing only a run shaped like a subdivision flag emoji (🏴, up to eight TAG letters, CANCEL TAG — England, Scotland, Wales) from the bare-invisible-run flag while still scanning what such runs spell; and it joins UTF-16 surrogate pairs first, because PyYAML decodes a `\uDB40\uDC70` escape into two lone surrogates that no code-point range in `quarantine.py` matches but that a JSON serialiser on the way to a model re-joins into the invisible TAG character (reproduced). One hit refuses the whole entry — a heartbeat is one scheduled job with no 'rest of the persona' to preserve, so the fail-closed answer is not to schedule it: `_parse_heartbeat` never returns a flagged config, and `load_from_config` — which the orchestrator calls right after `load_all` at startup — skips a refused agent instead of writing the agents.yaml interval entry that put it back before `start()`, so nothing reaches `_heartbeat_configs`, `start()`, `start_heartbeat()` or the `POST /heartbeat/{id}/run` path; a flagged overlay does not fall back to the shipped template; a reload starts each directory from a clean slate (no stale verdict, no stale config, in either direction); the refusal is logged with the file's absolute path, its sha256 over the one buffer that was parsed and scanned, and the matched patterns, never the payload; and `get_status()` — what `GET /heartbeat/status`, a deliberately public route, and the runtime run-log read — carries a `blocked` list (agent, file named relative to its root such as `souls/<id>/HEARTBEAT.local.md`, flags, digest) in both of its shapes. Every shipped HEARTBEAT.md loads clean. **`agents/core/security/quarantine.py` changed with it, for both loaders.** The review found that a blank-rendering character put INSTEAD of the space — the Hangul fillers (letters, so they also kill the raw `you are now\b` match), U+2800, a private-use character, or any character already in the table — defeated the SOUL path and the HEARTBEAT path alike: the raw copy had no space to match and the stripped copy had the words glued. `_detection_variants` also scans a copy in which every invisible character becomes a space, the table gains U+2800 and the three private-use planes (Co), and each copy is scanned again over its NFKC fold (fullwidth, ideographic space, ligatures). **An independent review of the first cut — two reviewers, ten distinct findings: two blocking, three major, four minor, one nit — eight fixed here, each red-first and neutered once:** `!!set`/`!!binary` skipped by the walker (blocking); the depth bound fail-open, and the 'at any depth' claim in this row, the BACKLOG bullet, the code comment and the test docstring false (blocking — corrected); blank-instead-of-space (major); `load_from_config` resurrecting a refused agent, and 'a refused entry is never scheduled' overstated for the production load order (major — corrected); the absolute path on the public route, the flag-emoji false refusal and the stale verdict on reload (minor); the two-read digest (nit). `tests/test_instruction_files_read_side_scan.py` (47) pins all of it — including equality with the plain spelling for fourteen blank characters through the detector, the HEARTBEAT loader and the SOUL per-line scan — and pins through `Agent._load_soul` the SOUL spellings the previous version of this row named as unproven ('You are now<U+200B>in developer mode' and 'You are now<U+0007>in developer mode'), which #1179 had already closed in code by routing `_scan_soul_body` through `detect_injection_normalized`.
reviews.remaining: **The read half now covers two of the three Nerva loaders and none of the external ones — the row stays partial.** H506 requires the same file class to be scanned at context-load time with a positive match replaced by `[BLOCKED: … Content not loaded.]`. What holds: SOUL.md / SOUL.local.md through `Agent._scan_soul_body` (H387's evidence, not this row's — per-line quarantine over the union of raw and normalised copies, cross-line wraps, whole-body drop above the ratio; the U+200B and U+0007 spellings after 'now' are pinned in this row's own test file), and HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md through `scan_heartbeat_config`, entry refused rather than line-stubbed. **Precisely what is not covered, stated rather than smoothed over:** the Markdown body after the front-matter is discarded by `_parse_heartbeat` and reaches no model, log or scheduler, so it is not scanned — `test_the_prose_body_is_not_loaded_and_therefore_not_scanned` is the tripwire a loader that starts reading it must flip; no heartbeat text is model input today — the checklist strings are keyword-routed to skills with constant arguments and echoed into a logged run summary — so the scan guards the mapping the loader hands to the agent, not a live prompt path; the keyword scanner is literal after normalisation, so a Cyrillic homoglyph ('Іgnore'), a combining overlay, markdown emphasis inside a phrase ('Ignore _all_ previous') and a phrase split across two checklist items still scan clean — a confusables fold is a separate `quarantine.py` slice, and the homoglyph is pinned as a tripwire in this row's test file; and the SOUL cross-line path (`_wrapped_injection_hits`) builds its own normalised copy inside `agent.py`, so a blank-instead-of-space spelling that ALSO wraps across lines is not covered there (agent.py is untouched here; it is H387's evidence, being re-evaluated by a sibling stream). **Adjacent, pre-existing, NOT fixed:** the orchestrator's `load_from_config` overwrites every shipped HEARTBEAT.md cron+checklist with the agents.yaml interval (all twelve shipped agents carry one), so at runtime `Agent.run_heartbeat` finds no checklist and returns None for the shipped roster — the loader semantics this row describes are what the code does, not what the shipped agents experience (recorded as a separate task); `load_all` keys the config by the front-matter's own `agent` field, so a clean `HEARTBEAT.local.md` in one agent's directory that says `agent: jarvis` replaces Jarvis's schedule (a refused file cannot — the verdict is keyed by directory); and `enabled: false` is parsed and never honoured. Still open on the read side: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / `.cursorrules` / `*.mdc` are read by the external harnesses rather than by Nerva, so 'the same file class on the way in' is not met for them. The write-side deviations stand as before: the row's *"fails closed on a config read error"* clause has no analogue because the roster is a hard-coded frozenset; `allow_session=False` holds only incidentally through the gated toolrpc `autonomy_level="ask"` intake, with nothing pinning it; and the class covers `file_write`/`file_delete` only — the terminal contract, the skill importer and the desktop operator are outside it. Unverified, stated as such: whether the Telegram decision card and the HUD decision inbox render the write-side notice verbatim, and whether any HUD renders the `blocked` list (the API carries it; `frontend/src/gap.tsx` and `agents/web/static/systems.js` read `heartbeats` only). `_mutate`'s floor remains lifted by a caller-supplied `approved=True` by design.

reviews.summary: Nothing in the agent loop checks code the model writes for dangerous patterns. FileTools.write_file (agents/core/file_tools.py:944) hands off to FileTools._mutate (agents/core/file_tools.py:961), which returns only ok/op/path/bytes/existed/snapshot_ref. The one classifier on the file_write approval card is FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1136). It delegates to instruction_labels (agents/core/file_tools.py:292) and labels only instruction files (H506); for ordinary code it returns None. ToolRPCServer._classify (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:556) merges classifier labels into the card payload and appends a `notice` label to the card title (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:400), which is where a warning would plug in, but no code-guidance label exists. A probe wrote `pickle.load(open(...))`, `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)` and `eval(user)` to a .py file with approved=True. The result had no warning field and classify_mutation returned None. Neither skill path (SkillMarketplace.install_skill at agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:579, SkillLoader.generate_skill at agents/core/skills/loader.py:914) runs code-pattern rules; they check contracts, moderation, signatures, quarantine and — since H503, for a marketplace package unpacked by install_from_zip — archive shape (member names, link and device entries, member and byte caps) only. bandit/semgrep in .github/workflows/security.yml scan Nerva's own repository, not what the agent writes into the owner's trees. There is no rule table anywhere under agents/: a grep for pickle/yaml.load/shell=True/new Function/createCipher/github.event rules returns nothing.
reviews.remaining: The whole feature is missing: a warn-only table of about 25 rules with per-extension path filters and lookbehind guards. It must cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill, yaml.load without SafeLoader, torch.load without weights_only), command injection (os.system, shell=True, child_process.exec, Go exec.Command("sh")), code injection (eval, new Function), XSS sinks, crypto footguns (ECB, createCipher without IV, disabled TLS verification), XXE, missing SRI and `${{ github.event.* }}` inside workflow `run:`. `model.eval()` must not match. Its findings must be attached to the file_write approval card and write result and to skill install/generation results, with a kill switch. It must never block.

reviews.summary: Reviewed against live code; the inherited 2026-09-07 "partial" verdict stands, but for a different and much smaller reason than the audit recorded. The audit's "no Host-header validation anywhere" is stale: agents/core/host_policy.py is a 204-line module whose docstring (:4-22) names DNS rebinding explicitly, with normalize_host() at :54, parse_allowed_hosts() at :104 refusing a `*` entry at :119-120 and a leading-dot suffix wildcard at :121-122, host_accepted() at :157-181 matching loopback names, any IP literal, JARVIS_HOST, the ASGI scope's arrival address and JARVIS_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and assert_parseable_allowed_hosts() at :184 refusing boot on an unparseable list. It is wired at agents/web.py:19 (import) and :735-755 (`_host_guard`, returning {"error": "host not allowed", "code": 400}), registered so it runs before the rate limiter and inside the security-header and golden-signal layers (:709-712). Dumping app.user_middleware on the HEQ lot-1 head gives _golden_signals, _security_headers, _host_guard, _rate_limit, _no_store_for_polling, then lot 1's pure-ASGI _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, which only sets the request scheme and runs inside the guard. The boot guard is genuinely reached on the real serve path: agents/core/boot_guards.py:354, inside enforce_boot_posture, which the lifespan calls at agents/web.py:420-421 after the .env files load (agents/web.py:414-415, H273), so a list that lives only in .env is checked too; assert_front_door runs the same check over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:320). Refusal logging is rate-shaped (:718-720, :751) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (:723-732), never the attacker-chosen header value. Driven live on the lot-1 head with a loopback TestClient: `Host: evil.test` gets 400 on /status, /dashboard and /api/agents, where the real host gets 200 on /status and /api/agents. The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:694), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. CORS is validated with reported rejections at agents/core/cors_policy.py, and no CORS middleware is installed at all by default. The WebSocket clause is excluded by the row itself and the exclusion still holds: no WebSocket server route exists in agents/ (lot 1's _ForwardedProtoMiddleware maps a listed proxy's scheme onto ws/wss scopes but adds no route), agents/web.py:713-714 says a future one must call host_accepted() itself, and agents/web.py:590 is the only ASGI app. 104/104 tests pass across the five relevant suites on the lot-1 head. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:715-717: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (:739-740), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. Re-confirmed live on the lot-1 head: a rebound page therefore still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent.
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:682, applied at :739-740), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:715-717 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body.

reviews.summary: The tamper-evident sink exists. AuditLogger.log (agents/core/security/audit.py:111) appends to a hash-chained SQLite log checked by verify_chain (agents/core/security/audit.py:209). The admin HUD reads it through GET /api/admin/audit (agents/core/routers/admin.py:301). One credential event is recorded: POST /api/admin/rotate-tokens (agents/core/routers/admin.py:176) writes a best-effort SecurityEventType.AUDIT_LOG row (agents/core/routers/admin.py:194) with action_taken token_rotated and no token value, and a sink failure only logs a warning. Nothing else in authentication reaches the audit. SecurityEventType (agents/core/security/types.py:22) still lists only secret_detected, pii_detected, ssrf_blocked, egress_downgrade, audit_log, llm_call and settings_change. _admin_guard (agents/web.py:209) and _user_guard (agents/web.py:285) return or raise 401/403 without writing an event, so a wrong admin token leaves only an HF-2 rate-limit bucket entry. TokenStore.issue, rotate and revoke_all (agents/core/security/token_store.py:73, agents/core/security/token_store.py:131, agents/core/security/token_store.py:143) write no audit, so CLI mint/rotate/revoke (agents/core/security/token_store.py:229) is invisible. No test asserts any auth audit row, including the existing rotation row.
reviews.remaining: Add auth event types: admin/user auth success, auth failure with reason (missing, invalid, network-disabled), token issued, token rotated, token revoked. Emit them from _admin_guard and _user_guard: failures always; successes deduplicated per token hash and client so the chain is not flooded. Also emit from TokenStore issue/rotate/revoke_all, which covers the CLI. Each event records scope, client host, reason and a token-hash prefix. A fixed redacted-field set (token, x-admin-token, x-user-token, authorization, cookie, code, state, ticket) is dropped before serialisation. Writes are best-effort: an audit failure must never change the allow/401/403 decision. The rotation route should switch to the new type. Tests must cover all of this.

reviews.summary: Two of the three accepted parts exist. Surface scoping: agents/core/tool_profiles.py resolves the offered tool set per agent × surface × principal in one module (classify_turn at agents/core/tool_profiles.py:121, resolve_tools at agents/core/tool_profiles.py:207). A call outside the profile is refused before execution (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:335), and tests/test_tool_profiles.py pins the resolved sets in a snapshot. Install posture: requirements-beta.lock is hash-pinned and gated in sync by .github/workflows/lockfile.yml, with no runtime installs; docs/FLAGS.md states the risk delta of each flag. The data-handling part, which the row named as the gap worth closing, is still mostly absent. The lot added one narrow control. `llm.openrouter_data_collection` (agents/core/settings_db.py:165), seeded `deny` (agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:41), is sent as OpenRouter's `provider.data_collection`, asking OpenRouter to route only to upstreams that do not store or train on prompts. HybridRouter hands OpenRouterBackend a reader that re-reads it before every request (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:395), only the openrouter profile carries it (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:70), and it is written only through the admin-guarded, audited PUT /api/admin/settings/{category} (agents/core/routers/admin.py:144). tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py pins the `deny` default and the wire object. It is not a provider tier. ProviderProfile (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:28) carries auth, capabilities, fallback models and reasoning vocabulary but no data-handling or training tier. HybridRouter.select_backend (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:498) routes to Gemini, Claude or a non-OpenRouter compatible provider without consulting one. Switching the OpenRouter knob to `allow` is taken silently. GET /api/security/posture (agents/core/routers/security.py:282) and the HUD PosturePanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:970) report secrets, signing, sandbox, hardened and product posture only. No acknowledgement setting and no warning exist.
reviews.remaining: Missing: a per-provider data-handling tier (for example no_training / may_train / unknown) on the provider metadata, covering the direct Gemini and Claude routes and the openai-compatible, openai-responses and xai providers that `llm.openrouter_data_collection` does not reach; a warning emitted every time a turn is routed to a may_train or unknown provider, including an OpenRouter turn under `data_collection=allow`; a durable per-provider acknowledgement written only through an admin_guard settings route. Following Hermes, the acknowledgement removes the stop on unattended runs but never the warning. The tiers, the OpenRouter `data_collection` value and the acknowledgement state are also missing from /api/security/posture and PosturePanel.

reviews.summary: Implemented configured local ComfyUI backend aliases and allowlisted checkpoint selection, up to four opaque generated-image references blended before editing, and explicit 2x bicubic upscale. Options remain bound into the existing exact, single-use approval tuple. HUD submits and displays these choices. A separate cloud-image adapter now completes one exact human-approved OpenAI gpt-image-1.5 request with finite size/quality options, fail-closed secret screening, fresh DNS-bound transport and durable no-replay attempts. Validated PNG bytes persist under an opaque local ID; opt-in catalog finalization is idempotent and reaches the existing gallery/blob/export flow. Independent mocked-transport checks cover the full guarded path; no live paid generation was performed. The owner Images panel now defaults to local and exposes the fixed cloud provider with finite size/quality controls. Read-only status does not sign, write configuration, probe network or expose credentials. Cloud serialization excludes local-only options. Decision Inbox shows immutable paid-operation details and retains a visible task-return link after approval. Strict task-ID URL restoration only reads existing tasks; no automatic resubmission. Independent click-only browser tests cover a nonempty prefix, signed worker, PNG, gallery and ZIP with mocked provider transport. After the separate HUD grid repair, the actual approved cloud browser workflow also passes at1280px and Pixel7; the desktop fixture no longer avoids the reproduced overflow. The model-callable image_generate tool now accepts an explicit cloud selector with only the existing fixed OpenAI model/size/quality vocabulary. Server-owned gated intake preserves the trusted actor and turn origin and proposes one signed plugin.egress task; the agent loop stops for the same human approval. Local generation/edit remains the default. Cloud arguments cannot execute as a local tool.rpc task, and missing runtime or ambiguous enqueue does not trigger fallback or resubmission. Actual ToolRPC/approval/worker/mock-provider/PNG/catalog and cancellation/restart regressions pass. The default-off local residency manager now requires exact controller acknowledgments before confirming loads or forgetting unloaded models. Refused unloads retain prior accounting and stop replacement; request references alone never imply residency. Strict LM Studio and Ollama adapter checks, cancellation/concurrency cases and actual Agent best-effort continuation pass offline and independent review.
reviews.remaining: The real ComfyUI path does not yet use the existing LLM unload/restore orchestrator. Frozen media.generate/file.write action-kind requirements need explicit architecture adjudication; current local tool.rpc and cloud plugin.egress mediation are verified but are not silently equated to that requirement. Local reference blending is pixel composition and upscale is bicubic resampling. The accepted adaptation requires one cloud seam, not eight-provider fan-out. Ambiguous provider attempts never retry automatically; catalog opt-out is respected. No live ComfyUI, billed provider or native-device validation is claimed. This acknowledgment foundation is not a VRAM swap: canonical aliases, production backend/controller identity, atomic per-generation leases, owner control coordination and authoritative hardware snapshots remain unresolved. Existing coarse headroom and no-victim overcommit behavior remain. ComfyUI unknown submissions need reconciliation before any future exclusive lease can safely release.

reviews.summary: The unified gallery now scans retained generated and attachment metadata through bounded keyset pages. Search and kind filters apply during each scan, including MIME matches; zero-match pages retain continuation to older records. Cursor fields, ordering and filter/source binding are checked before catalog or header I/O. Each request inspects at most 200 candidate headers and retains the existing authenticated path/byte validation. The HUD resets and cancels stale searches, reports retained versus loaded/scanned counts separately, and exports an explicit selection of at most 200 files/128 MiB. Independent review and desktop/responsive-browser tests cover older-only matches, empty-page continuation, deletion boundaries, source flags, malformed cursors and exact export selection. Shared attachment previews now abort on card unmount and reject late fetch/body continuations; owned object URLs are revoked even before a pending React state update commits. Reassessment against the frozen keep/superior row confirms the bounded retained-catalog browse/search/export contract. Retention and unavailable-byte handling match the original scope; deleted/evicted history restoration, native controls and unlimited ZIPs are not acceptance requirements. Timestamp/key traversal excludes newer appends without promising exact membership against backdated inserts. The current local generator catalogs produced assets; legacy cloud proposals do not execute a cloud image backend. Future approved cloud completion must persist catalog output as part of H515, not be inferred from generic text-task completion. No live-provider or universal producer-provenance proof is claimed. The implemented cloud-image producer now writes canonical validated output and an idempotent opt-in catalog record before successful completion; independent signed-worker/mock-provider/blob/ZIP checks cover the previously conditional writeback obligation. The legacy generic text task is not treated as an image producer.

Generated/cache and attachment bytes are served by opaque ID through one authenticated shared reader, bounded canonical roots, 16 MiB file caps and MIME/disposition checks. The unified gallery opens and exports retained entries. Scheduled reminders now send 1..8 exact owner-bound media IDs (32 MiB aggregate) through the real Telegram binary/text adapter under one validated 1..300-second total deadline, default 300, including lookup, reads, all files, final text and held flushing. Durable sending/partial/unknown states, current recipient/content checks and process locks prevent automatic replay, stale-held duplication and late-ack continuation. Independent review confirms owner-authored IDs satisfy the frozen cron-media clause; no model MEDIA parser or every-channel requirement was accepted. At the original review: fresh 148 reader/generation/media checks, independent 98 backend/16 frontend checks and full 1,315 frontend tests pass. Synchronous local I/O is not preemptible, but no subsequent dispatch occurs after expiry. This is code equivalence with mocked HTTP; no live Telegram, new-provider/native-codec or arbitrary-path guarantee. The complete integrated backend suite collected 11,428 tests with 11,404 passes, 23 skips and one expected failure; no unexpected failures. Workdir integration rechecked previously-current evidence against base 837d6d08: additive script-only option validation and adjacent HUD fields leave the media contract unchanged. Existing media and frontend regressions remain green.

A pure, offline speech normaliser exists, but only chat-channel voice notes and the gated speak tool use it. agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:73 speakable() drops fenced code (_FENCE_RE, :56). It strips bold/italic/heading/inline-code markers through to_plain() in agents/core/channels/render.py and replaces URLs with the word "link" (:57). It then folds newlines and whitespace to single spaces and cuts at a sentence boundary within 1,500 chars. Its callers are SpokenReply.__call__ (:196), used by Telegram's per-chat voice mode (agents/core/channels/telegram.py _speak) and the /voice command, and, since HEQ lot 1 (H313), the gated speak ToolRPC tool (registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on): its preflight refuses text with nothing speakable (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:315) and its approved run synthesizes through SpokenReply (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:471), so a model-chosen room announcement gets speakable()'s cleaning and the speakable() gaps listed at the end. The main speech paths do not normalise:
- POST /tts passes req.text straight to TTSEngine.speak (agents/core/routers/voice.py:57), and /tts/stream splits the raw text (:115).
- TTSEngine.speak removes only the twelve Fish [emotion] tags (agents/core/voice/tts.py:47, :167).
- The HUD voice loop sends the raw reply and each raw streamed sentence to /tts (frontend/src/voice.ts:238, :297), fed by raw token deltas (frontend/src/app.tsx:311).
- Mobile ttsFetchBase64 posts raw text (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2384).
- The wake-word VoicePipeline speaks the raw response (agents/core/voice/pipeline.py:60), and so does VoiceChannel.send (agents/core/channels/voice.py:41).
speakable() itself also has gaps. A probe on a mixed markdown sample kept emoji, "- " list bullets, table pipes and |---| separator rows, a <think> block, and the symbols & % ->. Its URL regex also swallows the closing parenthesis that to_plain() puts after a link, producing "doc (link". <think> blocks are removed upstream only, by strip_thinking() in agents/core/llm/base.py on model output, not by any speech normaliser.
reviews.remaining:
Apply one speech normaliser at every TTS entry point: POST /tts, /tts/stream, TTSEngine.speak (and with it VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and SpokenReply), the HUD per-sentence streaming path and mobile. Today only Telegram voice notes, /voice and the gated speak tool (H313) go through speakable(), and the speak tool shares its gaps. The normaliser must also:
- remove emoji
- strip list markers and tables
- drop <think> blocks, including unclosed ones
- expand symbols (&, %, ->, °) for RO and EN
- stop the URL regex from eating the link's closing parenthesis
- keep Fish [emotion] tags intact.
On the streaming path, a fenced code block split across token deltas must not be spoken.

reviews.summary: Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant.
reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul.

A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: There is no scanned-PDF coverage detection. An image-only PDF extracts to empty or near-empty text and is returned as a successful read, with no warning and no list of empty page ranges, and there is no OCR anywhere in the repo. Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: slides (.pptx), spreadsheets (.xlsx) and the other converter formats are not read, and no Office skills are bundled. The drop-a-file-in entry point belongs to the chat-attachment row.

reviews.summary: Modelul poate căuta și extrage pagini prin egressul existent, cu rezultate limitate și marcate ca date.
reviews.remaining: Rămân cerințe de extracție/paginare/cache/configurare din rândurile complete; x_search exclus nu este reinclus.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no ACP editor-agent surface. No handler for session/new, load, resume or fork exists anywhere under agents/, and the editor-surface row H542 is itself still missing, so nothing can accept an mcpServers array from an editor. The only outbound MCP registry is the process-wide MCPManager (agents/core/mcp/client.py:728-730), which holds a single servers dict. It is filled by the admin-guarded POST /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:142-143) and the persisted global config. There is no per-session server scope, no per-session mcp-<name> toolset, no bounded discovery join and no late refresh of the tool registry. tests/test_mcp_client.py and tests/test_mcp_admin.py exercise only the global registry.
reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary: Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (`tools_allow`/`tools_deny`, potrivite cu `fnmatchcase` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (`tool_visible`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-610). `_list_tools` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar `MCPServer.call_tool` răspunde `tool_filtered` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine `[]` (`_clean_tool_patterns`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (`admin_mcp_add`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:165-174) refuză cu 400 `{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}` un `tools_allow` sau `tools_deny` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (`tool_patterns_over_bounds`, client.py:138-154), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin `load_from_config` îngustează serverul la nimic (`tools_allow = []`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. Filtrele fac round-trip prin `to_config`/`load_from_config` (:808-809, :846-847). Teste (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py, 13/13 verzi): listare și deny prevalează (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:47-57), unealtă filtrată refuzată la apel pe nume (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:60-70), filtru malformat → nimic și round-trip de config (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:73-84), ruta primește filtre și refuză formele malformate (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:98-109), ruta refuză 129 de caractere / 65 de intrări pe ambele câmpuri (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:121-129) și acceptă un filtru exact la limită (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:132-138), un deny imposibil de păstrat ascunde toate uneltele cu avertisment (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-147), iar un config editat manual cu deny peste limite se încarcă fail-closed fără să atingă serverul vecin (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:150-159). Resursele/prompts sunt urmărite separat în H552.

Trust tiers și readOnlyHint limitează doar apelurile MCP, nu oferta. Tier-ul (`read-only` implicit, `full` explicit; alias-uri + `normalize_trust`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:105-117; `MCPServer.__init__` ridică ValueError pe o ortografie necunoscută, :397-400; `load_from_config` tratează tier-ul lipsă ca full-cu-avertisment și unul necunoscut ca read-only, :819-836; ruta de add validează tier-ul, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:159-162) și `MCPTool.read_only` (adevărat doar când `annotations.readOnlyHint is True`, :363-365) sunt consultate exclusiv în `_trust_denial` (:636-649), pe care `call_tool` îl rulează înaintea contractului de formă și înainte ca vreun frame să plece (:618-624): pe un server read-only orice tool nemarcat sau nelistat e refuzat pe nume cu `trust_denied` (`readOnlyHint_required` / `unlisted_tool`); `full` lasă totul la contractul de formă. Oferta (listarea) e îngustată numai de `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` (`_list_tools`/`tool_visible`, :584-610 — mecanismul H-4c pe care îl fixează tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py; un deny care nu încape în limitele de 64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere îngustează serverul la nimic tot prin `tools_allow`, :407-418); tier-ul și hint-ul nu ascund nimic: un server read-only își listează și tool-urile de scriere (`get_tools` :742-746 neîngustat; tests/test_mcp_trust.py:61-68; ruta admin le afișează cu `read_only: false`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:106-112).
reviews.remaining: Rămâne reconcilierea fiecărei căi de autorizare outbound față de contractul complet: nu există hop de aprobare (`kernel|authorize|approval|elicitation|retry` apare în agents/core/mcp/client.py doar în comentariul de la linia 103; `request_elicitation_consent` nu există în Nerva), tier-ul read-only refuză scrierile în loc să le ruteze la consimțământ, dict-ul de refuz (liniile 643-649) nu îi spune modelului să nu reîncerce, `_tool_call_blocked` (:651-670) evaluează doar forma `kind/server/tool/transport/args_keys`, iar apelul outbound nu scrie niciun rând de audit — singura cale outbound guvernată (kernel + audit) rămâne agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py, construită manual pentru un singur server `full`. Dovada pentru mecanismul trust/readOnlyHint e în tests/test_mcp_trust.py (necitat); tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py fixează doar filtrele: serverele pe care le apelează sunt construite cu `trust="full"` (helper-ul `_server`, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:33-44), iar celelalte (inclusiv cazurile fail-closed pentru limite, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-159) rămân pe tier-ul implicit fără să aserteze ceva despre el.

reviews.summary:
H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong. Re-read 2026-09-22 after #1179 (cda4e19d): that PR touched agents/core/mcp/client.py only in the stdio env-baseline disclosure — the scope paragraph of the module docstring (client.py:17-36), `from pathlib import Path` (:58), the `_CWD_SECRET_FILES` comment block + constant + `cwd_secret_files()` (:211-242) and the "withholding is undercut" warning block in `MCPServer._merged_env` (:560-571) — none of which this row relies on; `MCPTool`, `_list_tools`, `MCPManager.get_tools`/`_resolve`/`find_tool`/`call_tool` are byte-identical to the pre-#1179 file, and the six other evidence files are unchanged. Only line numbers moved (they had already drifted 94 lines at #1174 and were 151 off after #1179). Re-read again 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1): it added `tool_patterns_over_bounds` after `_clean_tool_patterns` (client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (:407-418), a bounds refusal in `admin_mcp_add` (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:167-173) and bounds tests at the end of tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:112-159); none of it touches a schema, a tool name or the resolver, so client.py pointers moved another +19 (the `MCPTool` block) or +31 (from `MCPServer.__init__` on) and routers/mcp.py pointers past the filter check moved +4. Every pointer below is at HEAD. One fact did change between the 2026-09-07 stamping and HEAD, by #1152 (0ef4002f, 2026-09-15) rather than #1179: a fifth provider serialization path now exists (see NOT SHIPPED).

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:748-777 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}` (:772-776); `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server (:756-767); `find_tool` (client.py:779) and `call_tool` (client.py:788) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing; file 6/6 at HEAD). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:592) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:357) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and on only ONE of five provider serialization paths: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-438 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:424-428) and missing-`type` coercion (:421), and :441-451 `gemini_function_declarations` avoids the empty-OBJECT 400 (:447-449); its output feeds only gemini.py:340-342. The other four paths pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte: Anthropic (tool_dialects.py:147-151 `anthropic_tools`, :149, via anthropic.py:171), OpenAI chat-completions (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `ToolSpec.as_openai`, :25 — shared by base.py:553, the Ollama path base.py:805 and openrouter.py:95), OpenAI Responses (responses.py:72-81, :77) and xAI Responses (xai.py:79-80 — `XAIBackend._payload` at xai.py:55 overrides `ResponsesBackend._payload` at responses.py:59, so the responses.py builder never runs for xAI; this path landed in #1152 on 2026-09-15, after the original verdict counted four). Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: re-run at HEAD, `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed; on the Gemini path it degenerates to an empty schema, and the Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI paths ship the raw nullable union untouched — reproduced through `anthropic_tools` and `as_openai` on a ToolSpec carrying that property), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"type":"object","properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` is empty, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:742-746) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor (`grep -rn "MCPTool" agents/` hits only client.py; `grep -rn "\.input_schema" agents/` outside agents/core/llm/ hits only client.py:357 and the hub's own MCP-server side in route_tools.py), the only `MCPManager` instances are `orch.mcp` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:516, reached from agents/web.py:1650 and agents/web.py:1660 and routers/mcp.py for config and HUD only) and worldview_write.py:77, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:105-112 and :231-232 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. But the triage's grep was scoped wrong and missed a real production consumer of the dispatch path: agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:163 calls `self.mcp.call_tool(tool, mcp_args)` by bare name (it lives inside agents/core/mcp/, which their grep excluded). So `_resolve` is not dead code, and its bare-name path is live today.

Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. Six of Hermes' nine clauses are unsatisfied or satisfied on only one of five provider paths, and no test anywhere exercises repair of a third-party `inputSchema`. Recording `equivalent` would put a false claim on a public status page; `partial` with a named remainder is the honest row.
reviews.remaining: No provider-agnostic repair of a third-party MCP server's JSON Schema exists (re-verified at HEAD 2026-09-22, line numbers re-mapped 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change, which touches none of this path; #1179 changed nothing on this path either — its client.py hunks are the stdio `cwd_secret_files` disclosure at :17-36, :58, :211-242 and :560-571; the only change since the 2026-09-07 stamping that bears on this row is #1152 adding a fifth unrepaired provider path, below). (1) `agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601` `_list_tools` still stores `inputSchema` verbatim (`:592`) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (`:357`); add a `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` applied at registration. (2) Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path, verified by running the code: draft-07 `definitions`/`#/definitions/...` are never promoted to `$defs`/`#/$defs/...` (and `gemini_schema` silently reduces a `$ref` property to `{}`, deleting the shape), and a Pydantic nullable union `anyOf:[{...},{"type":"null"}], default:null` is never collapsed to its non-null branch (`gemini_schema` yields `anyOf:[{"type":"string"},{}]` with `default:null` retained on the Gemini path; the other four paths ship the raw nullable union untouched). (3) The three repairs that do exist (`required` pruned to declared names `:424-428`, missing `type` coerced `:421`, empty-OBJECT avoided `:447-449`) live only in `agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-451` and therefore apply to Gemini alone; the other four serialization paths pass `input_schema` through unrepaired: `anthropic_tools` (tool_dialects.py:147-151), `ToolSpec.as_openai` (tool_protocol.py:19-27; used by base.py:553, the Ollama path base.py:805 and openrouter.py:95), the OpenAI Responses payload (responses.py:72-81) and the xAI Responses payload (xai.py:79-80, whose `_payload` overrides responses.py's, added by #1152 on 2026-09-15). (4) No name sanitization or provider-legal prefixing: `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is `server/tool`, whose `/` is outside the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` function-name charset both Anthropic and OpenAI enforce, and nothing replaces characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` returns nothing. (5) The row's security property — a third-party tool shadowing a built-in governed tool name — is unaddressed: `_resolve` (client.py:748-777) disambiguates only among `self.servers` (:768), never against the agent tool registry. (6) No test covers any of this; `grep -rln "gemini_schema" tests/` returns only tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, and neither test that constructs `MCPTool` (tests/test_mcp_hardening.py, tests/test_mcp_trust.py) asserts on `input_schema`. All of the above is currently unreachable by a model because no MCP-client -> tool-registry bridge exists (`MCPManager.get_tools()`, client.py:742-746, has zero callers repo-wide), so the normalizer plus its tests should land inside whichever PR first offers MCP client tools to the model, not as a standalone pure function — and that normalizer must sit at registration, ahead of all five dialect serializers, not inside `gemini_schema`.

reviews.summary: The model can read a document mid-turn through a tool call. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. There is no size refusal for documents (Hermes refuses over 50 MB): the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. There is no scanned-page coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text, which the row calls the clever half. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. A missing parser is named (`parser_missing`) rather than installed lazily.

reviews.summary: Nothing on main expands @-references. The HUD composer (InputBar, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:216) does not parse `@file:path` or `#Lx-y` ranges, and neither do the /chat and /chat/stream routes (agents/web.py:1119, agents/web.py:1259). There is no expander module, no `--- Attached Context ---` section and no completion over reference types or paths. A grep for `@file:`, `Attached Context` or `context_ref` across agents/, frontend/src/, mobile/src/ and tests/ finds no real hit. The closest affordance is `nerva chat -f PATH` (agents/cli/nerva.py:251). It reads the whole message body from a file. It does not go through FileScope, cannot take a line slice, does not detect binary files or warn on size, and does not taint the turn. The guards the row depends on exist and are tested. FileScope.resolve (agents/core/file_tools.py:328, agents/core/file_tools.py:360) refuses paths outside the roots, `..` traversal, symlink escapes and secret-looking names (tests/test_file_tools.py, 46 passed). mark_turn_recall_tainted (agents/core/security/recall_taint.py:47) raises the turn's action origin so the kernel escalates GRANT to QUEUE. Nothing calls either one for inline file references. file_read now pages a file by byte offset and can read a spilled tool result back through a read-only door (H661), but that is a model tool call, not an owner inline reference, and it takes no line range.
reviews.remaining: The expander needs to be built. It must parse `@file:path` and `@file:path#Lstart-end` in the owner's message and resolve every path through FileScope. It must reject binary files, cap bytes per reference and in total, and append the content under `--- Attached Context ---`. Refused, missing or truncated references should produce inline warnings instead of failing the turn. It must call mark_turn_recall_tainted whenever content is attached, so kernel GRANT decisions escalate to QUEUE. It should run in the /chat and /chat/stream turn path, so both the HUD and `nerva chat` get it. Completion over reference types and in-scope paths also needs to be added: a user-guarded, read-only FileScope listing that the InputBar queries when the owner types `@`.

reviews.summary: OpenRouter provider routing ships, and the owner's changes reach the live backend on the next request. Six llm rows are seeded right after compatible_provider (agents/core/settings_db.py:160-165): openrouter_sort, openrouter_only, openrouter_ignore, openrouter_order, openrouter_require_parameters, and openrouter_data_collection, seeded deny. The HUD PUT /api/admin/settings/llm and `nerva config set` both validate through settings_db.validate_category, and the three slug lists share one slug check (agents/core/settings_db.py:688 -> agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:97). build_provider_block (agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:110) turns the knobs into OpenRouter's `provider` object. It lower-cases and de-duplicates slugs, caps each list at 32, sends require_parameters only as a literal true, omits empty knobs, and raises on an invalid value instead of dropping it. HybridRouter.detect hands OpenRouterBackend a reader over the rows, not a snapshot (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:395). Before every text or tool-turn request the backend re-reads and re-validates them off the event loop (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:94, called at agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:163 and agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:201) and puts the object in the body (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:124). A HUD change, or a `nerva config set` run from another process against the same settings DB, therefore governs the next request, so the CLI's '(a running hub picks it up within 30 s)' holds for these rows. The object goes only to the openrouter profile, never to openai-compatible (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:70). Fail-closed limits: a stored value that decodes but does not validate refuses to build the backend at detect (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:398, logged). After detect it refuses that request: '[OpenRouter error]', nothing sent, and an error log naming llm.openrouter_* (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:107-111). The next request flows once the row is fixed. Known limit: a row that cannot be read or decoded (a sqlite error, or malformed JSON written around the API) is swallowed by settings_db.get_value into that knob's seeded default with no log line. Such a request keeps data_collection deny but loses only/ignore/order/sort/require_parameters. A 400/404 to a request that carried the object logs OpenRouter's own message (log-safe, 200 chars), the object sent and the settings to loosen (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:128), so the seeded deny does not fail opaquely after an upgrade. Coverage is tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py (30 tests). It checks the exact body on the tool-turn and text paths (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:78, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:93), and on the wire through the real egress client with a MockTransport injected through its public transport kwarg (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:135). It checks that no object is sent with nothing set or for openai-compatible (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:102, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:114), and that bad values are refused (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:174, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:180). It covers the rows, the deny default, write validation and the CLI entry point (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:192, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:206, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:223), and router wiring with a stubbed read (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:274, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:287, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:300). Three router tests run on a real temporary settings DB: rows -> detect -> body (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:346); a change after detect reaching the next request, tightening and loosening (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:358); and a tampered row after detect refusing the request, then healing (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:384). Two more cover the policy-404 hint and its absence without an object or on a 401 (tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:406, tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py:424). Nerva has no Nous Portal provider, so the knobs apply to OpenRouter only.

The HUD half of the accepted adaptation is delivered. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:42-43) plus a file chooser. It accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each, and the shared InputBar wires it in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:238). App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:372, frontend/src/app.tsx:347). runVision posts to the user-guarded POST /api/vlm/composer/describe (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:191, registered at agents/web.py:1399). The route checks data-URI signatures and bounds raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:28). It binds the request to the reviewed destination/model revision and refuses a non-local VLM unless the owner has acknowledged it (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:212). It then calls VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:357). Images reach only the configured VLM, never the text chat model. The taint governance holds through isolation rather than a taint flag. The vision answer is a client-only transcript entry, and ordinary turns post only {message, agent} to /chat/stream (frontend/src/app.tsx:301), so no tool plan can be derived from image content. tests/test_composer_vision.py (27 passed) covers validation, auth, binding, the remote acknowledgement and error shapes. Intake and the vision turn are covered by frontend/src/test/composer-images.test.tsx, frontend/src/test/composer-vision-turn.test.tsx and frontend/e2e/composer-images.spec.ts, which were not run here because frontend node_modules is absent.
reviews.remaining: The terminal image path in the accepted adaptation is missing. The `nerva chat` verb (agents/cli/nerva.py:229) has no image argument and does not read the clipboard, so a terminal user cannot attach a screenshot file or a pasted image to /api/vlm/composer/describe.

reviews.summary: No convention-file discovery exists on main. No module walks from a git root down to a working directory, loads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules or .cursor/rules/*.mdc, or discovers such files progressively as file tools or the terminal move into subdirectories. A grep for these names under agents/ finds only write-governance code and comments. INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES and looks_instruction_name (agents/core/file_tools.py:270, agents/core/file_tools.py:284) classify these files so that a write to one counts as an instruction-class mutation (tests/test_file_tools_instruction_floor.py, 44 passed). They never feed a prompt. The building blocks the row depends on exist. The core-block renderer applies detect_injection (agents/core/security/quarantine.py:53) to memory facts (agents/core/learning/core_block.py:30), and the orchestrator injects that block through _living_core_memory_block (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2852; tests/test_core_block_injection.py, 7 passed). A hardened variant, detect_injection_normalized (agents/core/security/quarantine.py:213), also scans invisible-as-space and NFKC-folded copies, and is what the SOUL and HEARTBEAT loaders use. mark_turn_recall_tainted (agents/core/security/recall_taint.py:47) can taint a turn. Neither is applied to project convention files, because none are loaded. The skills importer reads CLAUDE.md only as a one-time migration source, not at runtime.
reviews.remaining: Runtime discovery needs to be built. It must resolve the working directory (the FileScope root or the terminal cwd) and walk from its git root down to it, collecting AGENTS.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc. It must discover again when tools move into a subdirectory, and must never load SOUL.md from a project. Every file goes through FileScope, gets a per-file and a total byte budget with explicit truncation, and is scanned with detect_injection (preferably detect_injection_normalized); a flagged file becomes a [BLOCKED ...] placeholder. Loading any file marks the turn tainted. The result is injected as a caveated prompt block beside the core-memory block. Tests must cover the walk, the budgets, blocking and the taint.

reviews.summary: K1/K2/K3 are delivered: default-off execute_code with fresh host authorization, persistent session namespaces, operator status/reset, and redirected Python stdout/stderr stream spills on both one-shot and session paths. Each stream spill keeps at most 5,000,000 bytes (the ToolResultStore default, which the coordinator does not override). Past that, the file ends in one explicit spill-capped marker, the result reports the cap with kept and on-disk byte counts, and the notice says the stream's end survives only in the inline tail. Bounded previews retain file references, original byte counts and the on-disk file hash without buffering the full stream. A notice names the exact file_read(path, offset, max_bytes) paging call, also returned as a read_with field and continued by next_offset, only when two conditions hold: the run's own offer includes file_read, and the coordinator's probe confirms file_read can open that spill through the live file scope or the spill directory's read-only door. Otherwise the notice says the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from that turn. H660 now supplies the detached Docker transport. Review fixes retain unconfirmed teardown as quarantined/retryable state and prevent fallback dispatch after current authority or e-stop refusal. Native macOS and Linux real-Docker containment are now verified. The host CLI and local Unix endpoint are frozen; private CLI configuration prevents operator proxy credentials reaching the worker, including after context changes.
reviews.remaining: Generic SSH/Modal provisioning remains unsupported; the validated Docker transport accepts local Unix endpoints. Deliberate native-fd bypass output is not a redirected Python stream. Stream spills are capped at 5,000,000 bytes per stream: later bytes are counted but not kept, so only the inline tail shows a runaway stream's end. Hermes project|strict mode remains intentionally represented by Nerva tool profiles (agent x surface x principal), not copied as a separate switch.

reviews.summary: The pool mechanism is wired end to end. AuthProfilePool (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py) holds several keys per provider, read from *_API_KEYS with a *_API_KEY fallback (from_env, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). hybrid_router builds Gemini and Anthropic pools (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:327). ClaudeBackend and GeminiBackend fail over to the next key on a rotatable status (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:116, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:201). report_failure (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159) applies an exponential cooldown from 30 s to 15 min. Pool health is exposed. status() (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:178) returns masked per-profile failures and health through the admin-guarded GET /api/llm/auth-profiles (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:427). AuthProfilesPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2597) renders it, under the console route at frontend/src/console-routes.ts:116. tests/test_h12_20_auth_rotation.py (18 passed) and tests/test_route_guard_contracts.py::test_llm_auth_profiles_requires_admin (passed) cover the pool and the guard.
reviews.remaining: The accepted branches are missing. _ROTATABLE_STATUS (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:28) is {401, 403, 429}, so a 402 billing failure neither rotates nor gets the long (1 h) cooldown. No OAuth credential type exists, and a 401 has no refresh-then-rotate step. Keys resolve only from os.environ in from_env; VaultResolver (agents/core/secrets_vault.py:16) is never consulted for LLM keys. The owner also cannot see partial degradation. AuthProfilesPanel shows one healthy/failing tag per provider, derived from the pool-level healthy count, so a pool with some keys cooling still reads green. The API returns per-profile cooldown, but the panel does not render it.

reviews.summary: Local image generation and editing retain exact single-use approvals; the HUD now offers configured local ComfyUI backend/checkpoint choices, up to four blended opaque references, and explicit 2x bicubic upscale. The API additionally accepts one governed OpenAI image generation with fixed model and finite size/quality options; the current HUD still authors local requests.
reviews.remaining: Cloud HUD authoring, additional vendor model inventories and broader provider controls remain open. Reference blending is pixel composition and upscale is bicubic; no real ComfyUI or billed cloud provider proof was performed.
