reviews.summary: Five TTS backends exist: Edge (the default), ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, local XTTS and Kokoro. TTSEngine.speak (agents/core/voice/tts.py:144) sends Fish, XTTS and ElevenLabs voices to _speak_fish, _speak_xtts and _speak_elevenlabs (agents/core/voice/tts.py:275, agents/core/voice/tts.py:213, agents/core/voice/tts.py:236) by voice-name marker. Otherwise it falls back to edge-tts, then Kokoro (agents/core/voice/tts.py:182, agents/core/voice/tts.py:320, agents/core/voice/tts.py:331). strip_emotion_tags is applied for every backend except Fish. The consent gate for cloned and persona voices is intact. is_persona_or_cloned_voice (agents/core/voice/tts.py:54) checks PERSONA_VOICE_MARKERS (agents/core/voice/tts.py:35), and voice_persona_consent_granted (agents/core/voice/tts.py:62) reads the voice.persona_voice_consent setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:196). STT is faster-whisper only (STTEngine, agents/core/voice/stt.py:53; transcribe at agents/core/voice/stt.py:85). tests/test_tts.py (10), tests/test_tts_fish_emotion.py (12), tests/test_q4_voice_consent.py (7) and tests/test_voice_stt.py (6) pass.
reviews.remaining: Both accepted additions are missing. There is no Piper provider: agents/ and tests/ never reference piper, and the only mention is a demo ADMIN fixture in the HUD. A fully local Romanian voice therefore still depends on Kokoro or XTTS being installed. There is also no command-provider escape hatch for TTS or STT. The voice.tts_voice setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:195) only chooses among the hard-coded backends in speak, and STTEngine has no alternative to faster-whisper.

reviews.summary: No external intake has request-level idempotency. POST /api/actions/request (agents/core/routers/actions.py:34) calls ActionApprovalQueue.request, which mints a fresh uuid on every call (agents/core/autonomy/action_approvals.py:44). POST /api/webhooks/{id} (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:457) runs orch.handle_input on every delivery its event list admits to an agent target, and a workflow target's resolved pipeline as an inbound turn; it keeps only call and skip counters, so a retried identical delivery runs again, and a deliver-only hook sends it to the owner's channel again (up to the hook's push limit, 30 an hour). A2ARegistry.receive_task mints a new inbox id for every verified body (agents/core/a2a.py:244). A scratch probe confirmed that two identical requests produce two pending actions and two A2A inbox rows. The only idempotency_key under agents/ is a field on an inert value type (agents/core/execution_provider_contract.py:481) with no reservation store behind it. Nothing sits in front of govern_enqueue in agents/core/autonomy/worker.py.
reviews.remaining:
The whole accepted row is missing:
- Idempotency-Key header parsing, with 1–255 visible-ASCII validation and HTTP 400 invalid_idempotency_key.
- A durable UNIQUE(scope,key) SQLite reservation taken under BEGIN IMMEDIATE that survives restarts and multiple workers. It stores only a request fingerprint and a public status/result reference, never bodies or credentials.
- A caller-derived scope (webhook id, A2A peer, principal) so two callers cannot collide.
- A duplicate returns the original action/run, and a key reused with a different fingerprint is refused.
- A `durable` property on the store.
- Placement in front of the kernel/approval enqueue, so a retry never becomes a second approval item or audit row.
It has to be wired into /api/actions/request, /api/webhooks/{id} and /api/a2a/task, and into the run-create route once H476 lands.

reviews.summary: K2/K3 now include a production detached Docker worker over run-to-completion CLI calls, with a private size-limited container mailbox, bounded response packets/backpressure, ready handshake, cell nonces, asynchronous liveness monitoring, and kill/reset/cancel lifecycle. Each cell still crosses the current host authorization and ToolCallBroker. Only a proved pre-dispatch startup refusal permits explicit isolated per-call fallback; dispatched/ambiguous cells never retry. Python cell stdout/stderr streams now reach existing ToolResultStore spills before preview truncation, retaining the middle without unbounded worker buffers up to a 5,000,000-byte per-stream spill ceiling. Past the ceiling, the file ends in one explicit capped marker and the result reports the cap with kept and on-disk byte counts. Spill notices name the exact file_read paging call (path, offset, max_bytes, continued by next_offset) only when the run was offered file_read and it can open that file; otherwise they say the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from that turn. Session tool-RPC uses directory-pinned no-follow I/O and random cell directories, closing a reproduced host-write symlink issue. Existing opt-in settings and digest-pinned Docker isolation remain. Independent-review repairs recheck e-stop/expiry and authorization inside fallback dispatch, retain unconfirmed removals as quarantined records with retryable operator reset, validate hostile stream labels, and keep deadline/stop monitoring independent of awaited tool calls. Late broker replies cannot write after cancellation; old-cell cleanup cannot destroy a replacement kernel. Native macOS and Linux real-Docker containment are now verified. The host CLI and local Unix endpoint are frozen; private CLI configuration prevents operator proxy credentials reaching the worker, including after context changes.
reviews.remaining: Generic SSH, Modal and remote TLS provisioning remain unsupported and require an explicitly isolated governed transport design. Docker selection currently supports local Unix endpoints. Correlation tokens/nonces reject stale frames but cannot attest output against Python introspection inside the same worker; authorization is enforced by the host broker. Spills cover redirected Python stdout/stderr up to 5,000,000 bytes per stream; deliberate native-fd bypasses and the part of a runaway stream past that ceiling are not kept on disk. Production deployment evidence is separate from these real-container tests.

reviews.summary: Oversized output is paged back from its spill file instead of being re-run. execute_code stdout/stderr are spooled to disk as they arrive (agents/core/code_tools.py:480, agents/core/tool_result_store.py:431) under <data root>/workspace/tool_results. Each stream is capped at DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES = 5,000,000 (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:130): StreamSpill.write stops writing at the cap but keeps counting (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:600), close appends one '[... spill capped at N bytes: M more bytes ...]' marker (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:642), and the result carries <stream>_spill_capped and <stream>_kept_bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:274-275). Head and tail stay inline with omitted-byte accounting (agents/core/environments/output_limits.py:42, tests/test_environment_output_limits.py:38). A whole result the loop spills (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1367) keeps both ends in its preview (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:705-706, tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:139), and file_read itself is never spilled (tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:287). Every notice carries the exact call from page_recipe (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145): file_read(path="<resolved path>", offset=0, max_bytes=N). The same arguments are returned as <stream>_read_with (agents/core/code_tools.py:272) and read_with (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:736), and stream recipes propose pages of at most 8,000 bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:226). file_read takes an integer offset from 0 to MAX_OFFSET = 2**53-1 (agents/core/file_tools.py:122, agents/core/file_tools.py:1476). Anything else is refused as bad_offset, both in the preflight and in a direct call (agents/core/file_tools.py:1395, agents/core/file_tools.py:728). An offset at or past the end is an empty final page, answered without seeking (agents/core/file_tools.py:746). A page that stops early returns next_offset (agents/core/file_tools.py:1250) and never ends inside a UTF-8 character (agents/core/file_tools.py:1202). A .pdf/.docx pages through its extracted text (agents/core/file_tools.py:1254). The named call is one file_read answers in every live setup, including the three the review found broken. The recipe path is resolved (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:207). A spill is never named like a secret (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:190). file_read alone gets a read-only door for exact spill-file names in the coordinator's spill directory (agents/core/file_tools.py:636, agents/core/file_tools.py:673, agents/core/file_tools.py:1167), wired at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:796. So JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS pointing elsewhere, a symlinked JARVIS_HOME or a bridged tool with a secret-looking name no longer strands the file (tests/test_spill_paging.py:507, tests/test_spill_paging.py:535); the door's limits are pinned by tests/test_spill_paging.py:414. The recipe is named only where that call is answered. ToolResultStore.readable(path) (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:361) asks the coordinator probe (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:800). The probe requires four things: file_read registered, allowed by the job toolset, in this turn's profile offer (noted at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:918), and able to open this very path (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:812, agents/core/file_tools.py:701). execute_code also requires file_read in its own run's offer (agents/core/code_tools.py:462, agents/core/code_tools.py:559). Otherwise the notice says the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from this turn (tests/test_spill_paging.py:545, tests/test_spill_paging.py:589, tests/test_code_tools.py:866), and concurrent turns each see their own offer (tests/test_spill_paging.py:627). A failed spill just omits the path (agents/core/code_tools.py:258-259, tests/test_code_tools.py:698). Retention is unchanged (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:490, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:214, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:353). End to end, a real AgentToolRuntime follows read_with and then next_offset through the real file_read and rebuilds the spilled result byte for byte, while the producing tool runs once (tests/test_spill_paging.py:719). execute_code stdout does the same on the one-shot and session paths (tests/test_code_tools.py:824), and a runaway stream stops at its ceiling with one marker (tests/test_code_tools.py:877, tests/test_spill_paging.py:233). Adaptations: offsets are bytes, not Hermes' lines. The 5,000,000-byte cap covers streamed spills, which is Hermes' execute_code scope; whole-result JSON spills stay bounded by the 256 MB retention sweep. A spill stays third-party when it comes back: every file directly in a spill directory counts as one (agents/core/file_tools.py:687), a file_read page of it and a file_search whose matches reach it declare tainted (agents/core/file_tools.py:753, agents/core/file_tools.py:905), and the loop fences the result as DATA and raises the turn's recall taint, in the turn that spilled it or any later one (tests/test_spill_paging.py:761, tests/test_spill_paging.py:812, tests/test_spill_paging.py:834, tests/test_spill_paging.py:856). A trusted tool's spill counts too, because a spill's file name cannot say reliably which tool wrote it.

Built in #1207. Hermes nests the agent's subtasks with one optional parent on each todo item (the id of another item) instead of a nested array, so merge-by-id keeps working, and draws the list through one defensive tree builder. Nerva now does both, for the todo tool's items and for mission plan steps.

The tree builder:
- agents/core/todo_tree.py tree() (agents/core/todo_tree.py:40) returns (item, depth) pairs in depth-first order, children in list order under their parent, with every item exactly once. It is stdlib only, because the CLI imports it.
- Depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH = 4 (agents/core/todo_tree.py:28); a deeper item is drawn at depth 4, under its parent.
- An item whose parent is missing, itself, or not an id at all is drawn at depth 0 in its place (agents/core/todo_tree.py:56). ref() accepts only text or whole numbers as ids; a bool, a float, a list or a dict is no id (agents/core/todo_tree.py:31). When two items share an id, the first holds it.
- Cycle members, and anything under them, are reached from no root, so they are appended flat at depth 0 in list order (agents/core/todo_tree.py:69). A getter that raises counts as no parent. The walk uses an explicit stack, so a 5,000-item chain costs no recursion.
- The HUD's twin is frontend/src/todo-tree.ts todoTree() (frontend/src/todo-tree.ts:28), with the same rules. frontend/src/test/todo-tree.test.ts pins it to the same shapes as tests/test_h666_subtasks.py.

The todo tool:
- An item may carry parent: the id of the item it sits under. It is an allowed item field (agents/core/todo_tool.py:84) and is in the schema as a string of at most MAX_ID (agents/core/todo_tool.py:102); the description tells the model how to nest and un-nest.
- _clean_parent (agents/core/todo_tool.py:197) cleans it like an id. An empty string means no parent. Anything else that is not an id is refused as todo_bad_parent, with a sentence the model can act on, and changes nothing.
- A parent need not name an item in the list: a dangling, self or cyclic parent is stored and drawn at the top, never refused and never lost.
- On a merge, parent null means not sent (as for content and status), and "" clears it. A changed parent counts as a write, so the plan cap applies. A parent moved by an untrusted turn taints the item, as a status does. Re-sending the same parent changes nothing: no taint, and the plan's labels stay (agents/core/todo_tool.py:383).
- model_items answers the parent only when it is set (agents/core/todo_tool.py:226), so a flat list answers exactly as before and plan_bytes counts a parent's bytes.

Mission plan steps:
- MissionStore.create (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:203) gives every step a nullable parent. _plan_step (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:390) reads each entry.
  - A title, or any other value, is a top-level step with its own text, as before; a mapping without title or parent is still stringified.
  - {title, parent?} may sit under an earlier step: parent is that step's index, and only an earlier one. A plan is therefore a forest by construction.
  - Anything else is refused as bad_plan_step: a self, later, out-of-range, negative, bool, text or float parent, a missing or blank title, or an unknown key.
- POST /api/missions (agents/core/routers/missions.py:50) accepts such a plan. A bad step answers 400 with one fixed sentence and code bad_plan_step (agents/core/routers/missions.py:73); no request data reaches the body.
- The build-queue plan kept out-of-range and self parents on mission steps and let the tree degrade them. The store refuses them instead: a mission plan is written once, by its creator, so a bad parent there is a caller's mistake worth a 400. The tree still degrades any step the store did not check, such as a row written before this change, which has no parent key.
- finish_step budget charging and the completion gates are unchanged. A child step is charged like any step, closing a child does not close its parent, and exhausting the budget still auto-fails the mission.

Rendering:
- nerva todo draws the tree through todo_tree, indented two spaces a level (agents/cli/nerva.py:1200).
- The Decision Inbox's plans in flight (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx) orders items through todoTree and indents each row 14 px a level, with data-depth (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:78). ITEMS_SHOWN counts rows in tree order.
- MissionCanvasPanel draws plan steps through todoTree, keyed by each step's idx (frontend/src/panels/mission-canvas.tsx:248). The finish controls still name the step's own idx, not its drawn position.

Tests:
- tests/test_h666_subtasks.py (37 cases):
  - the tree: DFS order, a child listed before its parent, the depth cap, dangling, self and cyclic parents, non-id parents, duplicate ids, a getter that raises, and a long chain;
  - todo parents: storage, merge, clearing, cleaning, refusal, the cap, labels, taint, the schema and the tool answer;
  - mission step parents in the store and through POST /api/missions, with the refusal cases, budget charging on a child step, and nerva todo indentation.
- Vitest: frontend/src/test/todo-tree.test.ts (8), plus one case each in the plans-in-flight and mission-canvas suites (indentation, and dangling or cyclic parents kept in view).
- 43 mutants of the new guards were all killed (four survivors of the first run were killed by added cases). One unreachable guard, a placed-twice check in the walk, was removed.

The execution sandbox still puts its work directory on the system temp root. Sandbox.__init__ falls back to tempfile.mkdtemp() (agents/core/sandbox.py:60), and the only production construction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:528-531) passes no work_dir. Script files for the WASM, subprocess and docker paths are written there. A scratch probe of Sandbox() resolved to /tmp/tmpXXXX under tempfile.gettempdir(). TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP pass through to child processes (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:24-26). paths.data_path (agents/core/paths.py:149) provides a real data root, but no exec cache is resolved under it. run_retention (agents/core/retention.py:148) purges conversations, audit and private ingestion only. Nothing ages or deletes the mkdtemp directories, there is no per-group prune, and nothing separates a managed directory from an owner-pointed one. The rationale made collision-safe task-id directory naming conditional on persistent per-task sandboxes. Those do not exist, so that part is not required.
reviews.remaining: (1) Resolve the sandbox temp root off tmpfs. An explicit owner setting or env var (e.g. security.sandbox_temp_dir / JARVIS_EXEC_TEMP_DIR) is checked first; otherwise use a managed data_path('cache','exec') directory. Sandbox.__init__ (agents/core/sandbox.py:60) must mkdtemp inside that root, and the orchestrator construction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:528-531) must use it. (2) Add a periodic prune (default max age 72h) wired to the scheduler or run_retention (agents/core/retention.py:148). It ages each sandbox directory as one group, so the newest file protects the whole group, and it never deletes the live Sandbox.work_dir. It runs only when the root is the managed directory; an owner-pointed directory is never bulk-deleted. (3) Tests for the resolution order, group-aware aging and the owner-pointed exclusion.

reviews.summary: The mechanism the rationale credits is present. Each agent's SOUL body is the system prompt (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2092). It is read, injection-scanned and capped by the one builder Agent._read_soul (agents/core/agent.py:432), which both Agent._load_soul (agents/core/agent.py:501) at construction and, since H672, Agent.refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:513) at a context-compaction commit use. So an edited SOUL reaches a running hub without a restart. SoulVersionStore in agents/core/soul_versioning.py provides immutable versions, diff and rollback. A persona layer is added to every turn (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2923 via Persona.prompt_block, agents/core/cognition/persona.py:142-150), and it already says 'do not flatter or over-agree'. Some behaviour rules exist, but per agent only: agents/jarvis/SOUL.md:90 forbids restating the owner's question and agents/jarvis/SOUL.md:97 requires 'Short. Then shorter.'. The quarantine fallback (agents/core/agent.py:75-80) carries four forbidden patterns: no AI disclaimers, flattery, hedging or preambles. What the rationale accepted is missing: there is no shared identity band. No single file's content reaches every agent's system prompt. The shipped SOULs and agents/_templates/SOUL.template.md still describe character and register. None of the following exists anywhere: a reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), an earned-depth rule, an 'agree because it is right, not because the owner said it' line, prohibitions on filler, re-summarizing or narrating visible tool calls as shared rules, or a maintainer note never to tell the model to explore efficiently.
reviews.remaining: Write one shared behaviour-contract file, for example agents/_system/IDENTITY.md. Mirror it in, or reference it from, a repo-root SOUL.md so agents working on the repo read the same text. It must contain: the reply-sizing rule; the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls); the anti-sycophancy line; the earned-depth rule; and a maintainer comment never to re-add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration'. Load it through the same H387 scan and cap builder as Agent._read_soul, including the compaction-boundary re-read that refresh_soul does. Prepend it to every agent's system prompt, at the points where agents/core/orchestrator.py:2092 and Agent.generate_response read soul content. Allow a per-install override in the user souls directory. Version it in SoulVersionStore so it can be diffed, rolled back and A/B-tested. Persona SOULs and Persona.prompt_block stay the character layer on top. Add tests that every active agent's system prompt carries the contract, that the override takes precedence, and that the banned exploration line is absent.

reviews.summary: Durable session birth is resolved through an immutable, generation-checked continuation root. Explicit owner-created child sessions carry bounded retained context and root birth through multiple generations, text/stream/process entrypoints and restart without switching the shared default. SQLite atomically commits child identity, seed, lineage and initial clock; idempotent request receipts resolve retries. Corrupt newer snapshots, reused identities and failed recovery stop dispatch or writes instead of silently replacing context. Accepted history/tool compaction alone advances the durable rebuild clock through compare-and-swap; request snapshots preserve same-day prefix bytes, reject late inherited commits, and add the trusted current-date line only when rebuild and root-birth days differ. Production rendering resolves explicit TZ or existing local IANA discovery and uses historical/current DST rules with an explicit UTC offset. Unknown birth is omitted; invalid or unavailable zone discovery preserves truthful offset-only rendering rather than inventing an IANA name. Independent actual-route, Agent, restart, concurrency, cancellation, failed-resume and observe-only regressions support the full frozen clock contract. This is code-equivalence, not a live-provider claim; ordinary subsequent JSON persistence remains best effort and turn leases are process-local. H672 hangs the persona re-read on the same commit: `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` calls `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` after the clock CAS and only when the compressor reported a compression, so a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing and an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order (`test_a_refused_clock_commit_migrates_nothing`, `test_an_accepted_clock_commit_is_followed_by_the_refresh_in_that_order`); the re-read neither reads nor writes the clock, so the same-day prefix bytes and the current-date line are untouched by it. #1188's edit to `orchestrator.py` is the pairing store's registry path, nothing on this row.

Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. A `tool_offer_refreshed` event (added/removed/reason) is written only when something moved. 17 mechanism tests (`tests/test_session_refresh.py`, red-proofed by mutation in the parked commit) plus 26 wiring tests (`tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). An independent review of the first cut found 14 items (4 major, 6 minor, 4 nits: the per-turn, process-wide re-read cost; the H387 verdict suppressed at the boundary; the overclaim that `ToolRPC.handle` refuses profile revocations; the unpinned gate map and CAS order; the front-matter blind spot; the traceback for a persona-less agent; the docstrings); 13 are addressed here and each code fix was neutered once and shown red (8 mutations, 11 distinct tests red).
reviews.remaining: **The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. **Profile revocations are not enforced on the execution path**: `ToolRPCServer.handle` checks the job toolset, registration and the gate, never the tool profile, and the executor's gate map is rebuilt only at a fold — so in a loop that never folds (small results, the common shape) a tool the profile withdrew mid-turn stays offered *and* executes until the loop ends; pre-existing, unchanged by this slice, pinned as a limit by `test_between_folds_a_profile_revocation_is_not_enforced_by_the_executor_either`. **The persona migration is process-wide**: `orchestrator.agents` is every agent and `agent.soul` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at `_history_for_prompt`, which it does not have. **On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit** (`_shared_route_plan` → `build()` measures `agent.soul` while planning; the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at `agents/core/file_tools.py` saying `_load_soul` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite `agent.py`, `agent_runtime.py` or `orchestrator.py` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in `orchestrator.py`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in `telegram.py` and `web.py`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through `_profiled`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. Three are rewritten — H387: the ERROR line now comes from `_announce_soul_verdict` behind the `_read_soul` builder, for boot and boundary alike; H671 and H673: `publish()` re-reads the personas after the clock CAS, and the staged-route budget limit above is now on H673's own row. The 16 other needs_review rows on main (H060, H061, H068, H071, H104, H108, H130, H135, H139, H398, H477, H510, H523, H683 from #1188's edits to `orchestrator.py`, `web.py` and `telegram.py`; H288 and H684 from #1187's `heartbeat.py` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) are main's own drift, not this branch's, and are left untouched here; #1187's five-line comment in `orchestrator.py` re-drifted the nine rows above once more, and they were re-read against it and re-stamped.

reviews.summary: Configured Ollama num_ctx is sent on generate/tool/stream; /api/show model parameters can resolve a cached effective ceiling, ignoring architectural model_info maxima. Shared-history compression clamps to that ceiling, hard threshold cannot exceed 85%, and a Gemini compaction model reserves its concrete cloud output cap including auto=8192. Review repair: effective soft/hard thresholds are normalized together and actual compression target stays below the effective hard trigger, including soft=hard=1 configurations; protected head/tail remains intact. Ollama and LM Studio structured tool turns now retain the provider-reported input/output token counts. Strict count normalization preserves valid answers when usage metadata is absent or malformed. Tool-loop usage accumulates for metering while context anchors replace with the latest request count; unavailable input does not erase a prior anchor. Gemini structured turns now retain inclusive prompt counts and disjoint candidate/thought output counts; explicitly OpenAI-compatible profiles retain standard prompt/completion totals without adding nested breakdowns. Complete context anchors now include Anthropic disjoint input/cache-read/cache-write counts, including cache-only requests, while totals-only mappings count the full prompt once. Billing semantics remain unchanged. Complete non-stream text replies now publish provider usage through closed request-local observers. Non-stream agent gathers retain per-agent measurements and complete-prefix anchors; ToolRuntime remains the single structured-turn reporter. Retries publish only accepted response usage; cancellation and inherited late tasks cannot outlive the observer. Public string/stream signatures and guardrails are unchanged. OpenRouter inherited streaming reports its single complete text request once. Ollama, LM Studio and Anthropic actual streams now publish one measurement only after confirmed completion: literal done=true, usage-only snapshot plus [DONE], or valid start/final cumulative message_delta usage plus message_stop respectively. Errors, interruption, malformed frames/containers and missing final usage do not reuse intermediate counts. Retry state resets, disjoint cache categories and text callbacks remain intact. Gemini streams now retain a terminal response's own validated prompt/candidate/thought counts after clean HTTP exhaustion and response close. Known single-candidate completion or explicit blocked-prompt semantics are required; errors, raw trailers, cancellation, conflicting response identities and nonzero/malformed candidate indices invalidate the whole attempt. Retries remain isolated and answer callbacks are unchanged. Pinned ask jobs now resolve and freeze their model/window before history construction, cap completion, and omit an unrelated prior usage anchor; unchanged default models retain their existing estimate. Ordinary tool turns now also use immutable configured/cached backend capacity forwarded before guardrails; known limits include completion, initial/later transcript, schemas and structured tool-call arguments. Unknown capacity remains estimated rather than discovered. Reasoning integration was reviewed against previously-current grid33165622 evidence: request-shaping refusals/empty controls do not change this row's cache, session or context/usage semantics. Existing focused regressions are retained. Responses completed text/tool turns and validated terminal streams now retain reported input/output usage. Inclusive input totals split cached_tokens once into disjoint uncached input and cache_read; output reasoning detail is not added to output totals. Missing/malformed metadata does not invent counts. Stream errors, incomplete/contradictory terminal items, cancellation or failed close do not publish usage; request-local sinks preserve existing single-publication semantics. The xAI Responses dialect inherits the same strict reported input/output/cache split and complete terminal accounting, while its own completed-response acceptance rechecks reasoning/replay lifetimes. Reasoning token detail is not added twice to output totals. Opaque function replay preserves main-loop provider usage without introducing ciphertext persistence, per-vendor prices or cache discount assumptions. Shared history compression now preplans each actual governed specialist route and its finite or dynamic completion reserve instead of borrowing the router default model. The strictest input budget stages one shared summary; final prompts/routes are revalidated through at most three monotonically tightening passes before a single accepted clock/history publication. Prepared text/SSE dispatch preserves backend/model/session/lifetime identity, policy gates and known-versus-estimated context metadata. Selected Ollama resolves its own context. Usage anchors require matching backend/model, session generation and retained-history digest; unmanaged old anchors are not promoted to exact managed measurements. Existing disabled-compression behavior and direct local auto output remain unchanged. Since H672 the accepted clock/history publication is followed by the persona re-read (`_refresh_souls_at_boundary`, after the CAS): it changes nothing in how pressure is measured or anchored, but on the staged shared-route path `_shared_route_plan` measured `agent.soul` while planning and the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`, so a persona that grew at that boundary is sent that turn with a budget planned for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, and the next response's usage anchor measures the real prompt. #1188's edit to `orchestrator.py` is the pairing store's registry path, nothing on this row.
reviews.remaining: A model with no num_ctx parameter and no operator configuration remains unresolved (server environment/running context is not probed). Fixed image estimates remain incomplete. Gemini usage-only final frames, absent terminal-local counts, unknown terminal semantics and ambiguous multi-candidate streams deliberately remain unreported. Synthesis/compression/background model calls are deliberately outside conversational usage attribution. Cache discounts/write premiums and undocumented vendor-specific usage mappings are not modeled by the new totals-only adapters. No live provider or billing proof. Responses accounting is limited to supported API-key GPT-4.1 and exact xAI Grok4.5/4.6 dialects, not Codex subscription usage or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Cache counts do not establish live discounts, prices or physical context occupancy. Actual specialist planning applies to the existing opt-in shared-compression path; disabled/unmanaged callers retain their existing behavior. Unknown capacity remains a conservative planning estimate, not verified provider metadata.

reviews.summary: The failure semantics and derived thresholds are in place. ContextCompressor.compress falls back to _fallback_digest over the whole older window when the summarizer raises or returns nothing (agents/core/context_compressor.py:541-548). CompactionPolicy derives soft/hard triggers from each model's window (0.6/0.85 at agents/core/context_compressor.py:210-211). _history_for_prompt clamps the window to the Ollama-reported ceiling or the pinned job selection. The summary output budget is a setting (memory.compression_summary_max_tokens, agents/core/settings_db.py:229). The timing discipline the rationale accepted is missing. Compaction runs inline in the arriving turn: _history_for_prompt awaits compressor.compact with no bound (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3450). The strict-local summarizer built by _compression_summarizer (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3242) awaits a non-streaming backend.generate (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3266-3269). Its only limit is the httpx read timeout from local_read_timeout (agents/core/llm/base.py:59; 120s for Ollama at agents/core/llm/base.py:699), which for a non-streaming call is a total-duration wait, not an inactivity deadline. A scratch probe with a summarizer that never returns kept ContextCompressor.compress pending past an external 3s wait_for. Nothing separates how long the summary may run from how long it may delay the user, and no notice is shown.
reviews.remaining: (1) Bounded hold: an arriving turn waits at most a configurable memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds (default about 10s) for an LLM summary. On expiry it proceeds with the deterministic digest, or verbatim turns when within the window, and shows a visible notice that the summary was deferred. The summary then finishes in the background and seeds _ctx_summary_cache for the next turn, without publishing through the compaction-clock CAS for the turn that did not use it. (2) Inactivity deadline: the summarizer streams and falls back to the digest after N seconds with no tokens (default 60) instead of holding the full read budget; a slow-but-alive stream is not killed. (3) Tests: a hanging summarizer returns within the hold; a trickling summarizer survives; a silent one is cut at the inactivity deadline.

reviews.summary: Joburile au refuz/raportare explicită și livrare prin aprobări existente.
reviews.remaining: Politica configurabilă queue/deny pentru toate originile fără operator nu este echivalată prin simpla livrare a joburilor.

reviews.summary: Boot posture is gated. The lifespan runs enforce_boot_posture (agents/web.py:421, agents/core/boot_guards.py:324) and awaits orch.load_agents (agents/web.py:456), which covers backend detection, SOUL loading and plugin build, before the app serves. The local-model warm-up is not a gate: load_agents starts LLMRouter.warm_up (agents/core/llm/router.py:231) as a fire-and-forget task (agents/core/orchestrator.py:843-845). A message that arrives right after boot therefore races the cold model load, with no bounded wait, no warming state and no mark on the reply that it was served during warm-up. Shutdown has one explicit budget: serve.py:83 sets uvicorn timeout_graceful_shutdown from JARVIS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT (default 10s, pinned in tests/test_h2311_operability.py). The lifespan teardown steps have no budget. ChannelManager.stop_all awaits each ch.stop() in turn (agents/core/channels/manager.py:120-122). _cancel_task awaits the cancelled task with no timeout (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1302-1304). Plugin close_all and aclose follow, also unbounded. Channel turns take the session lease (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1505) with a 180s maximum wait (agents/core/orchestrator.py:242). The Telegram poll loop handles updates one at a time (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:403, awaiting receive at agents/core/channels/telegram.py:477), so one lease waiter delays unrelated chats for up to 180s.
reviews.remaining: (1) Bounded warm-up gate: in the lifespan, before orch.start_channels(), await the warm-up task with asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...)) under a startup_warmup_timeout setting (default 20s). On timeout, log, open anyway and let warm-up finish in the background. Expose a warming state on the status/health surface and mark turns served before warm-up completed. (2) Explicit short budgets on every teardown wait: per-channel stop, cancelled-task awaits (interrupt grace of about 1-2s), plugin close_all and aclose steps. Log each overrun so a wedged step cannot use up the service-manager stop budget. (3) A short turn-lease wait for sequentially dispatched channels such as Telegram, or per-chat concurrent dispatch. (4) Tests: warm-up completes before serving; a hung warm-up does not block past its budget; a hung channel stop does not hold teardown.

reviews.summary: Dialectele de unelte cloud, compactarea în tură și recuperarea răspunsului gol au implementări și regresii.
reviews.remaining: Rândurile includ mai multe fire de streaming/cache/compactare/recuperare; completarea și probele fiecărei căi rămân explicite.

reviews.summary: Cached per-model tri-state hooks now preserve undeclared defaults, suppress all reasoning controls for explicit empty declarations, and canonically clamp nonempty vocabularies to the nearest weaker level. Below-minimum requests refuse before HTTP rather than escalating or restoring defaults. Immutable backend-owned Gemini/compatible declarations retain cold/reconnect/concurrent isolation; actual Anthropic text/stream/tool requests enforce empty declarations, including registry precedence and default-on families. Budget-only models expose existing product rungs while emitting only their budget schema, never an invented effort field. Independent 162-case guarded review and original mocked-wire counterexamples pass. Operator declarations must match actual provider capabilities; no live acceptance/billing or catalog-discovery proof is claimed. New Nebius/local wire support is not required by this frozen contract.

SubAgentManager (agents/core/subagents.py) provides capped, isolated, steerable spawns, and a schema-invalid child is recorded as failed (agents/core/subagents.py:408-414). The production runner _subagent_runner (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1450-1453) calls orch.process(task, agent=picked, channel='subagent') with no model, provider or request override. SubAgentManager.spawn accepts only task, agent, parent and output_schema, and SubAgentSpawnBody (agents/core/routers/mesh.py:191-195) accepts no model fields. A reusable model/provider pin exists for owner jobs (selection_scope, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:54, used at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1472) but is not wired to delegation. Provider failure is not reported honestly. Orchestrator.process returns '' on any backend failure or error/timeout marker (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1662-1667). The runner wraps that as {'output': ''}, and the manager records the child as done with ok=True; a scratch probe returned status 'done'. There is no batch spawn surface, and nothing collapses a batch of identical failures into one 'configured subagent model rejected' notice.
reviews.remaining: (1) Per-child API settings: accept model/provider, plus bounded request overrides such as max_tokens/temperature/extra_body deep-merged one level, on SubAgentManager.spawn, on the /api/subagents/spawn body and through a default autonomy.subagent_model setting. Apply them in _subagent_runner through selection_scope with documented precedence: explicit, then setting, then parent. (2) Failure honesty: a child whose provider call failed (empty output, degraded reply or error marker) is recorded as failed with the error class, not done. (3) Batch report: a batch spawn surface whose result emits one notice when every child failed with a model-not-found phrase AND the configured subagent model name. The notice names the model, the setting that controls it and whether a fallback exists. A failure naming a model that is not the configured one must not trigger it. (4) Tests for all three.

reviews.summary: Registrul de comenzi, tierele și catalogul HUD există.
reviews.remaining: Rândul include mai multe comenzi, meniuri și extensii de comenzi decât registrul livrat; echivalarea completă rămâne deschisă.

reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:54) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:347) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:50, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:127) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:170) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:363). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1512), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1392): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:1520) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with on_token=draft.push (orchestrator.py:1509) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1437) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:1517) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1446-1447); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Tests: 82 passed, 1 skipped (tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py needs slack_sdk, absent on this box) across tests/test_telegram_streaming.py, tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py and tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py. #1188's change to telegram.py (the process's shared SenderPairing handed in at construction, deeplink pairing refused when none is wired) does not touch the draft, edit or send paths.
reviews.remaining: (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation (no delete_message or deleteMessage anywhere in agents/), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:102, agents/core/channels/discord.py:32) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:329), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:613) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees).

reviews.summary: Read-only jobs doctor reports scheduler stop/pause, missing registrations, missing/invalid/overdue next runs, execution failures and delivery failures. CLI failures exit non-zero. Bounded native scheduler outcomes and owner delivery results survive restart; intentional skips do not erase failures. Real APScheduler and migration tests pass; the two diagnostic modules have 97% branch-inclusive coverage. Doctor also checks script paths and no_agent configuration without reading source; persisted jobs remain inspectable when a script disappears. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported.
reviews.remaining: Model workdir and wider per-job tool context remain unsupported. Production-host observation, complete runtime-availability diagnostics and the wider job-option contract remain open; this is not full Hermes cron-doctor equivalence.

reviews.summary: The per-turn data exists on the server. TokenUsage carries provider cache_read/cache_write (agents/core/llm/tool_protocol.py:70-72). The stream path sums provider usage per agent (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2248). The post-turn record writes input, output and cached tokens, a per-turn cache_hit boolean and usage_source into the learning ledger (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3911-3914). Aggregate readouts exist: /api/metrics/north-star (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:166) with %-local and p95 turn latency, shown as a HUD stat card (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:214), and the bench computes a chars/sec throughput (agents/core/bench.py:79). None of it reaches the chat surface live. The /chat/stream end event carries only agent, text and pending_approvals (agents/web.py:1237), and ChatResponse (agents/web.py:1000) has reply and pending_approvals only. No HUD component shows tokens/sec, latency, context % or cache hit for the current turn. There is no field-selection setting. Cache hit is not computed as a delta since the last invalidating event: the stored cache_hit is a per-turn boolean that does not reset on model switch or compaction. Nothing hides the readout when there are no cache reads.
reviews.remaining: (1) Compute a per-turn readout: wall latency; output tokens/sec over generation time; context % of the resolved model window; compressions count; and cache hit as a delta since the last cache-invalidating event (model switch or accepted compaction), omitted when there were zero cache reads. Attach it to the /chat/stream end event and the /chat response, leaving fields absent when there is no data. (2) Add a display.status_bar_fields setting with a fixed field vocabulary shared by backend and HUD. (3) Add a HUD status strip on the chat surface that renders only the selected fields, hides omitted ones and colours cache hit at the 70/40 thresholds. (4) Backend and frontend tests.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no durable install identity. The only install-level id is analytics: first_action.mark_installed (agents/core/first_action.py:108) mints uuid4().hex[:16] (agents/core/first_action.py:126) into the activation-clock record. When that record is unreadable or has another schema, _read (agents/core/first_action.py:91) returns None and mark_installed mints a fresh id (agents/core/first_action.py:120). There is no lock, no fsync, no read-back verification, and nothing compares the id. The surfaces that name a machine each use their own ids: node_mesh.register_node takes a caller-supplied node_id (agents/core/node_mesh.py:97), SatelliteHub.register takes a caller-supplied satellite_id (agents/core/satellite_hub.py:211), and channel pairing mints a random per-link id (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:254). There is no per-profile isolation either. JARVIS_PROFILE is only forwarded to child processes (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:49) and is never read. paths.data_root (agents/core/paths.py:138) is chosen only by JARVIS_HOME/JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR. There is no hub PID or lock file, and credentials are not scoped by profile. tests/test_first_run_first_action.py covers only the activation clock.
reviews.remaining:
1. A stable install id. Store one 32-hex opaque id under the data root, minted once under a cross-process lock (flock / msvcrt plus an in-process lock) and written atomically (mkstemp, fsync, os.replace, directory fsync), then verified by re-reading. When the id cannot be read or persisted, return None, never a fresh or ephemeral value.
2. Consumers. node_mesh registrations and grant scope, satellite pairings and channel pairings (agents/core/channels/pairing.py) use this id instead of per-registration ids, and first_action.mark_installed stops re-minting on an unreadable record.
3. Runtime isolation per profile or data root. Add a hub PID/lock file so a second hub on the same root is refused, and credentials resolved only from that root. JARVIS_PROFILE is either given a real meaning or removed.

reviews.summary:
JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES is the only allowlist that decides whose forwarding headers count: X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-Proto alike.

Parsing and refusals: parse_trusted_proxies (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:134) reads each entry with ip_network(strict=False) (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:160), so a bare address becomes its own /32 or /128. It refuses '*', 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 by name (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107), any prefix length 0 (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:165), unreadable entries and more than 64 entries, naming the variable and the position, never the value. A malformed list refuses boot through assert_parseable_trusted_proxies (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:411), whose message tells the operator to list the proxy's own address or a bounded CIDR range with no wildcard; it runs in enforce_boot_posture (agents/core/boot_guards.py:350), which the lifespan calls after the .env files load (agents/web.py:414-421, H273), and assert_front_door runs it over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:318). That is stricter than Hermes, which drops a bad entry and carries on. At request time a malformed list fails closed and is said once (agents/web.py:129). The default trusts nothing, not even loopback; the legacy JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXY flag means loopback only (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:206).

One trust set: uvicorn's own proxy-header layer used to rewrite the client address and scheme from loopback, or from whatever FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS named, before the app looked. serve.server_config now builds uvicorn with proxy_headers=False (serve.py:84) and records that choice (serve.py:86). docker-compose.yml passes --no-proxy-headers (docker-compose.yml:13); the Dockerfile, the systemd unit, start.sh, START.bat and the packaged build already start through serve.py. The app reads X-Forwarded-Proto itself, only from a listed peer and only when there is exactly one http/https/ws/wss value (forwarded_proto, agents/core/proxy_trust.py:389, applied by _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, agents/web.py:163, registered at agents/web.py:594), so a TLS proxy still yields https:// base URLs for the MCP resource and the widget snippet. The scheme is set on the scope in place, as uvicorn's layer did, so the route the router records reaches the golden-signals middleware and a forwarded request keeps its per-route metrics label (agents/web.py:194, tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:582). assert_server_proxy_layer_within_trust (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570) runs in the same boot pass (agents/core/boot_guards.py:353) and in assert_front_door (agents/core/boot_guards.py:319). It refuses FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, or --forwarded-allow-ips on a uvicorn command line when an entry is '*', a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES plus uvicorn's loopback default.

Gates: the localhost auth bypass (_real_client_host, agents/web.py:139) and the HF-2 rate-limit key (_client_ip, agents/web.py:317) resolve the client through forwarded_client, which trusts only a listed peer and walks the chain right to left. The HF-2 localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:694), so an unlisted same-box proxy, or a listed one whose chain vouches for nothing, is not waved through.

Logging: web.py's import-time read is silent (agents/web.py:121). The lifespan calls announce_trusted_proxies after setup_logging and the .env load (agents/web.py:462). When anything is trusted it logs one INFO line naming the source and the canonical networks (_log_trust_set, agents/core/proxy_trust.py:253), together with the wide-entry and legacy warnings that belong with it, which are repeated when the set was resolved before logging existed (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:294). Nothing is logged for the default. It also names uvicorn's layer whenever that layer believes anyone (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:528): on a raw uvicorn start without --no-proxy-headers, or under a launcher it cannot identify.

Tests: tests/test_trusted_proxies.py covers parsing and refusal (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:58, tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:74), the LAN-peer loopback spoof (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:183), the INFO line (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:295), the lifespan wiring run through the real lifespan (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:434), the silent import (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:416), and the served config with uvicorn's ProxyHeadersMiddleware in front, where a LAN peer sends X-Forwarded-For 127.0.0.1 under FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*' (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:506). It also covers the throttle exemption (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:534), X-Forwarded-Proto believed only from a listed peer (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:562), and the uvicorn-allowlist refusals (tests/test_trusted_proxies.py:624). tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py pins the new guard in the boot pass and in the mapping check (tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:148, tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:200), and that the lifespan loads the .env files before the boot pass (tests/test_o26_f6_boot_guards.py:218). tests/test_rate_limit_hf2.py and tests/test_admin_guard_hf7.py cover the two gates. Operator documentation is in docs/FLAGS.md.

Known limits, which the row does not require: a raw python -m uvicorn agents.web:app without --no-proxy-headers (the CI openapi, soak and smoke jobs, and dev use) still lets uvicorn believe loopback's forwarding headers, which is Hermes's own default. On that raw start uvicorn's loopback walk can also rewrite a loopback peer into a listed proxy's address, after which Nerva's walk trusts the rest of the chain; using it needs the raw start, a list naming a non-loopback proxy and a same-box unlisted proxy that passes the client's X-Forwarded-For through verbatim. The guard caps that layer at the Nerva list plus loopback, and the boot names it at INFO. A launcher that embeds uvicorn some other way passes its allowlist out of the app's sight. The RFC 7239 Forwarded header is not parsed. Behaviour change: a same-box proxy that is not listed no longer gets per-client throttle keys or https:// base URLs through uvicorn's implicit loopback trust until it is listed (127.0.0.1/32).

Nerva already has the shape of a small bundle plus a large on-demand catalog. 12 first-party skills ship under skills/ (for example skills/brief/SKILL.md). They are rendered into the 'Available skills' prompt block (agents/core/agent.py:615), which skills_index_component measures (agents/core/prompt_size.py:136). Hermes skills are not bundled; they are imported one at a time on request. POST /skills/import (agents/core/routers/skills.py:322) is user-guarded and DEV_MODE-gated, and frontend/src/panels/skills-import.tsx drives it. It calls SkillImporter.import_from_hermes (agents/core/skills/importer.py:204). That import checks an exact, digest-verified pin allowlist and fails before any network call (tests/test_hermes_import.py). The pin still predates the upstream reorganisation. agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4 and agents/core/skills/importer.py:50 are v2026.8.27 with 78 entries (tests/test_hermes_import.py:232). So the catalog still lists github-auth, github-code-review, github-issue-to-pr, github-issues, github-pr-workflow, github-repo-management, plan, session-librarian and blogwatcher. It has neither the consolidated github skill nor grill-me or the other new optional skills. _safe_pin_path requires every pinned path to start with skills/ (agents/core/skills/importer.py:113), so upstream's optional-skills/ tree cannot be pinned at all. Each pin entry digests only one SKILL.md, so reference files cannot be imported.
